56033.q: What is special about the old town of Trogir in Croatia?
a: It lies on a small island
It lies on a high mountain
It lies in a large cave
It lies in the middle of a lake
56033.e: The old town of Trogir lies on a small island between the mainland and the island of Čiovo. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
56033.m: Trogir is an island old town in Dalmatia.

56034.q: Which river flows right through the old town of Ljubljana?
56034.e: The Ljubljanica divides the old town of Ljubljana into two halves. There are many cafés and bridges along its banks.

56035.q: In which capital did the architect Jože Plečnik build the famous Triple Bridge?
56035.e: In the first half of the 20th century Jože Plečnik designed many bridges, squares and buildings in Ljubljana. His works have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021.
56035.m: Jože Plečnik shaped the look of Ljubljana.

56036.q: In which country is the city of Maribor, where the oldest grapevine in the world grows?
56036.e: Maribor is the second largest city in Slovenia. Its “Old Vine” is over 400 years old.
56036.m: The oldest grapevine in the world grows in Maribor in Slovenia.

56037.q: What do athletes do on the big hill at Planica in Slovenia?
a: They fly very far on skis
56037.e: Planica has one of the largest ski flying hills in the world. Ski jumpers fly further than 200 metres there, and several world records have been set.
56037.m: Planica is a famous place for ski flying.

56038.q: In which country are Lake Bled and Lake Bohinj?
56038.e: Both lakes lie in the Julian Alps in Slovenia. Lake Bohinj is the largest permanent natural lake in the country.

56039.q: On which big river is the Petrovaradin Fortress in Novi Sad?
56039.e: The Petrovaradin Fortress stands high above the Danube in Serbia. Today a big music festival takes place there every year.
56039.m: The Petrovaradin Fortress lies on the Danube.

56040.q: Into which big river does the Morava in Serbia flow?
56040.e: The Morava flows north through central Serbia and joins the Danube east of Belgrade.
56040.m: The Morava is a tributary of the Danube.

56041.q: In which country is the city of Niš, where Emperor Constantine was once born?
56041.e: Niš lies in the south of Serbia. In Roman times the city was called Naissus, and Constantine the Great was born there.
56041.m: Niš is a city in Serbia.

56042.q: What are the Kopaonik mountains in Serbia known for in winter?
56042.e: Kopaonik is over 2000 metres high and has the largest ski area in Serbia. It is also a national park.
56042.m: Kopaonik is Serbia's largest ski area.

56043.q: What is the capital of Serbia?
56043.e: Belgrade lies where the Sava flows into the Danube. To the south begins the hilly Šumadija, the heartland of Serbia.
56043.m: The capital of Serbia is Belgrade.

56044.q: For which fruit is Serbia one of the largest producers in the world?
56044.e: Serbia harvests a great many raspberries every year, especially in the west of the country. A large part of them is frozen and exported.
56044.m: Serbia is a big raspberry country.

56045.q: Which country did the Nobel Prize-winning writer Ivo Andrić come from?
56045.e: Ivo Andrić was born near Travnik in Bosnia in 1892 and received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1961. In his novels he describes the history of Bosnia.
56045.m: Ivo Andrić is a Nobel Prize winner from Bosnia.

56046.q: In which country is Sarajevo with its old bazaar, Baščaršija?
56046.e: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The old Baščaršija bazaar was created in the 15th century under the Ottomans.
56046.m: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

56047.q: What does the name Montenegro mean in English?
56047.e: Montenegro is Italian and means Black Mountain. The dark forests on the mountains gave the country its name.

56048.q: In which country is the island village of Sveti Stefan on the Adriatic?
56048.e: Sveti Stefan lies near Budva in Montenegro. The whole old fishing village on the rocky island is now a hotel.

56049.q: Lovćen is a mountain in Montenegro. What does the country's name Montenegro mean?
56049.e: Montenegro is Italian and means “Black Mountain”. Lovćen, with its dark forests, is considered a symbol of the country.

56050.q: On which sea is the town of Ulcinj in Montenegro?
56050.e: Montenegro lies on the Adriatic. Near Ulcinj in the south there is a sandy beach about 12 kilometres long.

56051.q: In which country is Durmitor National Park with its many mountain lakes?
56051.e: Durmitor lies in the north of Montenegro and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its small mountain lakes are called “mountain eyes”.

56052.q: On which sea is the port of Bar in Montenegro?
56052.e: Bar is the most important port in Montenegro. The country's coast lies on the Adriatic, opposite Italy.

56053.q: Where was the Ostrog Monastery in Montenegro built?
a: On an island in the sea
56053.e: The Ostrog Monastery was built into an almost vertical cliff face in the 17th century. It is an important place of pilgrimage.
56053.m: The Ostrog Monastery clings to a cliff face.

56054.q: On which sea does Albania lie?
56054.e: Albania lies on the Adriatic and the Ionian Sea. In the north of the country, the city of Shkodra lies on a large lake.

56055.q: Which city has the most important port in Albania?
56055.e: Durrës lies on the Adriatic near the capital. The city also has a large Roman amphitheatre.
56055.m: Durrës is the largest port in Albania.

56057.q: In which country is Gjirokastra, the “city of stone”?
56057.e: Gjirokastra lies in the south of Albania. The houses are built of grey stone and roofed with stone slabs; the old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56057.m: Gjirokastra is the “city of stone” in Albania.

56058.q: What are the high mountains in the north of Albania, also called the “Accursed Mountains”, called?
56058.e: The Albanian Alps are part of the Prokletije range, the southernmost part of the Dinaric Alps, on the border with Montenegro and Kosovo. The mountain villages of Theth and Valbona are well known.
56058.m: The Albanian Alps are also called the “Accursed Mountains”.

56059.q: Which animal is shown on the flag of Albania?
a: A black eagle with two heads
56059.e: Albania's red flag shows a black double-headed eagle. The Albanian name of the country, Shqipëria, is also often linked with the eagle.
56059.m: There is a double-headed eagle on Albania's flag.

56060.q: Pristina is the capital of which country?
56060.e: Pristina is the capital of Kosovo. Kosovo declared independence in 2008. The “Newborn” monument stands in the centre.
56060.m: Pristina is the capital of Kosovo.

56061.q: Which city has Romania's largest port on the Black Sea?
56061.e: Constanța is Romania's most important seaport. The port is also linked to the Danube by a canal.
56061.m: Constanța is Romania's big port on the Black Sea.

56062.q: In which country is Transylvania with the city of Sibiu?
56062.e: Sibiu is called Hermannstadt in German. The city in Transylvania was founded by German-speaking settlers and was European Capital of Culture in 2007.
56062.m: Sibiu is in Transylvania in Romania.

56063.q: In which country is the famous winding mountain road, the Transfăgărășan?
56063.e: The Transfăgărășan was built in the 1970s. It crosses the Carpathians in Romania with many hairpin bends and is only open in summer.
56063.m: The Transfăgărășan runs through the Carpathians in Romania.

56064.q: In which year did Romania and Bulgaria join the European Union?
56064.e: Romania and Bulgaria became members of the EU on 1 January 2007. They were not part of the big enlargement of 2004.
56064.m: Romania and Bulgaria have been in the EU since 2007.

56065.q: Which nickname did Bucharest get because of its splendid buildings and boulevards?
56065.e: Around 1900 many buildings in the French style were built in Bucharest. These even include its own triumphal arch.

56066.q: What are the painted monasteries of Moldavia in Bukovina in northern Romania famous for?
56066.e: The churches of these monasteries are completely painted on the outside with colourful pictures from the Bible. They date from the 15th and 16th centuries and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56066.m: The Moldavian monasteries have painted outside walls.

56067.q: In which country is the ancient city of Plovdiv?
56067.e: Plovdiv is the second largest city in Bulgaria and one of the oldest cities in Europe. In 2019 it was European Capital of Culture.
56067.m: Plovdiv is an ancient city in Bulgaria.

56068.q: In which country is Vitosha, the mountain on the doorstep of Sofia?
56068.e: Vitosha rises to about 2290 metres right on the edge of Sofia. It is a popular place for day trips.
56068.m: Vitosha is Sofia's home mountain in Bulgaria.

56069.q: On which sea is the old Bulgarian town of Nessebar?
56069.e: Nessebar lies on a small peninsula on the Black Sea. Its old town, over 3000 years old, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56069.m: Nessebar lies on the Black Sea.

56070.q: Which ancient people lived in the area of today's Bulgaria and left behind beautiful gold treasures?
56070.e: The Thracians lived in the area even before the Greeks and Romans. Burial mounds and gold treasures come from them, for example near Kazanlak.
56070.m: The Thracians used to live in Bulgaria.

56071.q: Which river forms most of the border between Bulgaria and Romania?
56071.e: For about 470 kilometres the Danube separates Bulgaria and Romania. At Ruse and Giurgiu a bridge links the two countries.
56071.m: The Danube separates Bulgaria from Romania.

56072.q: What is the capital of Bulgaria today?
56072.e: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria today. In the Middle Ages Veliko Tarnovo was the country's capital.
56072.m: The capital of Bulgaria is Sofia.

56073.q: What do people in Bulgaria welcome with red and white martenitsa bands from 1 March?
56073.e: The martenitsa is meant to bring good health. People wear it until they see the first stork or a tree in blossom.
56073.m: With the martenitsa, Bulgarians welcome spring.

56074.q: In which country is Pirin National Park with its many mountain lakes?
56074.e: Pirin National Park lies in the south-west of Bulgaria. It has many glacial lakes and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56074.m: Pirin is a national park in Bulgaria.

56077.q: Why is the Danube Delta slowly growing further out into the Black Sea?
a: The river deposits sand and mud
The sea level is falling sharply
56077.e: The Danube carries large amounts of sand and mud. They are deposited at the mouth, so new land is created.
56077.m: The Danube Delta grows through deposited mud.

56078.q: How do you reach many villages in the Danube Delta?
56078.e: There are hardly any roads in the delta, but many waterways. So people and goods mostly travel by boat.
56078.m: In the Danube Delta the boat is the most important means of transport.

56079.q: Which goddess is the Greek capital Athens named after?
56079.e: According to legend, Athena won a contest against Poseidon for the city by giving it an olive tree. That is why Athens bears her name.
56079.m: Athens is named after the goddess Athena.

56080.q: What is the name of the big port city right next to Athens?
56080.e: Piraeus is the most important port in Greece and forms one continuous urban area with Athens. Many ferries leave from here for the islands.
56080.m: The port of Athens is called Piraeus.

56081.q: In which year were the Summer Olympic Games last held in Athens?
56081.e: Athens hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2004. Beijing followed in 2008.
56081.m: In 2004 Athens was an Olympic city again.

56082.q: For which event was an old marble stadium in Athens rebuilt in 1896?
56082.e: The first modern Olympic Games took place in Athens in 1896. For them, the Panathenaic Stadium was rebuilt in white marble.
56082.m: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

56083.q: Which form of government came about in ancient Athens and is considered its greatest legacy?
56083.e: In the 5th century BC the free citizens of Athens could have their say in the people's assembly. The word democracy means “rule by the people”.
56083.m: Athens is considered the cradle of democracy.

56084.q: What is the rocky hill with ancient temples in the middle of Athens called?
56084.e: The Acropolis towers over the old town of Athens. The Capitoline Hill is in Rome, Montmartre in Paris, and Mount Olympus is a mountain in northern Greece.

56085.q: What is special about the Erechtheion temple on the Acropolis?
a: Statues of women hold up the roof
It is made entirely of gold
It has no walls and no roof
56085.e: At the Erechtheion, six statues of women instead of columns hold up the roof of the porch. Such figures are called caryatids.
56085.m: At the Erechtheion, statues of women hold up the roof.

56087.q: To which goddess was the Parthenon on the Acropolis dedicated?
56087.e: The Parthenon was the temple of Athena, the protector goddess of Athens. A huge statue of her used to stand inside.
56087.m: The Parthenon was the temple of Athena.

56088.q: Roughly how old is the Parthenon on the Acropolis?
56088.e: The Parthenon was built in the 5th century BC, so about 2500 years ago. An explosion in 1687 turned it into a ruin.
56088.m: The Parthenon is about 2500 years old.

56089.q: Which organisation has declared the Acropolis of Athens a World Heritage Site?
56089.e: UNESCO keeps a list of especially valuable places in the world. The Acropolis has been on it since 1987.
56089.m: The Acropolis is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56090.q: What material are the temples on the Acropolis mainly built of?
56090.e: The temples of the Acropolis are made of white marble from the mountains near Athens. Concrete and brick were not used for them.
56090.m: The Acropolis is built of marble.

56092.q: Which group of islands does Corfu belong to?
56092.e: Corfu lies in the Ionian Sea off the west coast of Greece. Kefalonia and Zakynthos also belong to this group.
56092.m: Corfu is one of the Ionian Islands.

56093.q: Which island is the home of Odysseus in Homer's legends?
56093.e: In the “Odyssey”, Odysseus spends ten years after the Trojan War trying to get home to Ithaca. Ithaca is one of the Ionian Islands.

56094.q: What does the name of the island group Dodecanese mean?
56094.e: “Dodeka” means twelve in Greek. Today, though, the group has more than twelve islands; the largest is Rhodes.

56095.q: On which island was the mathematician Pythagoras born?
56095.e: Pythagoras came from the island of Samos in the eastern Aegean. A harbour town there is called Pythagorio in his honour.

56096.q: Where do the Cyclades get their name from?
a: They lie in a circle around Delos
They are named after a king
56096.e: “Kyklos” means circle. The islands lie roughly in a circle around the small sacred island of Delos.
56096.m: The Cyclades form a circle around Delos.

56097.q: Which country do the Cyclades belong to?
56097.e: The Cyclades are a group of islands in the Aegean and belong to Greece. Santorini, Mykonos and Naxos are well known.

56098.q: On which Cycladic island was the famous statue “Venus de Milo” found in 1820?
56098.e: A farmer found the statue on the island of Milos in 1820. Today it stands in the Louvre in Paris.
56098.m: The Venus de Milo comes from the island of Milos.

56099.q: According to legend, which gods were born on the island of Delos?
56099.e: The goddess Leto gave birth to the twins Apollo and Artemis on Delos. That is why Delos was a sacred island.
56099.m: According to legend, Apollo and Artemis were born on Delos.

56100.q: Which canal separates the Peloponnese peninsula from the rest of the Greek mainland?
56100.e: The Corinth Canal cuts through the narrow isthmus between the Peloponnese and the mainland. Since then, strictly speaking, the Peloponnese has been an island.
56100.m: The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnese from the mainland.

56101.q: What is especially striking about the Corinth Canal?
a: It is very narrow with steep rock walls
It is frozen all year round
56101.e: The canal is only about 6 kilometres long and about 25 metres wide at the surface. Its rock walls are up to 80 metres high. It opened in 1893.
56101.m: The Corinth Canal is narrow and cut deep into the rock.

56102.q: Where in the Peloponnese were the Olympic Games of ancient times held?
56102.e: The games were held in honour of Zeus at the sanctuary of Olympia. The Olympic flame is still lit there today.
56102.m: The ancient Olympic Games took place at Olympia.

56103.q: Which ancient city-state in the Peloponnese was known for its strict training of warriors?
56103.e: In Sparta, boys were brought up harshly as soldiers from about the age of seven. That is where the word “spartan”, meaning simple and strict, comes from.
56103.m: Sparta was known for its harsh upbringing.

56104.q: What is Epidaurus in the Peloponnese especially famous for?
56104.e: The theatre of Epidaurus holds over 12,000 spectators and has remarkable acoustics. You can hear even a quiet word in the top row.
56104.m: The theatre of Epidaurus is famous for its acoustics.

56105.q: In which ancient citadel is the famous Lion Gate?
56105.e: The Lion Gate was the main entrance to the citadel of Mycenae. Two stone lions stand above the gate.
56105.m: The Lion Gate is at Mycenae.

56106.q: Which sea surrounds the Peloponnese peninsula?
56106.e: The Peloponnese lies in the south of Greece and is surrounded by the Mediterranean. Towns such as Nafplio, the first capital of modern Greece, are there.
56106.m: The Peloponnese lies in the Mediterranean.

56107.e: “Nesos” means island. The peninsula is named after Pelops, a king from Greek legend.

56108.q: According to Greek legend, who lived on Mount Olympus?
56108.e: The ancient Greeks believed that Zeus and the other gods lived on Mount Olympus. The highest summit is called Mytikas.
56108.m: The Greek gods lived on Mount Olympus.

56109.q: Which country did the two mountaineers come from who, together with a Greek, first climbed Mount Olympus in 1913?
56109.e: Frédéric Boissonnas and Daniel Baud-Bovy from Geneva, together with the Greek Christos Kakkalos, were the first to reach the highest summit in 1913.
56109.m: Two men from Geneva took part in the first ascent of Mount Olympus in 1913.

56110.q: What did the area around Mount Olympus become in 1938, the first of its kind in Greece?
56110.e: In 1938 Mount Olympus was declared Greece's first national park. Many rare plants grow there.
56110.m: Mount Olympus is the oldest national park in Greece.

56111.q: Between which two countries does the Aegean Sea lie?
56111.e: The Aegean lies between the Greek mainland in the west and Asia Minor (Turkey) in the east. It is part of the Mediterranean.
56111.m: The Aegean lies between Greece and Turkey.

56112.q: According to legend, who is the Aegean Sea named after?
56112.e: Aegeus was waiting for his son Theseus. When he saw a black sail, he thought his son was dead and threw himself into the sea.
56112.m: The Aegean is named after King Aegeus.

56113.q: Which Greek group of islands with white houses lies in the Aegean?
56113.e: The Cyclades include islands such as Santorini and Mykonos. They are known for white houses with blue roofs.
56113.m: The Cyclades lie in the Aegean.

56114.q: Which Greek city lies in the north of the Aegean on the Thermaic Gulf?
56114.e: Thessaloniki is the second largest city in Greece. It lies on the Thermaic Gulf in the north-west of the Aegean.
56114.m: Thessaloniki lies on the Thermaic Gulf.

56115.q: Which big Turkish city lies on the Aegean coast?
56115.e: Izmir, formerly Smyrna, is the third largest city in Turkey. It lies on a bay of the Aegean.
56115.m: Izmir is the big Turkish city on the Aegean.

56116.q: Which is the largest island in Greece?
56116.e: Crete is the largest Greek island and lies on the southern edge of the Aegean. Cyprus is a separate country.
56116.m: Crete is the largest island in Greece.

56117.q: Which two continents does the Bosporus separate?
56117.e: The Bosporus separates the European part of Istanbul from the Asian part. Bridges and tunnels link the two sides.
56117.m: The Bosporus separates Europe from Asia.

56119.q: Which famous building in Istanbul was the largest church in Christendom for almost 1000 years?
56119.e: Hagia Sophia was built as a church in the 6th century. After 1453 it became a mosque, later a museum, and in 2020 a mosque again.
56119.m: Hagia Sophia was once the largest church in the world.

56120.q: Why is a famous mosque in Istanbul called the “Blue Mosque”?
a: Because of the blue tiles inside
Because it is painted blue outside
Because it stands in the sea
Because its roof is made of blue glass
56120.e: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque from the 17th century is decorated inside with over 20,000 blue tiles. Outside it is grey.
56120.m: The Blue Mosque is named after its tiles.

56121.q: In which palace in Istanbul did the Ottoman sultans live for about 400 years?
56121.e: Topkapi Palace stands on a hill by the Bosporus. From there the sultans ruled their great empire.
56121.m: The sultans lived in Topkapi Palace for a long time.

56122.q: Who made Ankara the capital of the new Turkey in 1923?
56122.e: Atatürk founded the Turkish Republic in 1923 and chose Ankara as its capital. The city lies protected in the interior of the country.

56123.q: Who is buried in the great Anıtkabir mausoleum in Ankara?
56123.e: Atatürk founded the Turkish Republic in 1923. After his death he was given the great Anıtkabir mausoleum in Ankara.
56123.m: Atatürk rests in the Anıtkabir in Ankara.

56124.q: Which animals carry Ankara’s former name “Angora” in their names?
56124.e: The Angora cat, Angora goat and Angora rabbit are named after Ankara. Angora goats provide mohair wool.
56124.m: The Angora animals are named after Ankara.

56125.q: Where does Ankara rank among the largest cities in Turkey?
56125.e: Ankara has over 5 million inhabitants (as of 2024) and is the second largest city in Turkey after Istanbul.
56125.m: Ankara is the second largest city in Turkey.

56126.q: In which region of Turkey is Ankara?
56126.e: Ankara lies on a plateau in the middle of Anatolia, at around 900 metres above sea level.
56126.m: Ankara lies in the heart of Anatolia.

56127.q: What other name is often used for Anatolia?
56127.e: Anatolia is the large peninsula between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. It is also called Asia Minor.
56127.m: Anatolia is also called Asia Minor.

56128.q: Which country does the Anatolian peninsula belong to today?
56128.e: Anatolia makes up most of Turkey. The name comes from the Greek word for sunrise, because the land lies to the east as seen from Greece.

56129.q: On which continent is most of Turkey?
56129.e: Almost all of Turkey lies on the Anatolian peninsula in Asia. Only a small part around Istanbul belongs to Europe.
56129.m: Most of Turkey lies in Asia.

56130.q: Which mountain in eastern Anatolia is the highest in Turkey?
56130.e: Ararat is a volcano about 5137 metres high. According to the Bible, Noah’s Ark is said to have come to rest there.
56130.m: Ararat is the highest mountain in Turkey.

56131.q: Which two great rivers rise in the highlands of eastern Anatolia?
56131.e: The Euphrates and Tigris rise in the mountains of eastern Anatolia and then flow through Syria and Iraq. Mesopotamia lies between them.
56131.m: The Euphrates and Tigris come from eastern Anatolia.

56132.q: Which sea lies north of Anatolia?
56132.e: Anatolia is surrounded by three seas: the Black Sea to the north, the Mediterranean to the south and the Aegean to the west.
56132.m: The Black Sea lies north of Anatolia.

56133.q: Which large city lies partly in Europe and partly in Anatolia?
56133.e: Istanbul lies on both sides of the Bosporus. One part of the city belongs to Europe, the other to Anatolia in Asia.

56134.q: Which famous city of legend, where the fight over Helen took place, lay in north-western Anatolia?
56134.e: Troy lay near the Dardanelles. Heinrich Schliemann excavated the ruins from 1871.

56135.q: What are the pointed rock towers in Cappadocia called?
56135.e: The fairy chimneys formed because wind and water wore away soft rock. Caps of harder rock protected the columns underneath.
56135.m: Cappadocia’s rock towers are called fairy chimneys.

56136.q: What kind of rock are the rocks of Cappadocia mainly made of?
56136.e: Volcanoes such as Erciyes covered the land with ash, which turned into soft tuff. This rock is easy to hollow out.
56136.m: Cappadocia’s rocks are made of tuff.

56137.q: In what do many tourists fly over Cappadocia early in the morning?
56137.e: At sunrise, often more than a hundred hot-air balloons rise over Göreme. The calm morning air makes the flights possible.
56137.m: In Cappadocia people fly in hot-air balloons.

56138.e: Derinkuyu goes down many storeys and gave shelter to thousands of people. There were stables, kitchens and air shafts.

56139.q: What can you find in the Göreme Open-Air Museum?
56139.e: Christian monks carved churches and monasteries into the soft rock. Many are decorated with colourful wall paintings.
56139.m: There are rock churches in Göreme.

56140.q: In what do many tourists float over the rocky landscape of Cappadocia in the morning?
56140.e: Almost every morning many hot-air balloons rise in Cappadocia. From above you can see the fairy chimneys and valleys.
56140.m: Cappadocia is known for balloon flights.

56141.q: In which part of Turkey is Cappadocia?
56141.e: Cappadocia lies on a plateau in the middle of Anatolia, south-east of Ankara.

56142.q: What is special about Nicosia, the capital of Cyprus?
a: It is divided into two parts
56142.e: Since 1974 Cyprus has been divided into a northern and a southern part. The border runs right through Nicosia.

56143.q: Which currency do people use in the south of Cyprus?
56143.e: Cyprus has been in the EU since 2004 and introduced the euro in 2008.
56143.m: In Cyprus you pay with the euro.

56144.q: Which metal is named after the island of Cyprus?
56144.e: In ancient times a lot of copper was mined on Cyprus. The Latin name “cuprum” comes from the name of the island.
56144.m: Copper is named after the island of Cyprus.

56145.q: Which two languages are official languages of the Republic of Cyprus?
56145.e: The constitution of 1960 sets Greek and Turkish as official languages. English is also widely spoken in everyday life.
56145.m: Greek and Turkish are the official languages of Cyprus.

56146.q: Which two seas do the Dardanelles connect?
56146.e: The Dardanelles lead from the Sea of Marmara into the Aegean, part of the Mediterranean.
56146.m: The Dardanelles connect the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean.

56147.q: Which famous ancient city lay near the Dardanelles?
56147.e: The ruins of Troy lie in Turkey near the entrance to the Dardanelles. The legend of the Trojan Horse is set around Troy.

56148.q: What record does the Çanakkale Bridge over the Dardanelles, opened in 2022, hold?
a: Longest span of any suspension bridge
56148.e: The main span of the bridge measures 2023 metres. This makes it the suspension bridge with the longest span in the world.
56148.m: The Çanakkale Bridge has the longest span of all suspension bridges.

56149.q: Which country do the Dardanelles belong to?
56149.e: Both shores of the Dardanelles belong to Turkey. The northern shore lies in Europe, the southern one in Asia.

56150.q: What is the peninsula on the European shore of the Dardanelles called?
56150.e: The Gallipoli peninsula, Gelibolu in Turkish, lies on the European side. Opposite lies Anatolia.
56150.m: Gallipoli lies on the European shore of the Dardanelles.

56151.e: The Dardanelles are a narrow strait in Turkey, about 60 kilometres long.

56152.q: Which two continents do the Dardanelles separate?
56152.e: On the northern shore of the Dardanelles lies the European Gallipoli peninsula, on the southern shore Anatolia in Asia.
56152.m: The Dardanelles separate Europe and Asia.

56153.q: What are the Bosporus and the Dardanelles called together with the Sea of Marmara?
56153.e: The Turkish Straits connect the Black Sea with the Mediterranean.
56153.m: The Bosporus, Sea of Marmara and Dardanelles form the Turkish Straits.

56155.q: In which direction does the water flow at the surface of the Bosporus?
a: From the Black Sea into the Sea of Marmara
From the Sea of Marmara into the Black Sea
It does not flow at all
56155.e: Large rivers such as the Danube flow into the Black Sea, so its water is less salty and stands higher. It flows out southwards at the top, while saltier water flows north in the depths.
56155.m: At the surface, the Bosporus flows south from the Black Sea.

56156.q: Which big city lies on both sides of the Bosporus?
56156.e: Istanbul lies both in Europe and in Asia. The Bosporus runs right through the city.

56157.q: Why is the Bosporus so important for shipping?
a: It is the only sea route from the Black Sea to the Mediterranean
It is the deepest point of the oceans
It is always frozen in winter
It connects the North Sea with the Baltic Sea
56157.e: Ships from ports on the Black Sea must pass through the Bosporus to reach the Mediterranean and the rest of the world.
56157.m: The Bosporus is the gateway to the Black Sea.

56158.q: What was the city of Istanbul on the Bosporus called in the past?
56158.e: In ancient times the city was called Byzantium and later Constantinople. The Ottomans conquered it in 1453; today it is called Istanbul.
56158.m: Istanbul used to be called Constantinople.

56159.q: What is the Galata Tower in Istanbul used for today?
56159.e: The Galata Tower was built in 1348 by merchants from Genoa. Today you can climb up and look out over the whole city.
56159.m: From the Galata Tower you can see across Istanbul.

56160.q: What was the Greek settlement that later became Istanbul called?
56160.e: Greek settlers founded Byzantion on the Bosporus in the 7th century BC. The name Byzantine Empire also comes from it.
56160.m: Istanbul was originally the Greek city of Byzantion.

56161.q: What was Istanbul called when it was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
56161.e: Emperor Constantine made the city his capital in the 4th century and named it Constantinople. It has officially been called Istanbul since 1930.
56161.m: Istanbul used to be called Constantinople.

56162.q: What are the slender towers next to the mosques in Istanbul called?
56162.e: The call to prayer is made from the minarets. The Süleymaniye Mosque has four, the Blue Mosque even six.
56162.m: The towers of a mosque are called minarets.

56163.q: What was the Hagia Sophia in Istanbul originally?
56163.e: The Hagia Sophia was consecrated as a church in 537 under Emperor Justinian. Later it became a mosque, a museum and in 2020 a mosque again.
56163.m: The Hagia Sophia was built as a church.

56164.q: Which strait divides Istanbul into a European and an Asian part?
56164.e: The Bosporus connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara. Europe lies to the west of it, Asia to the east.
56164.m: The Bosporus divides Istanbul into Europe and Asia.

56165.q: In which country is Mount Olympus?
56165.e: Mount Olympus is the highest mountain in Greece. Hikes usually start in the village of Litochoro at the foot of the mountain.

56167.q: Which Cycladic island is known for white houses with blue domes on the edge of a volcanic crater?
56167.e: Santorini was formed by a huge volcanic eruption. The white villages sit high above the edge of the crater.
56167.m: Santorini is a volcanic island in the Cyclades.

56168.q: From which white stone did the ancient Greeks make many statues?
56168.e: On the Cyclades, for example on Paros, fine white marble was quarried. Many famous statues were made from it.
56168.m: Greek statues are often made of marble.

56169.q: What is the early Cycladic culture of the Bronze Age especially known for?
56169.e: The so-called Cycladic idols are very simplified human figures made of marble. They are about 4500 years old and look like modern art.
56169.m: The Cycladic culture made flat marble figures.

56170.q: What is the sea between Greece and Turkey with very many islands called?
56170.e: The Aegean is part of the Mediterranean. Island groups such as the Cyclades and the Dodecanese lie in it.
56170.m: The Aegean lies between Greece and Turkey.

56171.q: Which island in the Ionian Sea is known as a place where loggerhead turtles lay their eggs?
56171.e: On the sandy beaches of Laganas Bay on Zakynthos, sea turtles lay their eggs. A marine national park protects them.
56171.m: Sea turtles lay their eggs on Zakynthos.

56172.q: According to legend, which Greek god grew up as a child in a cave on Crete?
56172.e: According to legend, his mother hid Zeus in a cave on Crete. That way he escaped his father Kronos.
56172.m: According to legend, Zeus grew up on Crete.

56173.q: In which sea is the island of Cyprus?
56173.e: Cyprus lies in the eastern Mediterranean, south of Turkey. It is the third largest island in the Mediterranean.
56173.m: Cyprus is an island in the Mediterranean.

56174.q: What is the buffer zone, monitored by the UN, that divides Cyprus called?
56174.e: The buffer zone runs right across the island and through the middle of Nicosia. Its name comes from a line drawn on a map with a green pen.

56175.q: What does the Greek word “Acropolis” mean?
56175.e: “Akros” means high and “polis” means city. So the Acropolis is the high upper city on a rock.

56176.q: Where is the Acropolis of Athens?
a: On a rocky hill in the middle of the city
On an island in the sea
High in the mountains far from Athens
56176.e: The Acropolis stands on a steep limestone rock in the middle of Athens. From there you can see across the whole city.
56176.m: The Acropolis towers on a rock above Athens.

56177.q: How many countries does Poland border?
56177.e: Poland borders Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania and Russia (Kaliningrad region).

56178.q: What was Solidarność, founded in Gdańsk in 1980?
56178.e: In 1980 the workers at the Gdańsk shipyard went on strike and founded the free trade union Solidarność. It helped Poland later become a democracy.
56178.m: The trade union Solidarność began in Gdańsk.

56179.q: What is the Wieliczka salt mine near Kraków famous for?
a: For underground chapels and figures made of salt
For a coal power station inside the mountain
For an underground lake with whales
56179.e: Salt was mined in Wieliczka for over 700 years. Underground, miners carved whole chapels and figures out of salt.
56179.m: The Wieliczka salt mine has chapels made of salt.

56180.q: Which river forms part of the border between Germany and Poland?
56180.e: The Oder and its tributary the Neisse form a large part of the border. The Polish city of Wrocław also lies on the Oder.
56180.m: The Oder separates Germany and Poland.

56181.q: In which mountain range is Poland’s highest mountain, Rysy?
56181.e: Rysy (about 2500 m) lies in the High Tatras, right on the border with Slovakia.
56181.m: Poland’s highest mountain is in the High Tatras.

56182.q: What is the large lake district in north-eastern Poland called?
56182.e: In Masuria in north-eastern Poland there are over a thousand lakes, often linked by canals.
56182.m: The Masurian Lake District is in north-eastern Poland.

56183.q: In which year did Poland join the European Union?
56183.e: Poland became a member of the EU on 1 May 2004 together with nine other countries.
56183.m: Poland has been in the European Union since 2004.

56184.q: Who did the people fight against in the Warsaw Uprising of 1944?
56184.e: In the Second World War Warsaw was occupied by Germany. The uprising in 1944 lasted about two months, after which the city was largely destroyed.
56184.m: The Warsaw Uprising was against the German occupation.

56185.q: Which city was the capital of Poland before Warsaw?
56185.e: King Sigismund III moved his seat from Kraków to Warsaw at the end of the 16th century.
56185.m: Before Warsaw, Kraków was the capital of Poland.

56186.q: Which military alliance of the Eastern Bloc countries was named after the Polish capital in 1955?
56186.e: The Warsaw Pact was founded in Warsaw in 1955 and dissolved in 1991.
56186.m: The Warsaw Pact was founded in Warsaw in 1955.

56187.q: What is the large park in Warsaw with a palace on the water called?
56187.e: The Palace on the Isle stands in Łazienki Park. In summer there are open-air Chopin concerts there.
56187.m: In Łazienki Park there is a palace on the water.

56188.q: About how many inhabitants does Warsaw have (as of 2024)?
56188.e: About 1.8 million people live in Warsaw. That is about four times as many as in Zurich.

56189.q: In which part of Poland does the Vistula rise?
a: In the south in the mountains
In the north on the coast
In the west on the border with Germany
56189.e: The Vistula rises in the Beskids, a mountain range in southern Poland. From there it flows north to the Baltic Sea.
56189.m: The Vistula rises in southern Poland.

56190.q: Which record does the Vistula hold?
a: Longest river flowing into the Baltic Sea
River with the most water in the world
56190.e: At about 1050 kilometres, the Vistula is longer than the Oder, Daugava and Neman, which also flow into the Baltic Sea.
56190.m: The Vistula is the longest river flowing into the Baltic Sea.

56191.q: Which old royal city in southern Poland lies on the Vistula?
56191.e: Kraków lies on the Vistula. The royal castle of Wawel stands above the old town.

56192.q: Which countries does the Vistula flow through?
56192.e: The Vistula flows entirely within Poland, from its source to its mouth.
56192.m: The Vistula flows only through Poland.

56193.q: What is the eastern part of the Czech Republic, with the city of Brno, called?
56193.e: The Czech Republic consists mainly of Bohemia in the west and Moravia in the east. Brno is the capital of Moravia and the second largest city in the country.

56194.q: Which famous spa town in western Bohemia is known for its hot springs?
56194.e: Hot mineral springs bubble up in Karlovy Vary. For centuries, visitors have come to the town to take the waters.
56194.m: Karlovy Vary is a famous spa town in the Czech Republic.

56195.e: The Vltava flows right through the middle of Prague. The famous Charles Bridge crosses it.

56196.q: Which mountain range lies on the Czech Republic’s northern border with Poland?
56196.e: The Giant Mountains lie between the Czech Republic and Poland. The Elbe also rises there.
56196.m: The Giant Mountains separate the Czech Republic and Poland.

56197.q: Which language group does Czech belong to?
56197.e: Czech is a West Slavic language and closely related to Slovak.

56198.q: Which university in Prague was founded in 1348 and is considered the oldest university in Central Europe?
56198.e: Emperor Charles IV founded the university in Prague in 1348. Vienna followed in 1365, Basel in 1460.
56198.m: Charles University in Prague is the oldest university in Central Europe.

56199.q: What is the modern, curved building in Prague that looks like a dancing couple called?
56199.e: The Dancing House was completed in 1996. Its two towers look like a couple dancing.
56199.m: The Dancing House is a modern landmark of Prague.

56200.q: What is the 1968 reform movement in Czechoslovakia, ended by Warsaw Pact troops, called?
56200.e: In 1968 the government in Prague tried to allow more freedom. In August, troops from several Eastern Bloc countries ended these reforms.
56200.m: The Prague Spring was the reform movement of 1968.

56201.q: Which figure made of clay is a famous legend from the Jewish quarter of Prague?
56201.e: According to the legend, Rabbi Loew shaped a man out of clay, the Golem, who was meant to protect the Jewish community.
56201.m: The Golem is a legendary figure from Prague.

56202.q: Which structure does the lookout tower on Petřín Hill in Prague remind you of?
56202.e: The lookout tower was built in 1891 as a smaller copy of the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
56202.m: Prague’s Petřín Tower looks like a small Eiffel Tower.

56203.q: Which capital does the Vltava flow through?
56203.e: The Vltava, called Moldau in German, flows right through Prague. The famous Charles Bridge crosses it.

56204.q: In which mountain range does the Vltava rise?
56204.e: The Vltava rises in the Bohemian Forest in the south-west of the Czech Republic, near the border with Germany.
56204.m: The Vltava rises in the Bohemian Forest.

56205.q: Which composer dedicated a famous piece of music to the river Vltava?
56205.e: “Vltava” is part of the cycle “My Country” by Bedřich Smetana. The music follows the course of the river.
56205.m: Bedřich Smetana set the Vltava to music.

56206.q: What is the Vltava for the Czech Republic?
a: The longest river that runs entirely within the country
56206.e: The Vltava is about 430 kilometres long and flows entirely within the Czech Republic, from its source to where it joins the Elbe.
56206.m: The Vltava is the longest river in the Czech Republic.

56207.q: What is the second largest city of Slovakia, in the east of the country, called?
56207.e: Košice lies in the east of Slovakia and is the largest city after the capital.
56207.m: Košice is the second largest city in Slovakia.

56208.q: Which high mountain range lies in the north of Slovakia?
56208.e: The High Tatras are the highest part of the Carpathians. Slovakia’s highest mountain, Gerlach Peak, is also there.
56208.m: The High Tatras are Slovakia’s high mountains.

56209.q: About how many inhabitants does Slovakia have (as of 2024)?
56209.e: About 5.4 million people live in Slovakia, clearly fewer than in Switzerland.

56210.q: Which great river forms part of Slovakia’s southern border?
56210.e: The Danube forms a long stretch of the border between Slovakia and Hungary.
56210.m: The Danube partly separates Slovakia from Hungary.

56211.q: Which country does NOT border Slovakia?
56211.e: Slovakia borders the Czech Republic, Poland, Ukraine, Hungary and Austria, but not Germany.

56212.q: Because of its four corner towers, what is Bratislava Castle often compared to?
56212.e: The castle is a rectangular building with four corner towers. That is why people say it looks like an upside-down table.
56212.m: Bratislava Castle looks like an upside-down table.

56213.e: Bratislava lies on the Danube, only about 60 kilometres from Vienna.

56214.q: What is the Danube bridge in Bratislava with a round restaurant on top of its pillar called?
56214.e: On top of the bridge’s pillar sits a round restaurant that looks like a flying saucer.
56214.m: The UFO Bridge is a landmark of Bratislava.

56215.q: What is special about the location of Bratislava?
a: The city borders two other countries
The city lies on an island in the sea
The city lies higher than 2000 metres
The city lies on the Baltic Sea
56215.e: Bratislava borders both Austria and Hungary directly. This is unique among capital cities.

56216.q: About how high is Hungary’s highest mountain, Kékes?
56216.e: Kékes is 1014 metres high. Hungary is a rather flat country without high mountains.
56216.m: Hungary’s highest mountain is only about 1000 metres high.

56217.q: Which warm lake in Hungary is one of the largest thermal lakes in the world that you can swim in?
56217.e: Lake Hévíz is fed by a warm spring. Even in winter the water is warm enough for swimming.
56217.m: You can swim in Lake Hévíz even in winter.

56218.q: What colours is the flag of Hungary?
56218.e: The Hungarian flag has three horizontal stripes: red at the top, white in the middle and green at the bottom.
56218.m: The Hungarian flag is red, white and green.

56219.q: What is different about Hungarian personal names compared with English?
a: The family name comes before the first name
The name is written from right to left
56219.e: In Hungary people say, for example, “Liszt Ferenc”: first the family name, then the first name.
56219.m: In Hungary the family name comes before the first name.

56220.q: Apart from the Danube, which river flows through Hungary as the second great river?
56220.e: The Tisza flows through the east of Hungary and later joins the Danube in Serbia.
56220.m: The Tisza is Hungary’s second great river.

56221.q: Which famous puzzle was invented by a Hungarian in 1974?
56221.e: The Rubik’s Cube was invented by the Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik, which is why it bears his name.
56221.m: The Rubik’s Cube comes from Hungary.

56222.q: Which towns was Budapest formed from in 1873?
56222.e: In 1873 Buda and Óbuda on the right bank of the Danube and Pest on the left bank were united into one city.
56222.m: Budapest was formed from Buda, Óbuda and Pest.

56223.q: Which viewing terrace with seven little towers stands on Castle Hill in Budapest?
56223.e: Fisherman’s Bastion was built around 1900. Its seven little towers stand for the seven Hungarian tribes.
56223.m: Fisherman’s Bastion has seven little towers.

56224.q: On which side of Budapest is Castle Hill with the royal palace?
a: On an island in the river
56224.e: Buda is the hilly part of Budapest. The castle palace stands there on Castle Hill, while Pest is flat.
56224.m: The castle palace stands on the Buda side.

56225.q: About how many inhabitants does Budapest have (as of 2024)?
56225.e: About 1.7 million people live in Budapest, which is about a sixth of Hungary’s population.

56226.q: What is the large square in Budapest with the Millennium Monument and statues of Hungarian rulers called?
56226.e: Heroes’ Square was laid out for Hungary’s 1000-year celebration in 1896. Statues of the Hungarian tribal leaders and kings stand there.
56226.m: The Millennium Monument stands on Heroes’ Square.

56227.q: In which country is Lake Balaton?
56227.e: Lake Balaton is the largest lake in Central Europe. On its northern shore the Tihany peninsula juts out into the lake.

56228.q: About how long is Lake Balaton?
56228.e: Lake Balaton is about 77 kilometres long, but in most places only a few kilometres wide.
56228.m: Lake Balaton is long and narrow.

56229.q: What is typical of the water of Lake Balaton?
56229.e: On average Lake Balaton is only about 3 metres deep. That is why it warms up quickly in summer.
56229.m: Lake Balaton is shallow and warm in summer.

56230.q: What do people in Hungary often jokingly call Lake Balaton?
56230.e: Because Hungary has no sea coast, the large lake is also called the “Hungarian Sea”. Many families go there for beach holidays.
56230.m: Lake Balaton is the Hungarian Sea.

56231.q: Which currency do people use today in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania?
56231.e: All three Baltic states use the euro: Estonia since 2011, Latvia since 2014 and Lithuania since 2015.
56231.m: In the Baltic states you pay with euros.

56232.q: From which state did the Baltic states become independent in 1990 and 1991?
56232.e: The three countries were occupied and annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940. In 1990/91 they regained their independence.
56232.m: The Baltic states broke away from the Soviet Union.

56234.q: What is the peaceful freedom movement in the Baltic states, in which many people sang songs together, called?
56234.e: At the end of the 1980s, hundreds of thousands of people met at song festivals. Singing together became a sign of resistance.
56234.m: The freedom movement in the Baltic states is called the Singing Revolution.

56235.q: In which year did Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania become members of the EU?
56235.e: All three Baltic states joined the EU on 1 May 2004, and NATO in the same year.
56235.m: The Baltic states have been in the EU since 2004.

56237.q: Which of the Baltic states lies furthest south?
56237.e: Lithuania is the southernmost Baltic state and borders Poland and Belarus.
56237.m: Lithuania is the southernmost Baltic state.

56238.q: What is Trakai Castle in Lithuania?
a: A castle on an island in a lake
A tower in the middle of the sea
56238.e: Trakai Island Castle lies on an island in Lake Galvė west of Vilnius and is a popular place for day trips.
56238.m: Trakai Castle stands on an island.

56239.q: Which port city on the Baltic Sea belongs to Lithuania?
56239.e: Klaipėda, formerly Memel, is Lithuania’s only large seaport.

56241.e: Latvia has a long coast on the Baltic Sea. Riga lies on the Gulf of Riga, where the Daugava flows into the sea.
56241.m: Latvia lies on the Baltic Sea.

56242.q: Which architectural style is the centre of Riga famous for?
56242.e: Riga has one of the largest collections of Art Nouveau buildings in Europe. The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56242.m: Riga is known for its Art Nouveau buildings.

56243.q: Which Baltic state lies in the middle between the other two?
56243.e: Latvia borders Estonia to the north and Lithuania to the south.
56243.m: Latvia lies between Estonia and Lithuania.

56244.q: Which medieval league of towns did Tallinn, formerly called Reval, belong to?
56244.e: Reval was an important trading town of the Hanseatic League. The well-preserved old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56245.q: Which large lake forms part of the border between Estonia and Russia?
56245.e: Lake Peipus is one of the largest lakes in Europe. The border between Estonia and Russia runs right through it.
56245.m: Lake Peipus lies on the border with Russia.

56246.q: About how many inhabitants does Estonia have (as of 2024)?
56246.e: Only about 1.4 million people live in Estonia, fewer than in the canton of Zurich.
56246.m: Estonia has only about 1.4 million inhabitants.

56247.q: What is Estonia especially known for today?
56247.e: In Estonia you can do almost all official business online. The software Skype was also partly developed there.
56247.m: Estonia is a pioneer of digitalisation.

56248.q: What is Estonia’s largest island called?
56248.e: Saaremaa lies in the Baltic Sea off the west coast of Estonia. Gotland belongs to Sweden, Rügen to Germany, Bornholm to Denmark.

a: A long, narrow strip of sand between a lagoon and the Baltic Sea
A mountain ridge in the Carpathians
56249.e: The Curonian Spit is a tongue of sand about 98 kilometres long. It separates the Curonian Lagoon from the Baltic Sea.
56249.m: The Curonian Spit is a narrow tongue of sand.

56250.q: Which sea is the Curonian Spit on?
56250.e: The Curonian Spit separates the Curonian Lagoon from the Baltic Sea. It belongs partly to Lithuania and partly to Russia.
56250.m: The Curonian Spit lies on the Baltic Sea.

56251.q: What are the landscapes of the Curonian Spit known for?
56251.e: The spit has some of the highest shifting dunes in Europe. The wind slowly moves the sand along.
56251.m: High dunes move along the Curonian Spit.

56252.q: What slowly moves the dunes on the Curonian Spit?
56252.e: The wind carries the sand from one side of the dune to the other. In this way the dunes slowly move along.
56252.m: Shifting dunes are moved by the wind.

56253.q: In which year did Ukraine become an independent state?
56253.e: Ukraine declared its independence in 1991 when the Soviet Union broke up.

56254.q: Which script is Ukrainian written in?
56254.e: Ukrainian is written with a Cyrillic alphabet that also has letters such as “ї” and “є”.
56254.m: Ukrainian is written in Cyrillic letters.

56255.q: Where did a serious accident at a nuclear power plant happen in 1986?
56255.e: In 1986 a reactor exploded at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in northern Ukraine. Radioactive substances reached as far as Switzerland.
56255.m: The Chernobyl reactor accident happened in 1986.

56256.q: What is the shallow sea off the Black Sea in south-eastern Ukraine called?
56256.e: The Sea of Azov is connected to the Black Sea by the Kerch Strait. It is the shallowest sea in the world.
56256.m: The Sea of Azov is an arm of the Black Sea.

56257.q: Which city in western Ukraine is known for its old town on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
56257.e: Lviv, Lemberg in German, has a well-preserved old town with many churches and coffee houses.
56257.m: Lviv in western Ukraine has a famous old town.

56258.q: Which mountain range lies in the west of Ukraine?
56258.e: The Ukrainian Carpathians contain the country’s highest mountain, Hoverla (2061 m).
56258.m: The Carpathians lie in the west of Ukraine.

56259.q: On which great river is Kyiv?
56259.e: The Dnieper flows right through Kyiv. It is one of the longest rivers in Europe and flows into the Black Sea.

56260.q: What is the central square in Kyiv called?
56260.e: Maidan Nezalezhnosti means Independence Square. It has several times been the scene of large rallies.
56260.m: Kyiv’s central square is the Maidan.

56261.q: What was the medieval realm with Kyiv at its centre called?
56261.e: From the 9th century, Kyiv was the centre of Kievan Rus, a large East Slavic realm.
56261.m: Kyiv was the centre of Kievan Rus.

56262.q: Which famous monastery in Kyiv is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
56262.e: The Kyiv Monastery of the Caves was founded in the 11th century. Monks lived there in underground passages and caves.
56262.m: The Kyiv Monastery of the Caves is World Heritage.

56263.q: In roughly which direction does the Dnieper flow?
56263.e: The Dnieper comes from the north and flows south to the sea in a great curve.
56263.m: The Dnieper flows from north to south.

56265.q: Which three countries does the Dnieper flow through?
56265.e: The Dnieper, about 2200 kilometres long, rises west of Moscow in Russia, flows through Belarus and then through the whole of Ukraine.
56265.m: The Dnieper flows through Russia, Belarus and Ukraine.

56266.q: Which city lies near the mouth of the Dnieper?
56266.e: Kherson lies on the lower Dnieper, just before the river opens into the Dnieper-Bug estuary, a wide river mouth.
56266.m: Kherson lies near the mouth of the Dnieper.

56267.q: What is the location of Belarus like?
a: It is landlocked with no sea coast
It lies on the Baltic Sea
It lies on the Black Sea
56267.e: Belarus borders Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Russia and Ukraine, but has no access to the sea.

56268.q: Which large wild animal lives in the Białowieża Forest on the border between Belarus and Poland?
56268.e: The Białowieża Forest is home to the largest free-living herd of European bison in the world. The area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56268.m: European bison live in the Białowieża Forest.

56269.q: Which two languages are official languages in Belarus?
56269.e: In Belarus, Belarusian and Russian are official languages with equal status. In everyday life Russian is often spoken.
56269.m: In Belarus people speak Belarusian and Russian.

56270.q: What is the landscape of Belarus mainly like?
a: Flat with many forests, lakes and marshes
56270.e: Belarus is mostly flat; its highest point is only about 345 metres high. Forests and marshes cover large parts of the country.
56270.m: Belarus is a flat country with many forests.

56271.q: What is the capital of the Republic of Moldova called?
56271.e: Chișinău is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Moldova.
56271.m: The capital of the Republic of Moldova is Chișinău.

56272.q: Between which two countries does the Republic of Moldova lie?
56272.e: The Republic of Moldova borders Romania to the west and Ukraine everywhere else.
56272.m: The Republic of Moldova lies between Romania and Ukraine.

56273.q: Which language is the official language of the Republic of Moldova?
56273.e: The official language is Romanian, which used to be called “Moldovan” there too. Many people also speak Russian.
56273.m: In the Republic of Moldova people speak Romanian.

56274.q: Which neighbouring country lies west of the Republic of Moldova, on the other side of the river Prut?
56274.e: The Prut runs along the whole western border of the Republic of Moldova. Romania lies on the other side.
56274.m: The Prut separates Moldova from Romania.

56275.q: What is the Republic of Moldova especially known for?
a: For wine-growing and huge wine cellars
56275.e: Wine-growing has a long tradition in Moldova. In the Mileștii Mici wine cellar, millions of bottles are stored in underground tunnels.
56275.m: The Republic of Moldova is a wine country.

56276.q: Which inland body of water is part of the usual boundary line between Europe and Asia?
56276.e: The usual boundary runs from the Ural Mountains along the Ural River to the Caspian Sea and from there on towards the Black Sea.
56276.m: The Caspian Sea lies on the boundary between Europe and Asia.

56277.q: Which of these countries has territory in both Europe and Asia?
56277.e: Eastern Thrace with the European part of Istanbul lies in Europe; the larger part of Turkey, Anatolia, lies in Asia.

56278.q: Which Central Asian country has a small part of its territory in Europe, west of the Ural River?
56278.e: The Ural River flows through western Kazakhstan; by the usual boundary, the area west of it counts as Europe.
56278.m: Kazakhstan also has a small European part.

56279.q: Is the larger part of Russia’s territory in Europe or in Asia?
56279.e: About three quarters of Russia’s territory lies east of the Urals in Asia, mainly Siberia; but most people live in the European part.
56279.m: Most of Russia lies in Asia, but most Russians live in Europe.

56280.q: Why are Europe and Asia often considered a single continent called Eurasia?
a: They lie on one shared landmass
56280.e: Europe and Asia are not separated by an ocean but form one connected landmass; the boundary was set by people.
56280.m: Together, Europe and Asia form the landmass of Eurasia.

56281.q: Which mountain range is usually considered the boundary between Europe and Asia?
56281.e: The Ural Mountains run from north to south through Russia. Since the 18th century, geographers have used them as the boundary between Europe and Asia.
56281.m: The Urals separate Europe and Asia.

56282.q: Which river, together with the Ural Mountains, often forms the boundary between Europe and Asia?
56282.e: The Ural River rises in the Ural Mountains and flows into the Caspian Sea. Together they form the usual boundary line.
56282.m: The Ural River is part of the boundary between Europe and Asia.

56283.q: Which mountain range between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea is often taken as the boundary between Europe and Asia?
56283.e: In the south the boundary is not clear. The ridge of the Caucasus is often used, though some put it further north in a lowland.
56283.m: In the south, the Caucasus is often taken as Europe’s boundary.

56284.q: Which sea do the Ural Mountains reach in the north?
56284.e: In the north, the Urals reach as far as the Kara Sea, a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean.
56284.m: The Urals stretch to the Arctic Ocean.

56285.q: About how long are the Ural Mountains from north to south?
56285.e: The Urals stretch for about 2500 kilometres from the Kara Sea to the steppes of Kazakhstan.
56285.m: The Urals are a long, narrow mountain range.

56286.q: In which direction do the Ural Mountains run?
56286.e: The Urals are a long, narrow mountain range. They reach from the Arctic Ocean in the north to the steppes of Kazakhstan in the south.
56286.m: The Urals run from north to south.

56287.q: Which two great plains do the Ural Mountains separate?
a: East European Plain and West Siberian Plain
Po Valley and Great Hungarian Plain
North German Plain and Paris Basin
56287.e: West of the Urals lies the East European Plain, east of them the West Siberian Plain, one of the largest flatlands on Earth.
56287.m: The Urals rise between two huge plains.

56288.q: Which industrial city in the southern Urals is named after a mountain of magnetic iron ore?
56288.e: Magnitogorsk was founded in 1929 next to Mount Magnitnaya, which contained a lot of magnetite, and is still a major steel centre today.
56288.m: Magnitogorsk is a steel city in the southern Urals.

56289.q: Which green, striped ornamental stone is especially typical of the Urals?
56289.e: A lot of malachite was found in the Urals; it was used, for example, to make columns and vases for palaces in St Petersburg.
56289.m: Green malachite is a famous treasure of the Urals.

56290.q: What did Russians once call the Urals because of their shape?
56290.e: The Urals stretch across the land like a long belt; old Russian names therefore call them the stone belt.
56290.m: The Urals lie like a belt of stone between Europe and Asia.

56291.q: In which part of the Urals are the highest peaks?
a: In the north, in the Subpolar Urals
In the south on the border with Kazakhstan
Exactly in the middle near Yekaterinburg
On the islands in the Caspian Sea
56291.e: The highest mountains of the Urals are in the Subpolar Urals; the Middle Urals, by contrast, are so low that roads and railways cross them easily.
56291.m: The Urals are highest in the north and lowest in the middle.

56292.q: Which mountain in the Caucasus is often considered the highest mountain in Europe?
56292.e: Elbrus in the Caucasus is over 5600 metres high. If the Caucasus is counted as part of Europe, it is Europe’s highest mountain.
56292.m: Elbrus in the Caucasus is very high.

56294.q: Which figure from Greek legend was chained to a rock in the Caucasus as a punishment?
56294.e: Prometheus had brought fire to humans; as a punishment Zeus had him chained to a rock in the Caucasus.
56294.m: The legend of Prometheus is set in the Caucasus.

56295.e: A tectonic plate is pushing against Eurasia from the south. This folded up the Caucasus, similar to the Alps.
56295.m: The Caucasus is a young fold mountain range.

56296.q: In which mountain range are Georgia’s highest mountains?
56296.e: The Greater Caucasus forms Georgia’s northern border. Many peaks there rise above 5000 metres.
56296.m: Georgia’s highest mountains are in the Caucasus.

56297.q: How many summits does Elbrus have?
56297.e: Elbrus has a west summit and an east summit, connected by a saddle.

56298.q: Why is Elbrus often called the highest mountain in Europe?
a: Because it lies north of the Caucasus watershed
Because it lies in the Alps
Because it lies on an island
56298.e: If Europe’s boundary is drawn along the main ridge of the Caucasus, Elbrus lies on the European side.
56298.m: Depending on where the boundary is drawn, Elbrus is Europe’s highest mountain.

56299.q: How many metres higher is Elbrus, at 5642 metres, than Mont Blanc, at 4806 metres?
56299.e: You calculate 5642 metres minus 4806 metres, which gives 836 metres.
56299.m: Elbrus is more than 800 metres higher than Mont Blanc.

56300.q: Which famous list of mountains includes Elbrus as Europe’s highest peak?
56300.e: The Seven Summits are the highest mountains of the seven continents; in the best-known list, Elbrus represents Europe.
56300.m: Elbrus is one of the Seven Summits.

56301.q: In which mountain range is Elbrus?
56301.e: Elbrus is an extinct volcano in the Caucasus in Russia. In 1874 a mountain guide from Valais was among those who reached the west summit.

56302.q: In what shape do the Alps stretch across Europe?
a: In a zigzag across the sea
56302.e: The Alps form an arc about 1200 kilometres long, from the Mediterranean coast near Nice to the Vienna Woods.
56302.m: The Alps form an arc from Nice to Vienna.

56303.q: What are the peaks of the Alps that are higher than 4000 metres called?
56303.e: Four-thousanders are mountains over 4000 metres high; most of the four-thousanders of the Alps are in Switzerland.
56303.m: Most of the Alpine four-thousanders are in Switzerland.

56304.q: Which treaty of the Alpine countries has worked to protect the Alps since 1991?
56304.e: The Alpine Convention was signed in 1991 and is meant to protect nature and sustainable development in the Alpine region.
56304.m: The Alpine Convention protects the Alps as a habitat.

56305.q: Which Alpine pass between Innsbruck and Bolzano, at about 1370 metres, is one of the lowest major crossings of the Alps?
56305.e: The Brenner Pass is only about 1370 metres high and is one of the most important transport routes across the Alps.
56305.m: An important route from Austria to Italy runs over the Brenner.

56306.q: The Alps are divided into the Western Alps and the Eastern Alps. Which river roughly forms the boundary?
56306.e: The dividing line runs from Lake Constance up the Rhine valley over the Splügen Pass to Lake Como. The Grisons east of the Rhine therefore belong to the Eastern Alps.
56306.m: The Rhine roughly separates the Western Alps from the Eastern Alps.

56307.q: What is the warm, dry wind that blows down the northern side of the Alps and often brings clear views called?
56307.e: With the föhn, air rises on the southern side of the Alps, loses its moisture as rain and warms up strongly as it descends on the northern side.
56307.m: The föhn is a warm wind blowing down from the Alps.

56308.q: Which is the second longest river in Europe?
56308.e: The Danube is about 2850 kilometres long, making it the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.
56308.m: The Danube is the second longest river in Europe.

56309.q: Which is the longest river in Italy?
56309.e: The Po is about 650 kilometres long, flows through the Po Valley and into the Adriatic.
56309.m: The Po is the longest river in Italy.

56310.q: Which river, together with the Neisse, forms most of the border between Germany and Poland?
56310.e: The Oder rises in the Czech Republic and flows through Poland; on its lower course, together with the Lusatian Neisse, it forms the German-Polish border.
56310.m: The Oder and Neisse separate Germany and Poland.

56311.q: Into which sea does the Volga, the longest river in Europe, flow?
56311.e: The Volga flows through Russia and into the Caspian Sea in a large delta. The Caspian Sea is really a huge lake with no outflow.
56311.m: The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.

56312.q: On which river is the French wine city of Bordeaux?
56312.e: The Garonne rises in the Pyrenees, flows through Toulouse and Bordeaux and into the Gironde.

56313.q: Which river flows through France, Belgium and the Netherlands and is called the Maas in Dutch?
56313.e: The Meuse rises in France, flows through Liège in Belgium and, in the Netherlands, flows into the North Sea together with the Rhine.
56313.m: The Meuse is called the Maas in Dutch.

56314.q: Which canal has connected the river systems of the Rhine and the Danube since 1992?
56314.e: The Main-Danube Canal connects the Main near Bamberg with the Danube near Kelheim, so ships can travel right across Europe.
56314.m: The Main-Danube Canal connects two great river systems of Europe.

56316.q: Which city on the Volga used to be called Stalingrad?
56316.e: The city was called Tsaritsyn until 1925, then Stalingrad until 1961, and has been called Volgograd since then.
56316.m: Volgograd used to be called Stalingrad.

56317.q: About how long is the Volga?
56317.e: The Volga is about 3500 kilometres long, making it the longest river in Europe. Its largest tributary is the Kama.
56317.m: The Volga is about 3500 kilometres long.

56318.q: What do many Russians fondly call their largest river?
56318.e: The Volga is very important to Russia, so in songs and poems it is called “Mother Volga”.
56318.m: In Russia the Volga is also called Mother Volga.

56319.q: What has been built on the Volga to produce electricity?
a: Wind turbines in the middle of the river
56319.e: Several hydroelectric power stations dam the Volga. The Kuybyshev Reservoir is even larger than the canton of Bern.
56319.m: There are huge reservoirs on the Volga.

56320.q: Why is the mouth of the Volga below sea level?
a: The Caspian Sea lies lower than the ocean
The mouth is in a cave
A dam pushes the water down
56320.e: The surface of the Caspian Sea is about 28 metres below the level of the oceans, so the Volga ends below sea level.
56320.m: The Volga flows into the sea below sea level.

56321.q: Which waterway connects the Volga with the Baltic Sea?
56321.e: Through rivers, lakes and canals, the Volga-Baltic Waterway leads from the Volga to St Petersburg on the Baltic Sea.
56321.m: Ships can travel from the Volga to the Baltic Sea.

56322.q: Which two headwaters form the Rhine?
56322.e: The Anterior Rhine and the Posterior Rhine join at Reichenau in the canton of the Grisons to form the Rhine.
56322.m: The Rhine forms in the Grisons from two headwaters.

56324.q: What is the Rhine gorge in the Grisons, formed after a huge landslide near Flims, called?
56324.e: The Ruinaulta formed because the Anterior Rhine cut its way through the debris of the Flims landslide about 9500 years ago.
56324.m: The Ruinaulta is the Grand Canyon of Switzerland.

56325.q: Which river carries more water than the Rhine where they meet in Aargau?
56325.e: At Koblenz in the canton of Aargau, the Aare flows into the Rhine and on average brings more water than the Rhine itself.
56325.m: Where they meet, the Aare carries more water than the Rhine.

56327.q: What is the Middle Rhine Valley between Bingen and Koblenz famous for?
a: For many castles on steep banks
56327.e: In the Upper Middle Rhine Valley many castles stand above vineyards, and there is also the Lorelei rock. Since 2002 the valley has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
56327.m: The Middle Rhine Valley with its castles is World Heritage.

56328.q: Between which two mountain ranges does the Rhine flow north after Basel?
56328.e: From Basel, the Rhine flows north as the Upper Rhine. The Black Forest lies to the east, the Vosges to the west.
56328.m: The Upper Rhine flows between the Black Forest and the Vosges.

56329.q: In which country does the Rhine flow into the sea?
56329.e: In the Netherlands the Rhine splits into several branches, for example the Waal, and flows into the North Sea near Rotterdam.
56329.m: The Rhine flows into the North Sea in the Netherlands.

56330.q: Where does the Danube form from the headwaters Brigach and Breg?
56330.e: The Brigach and Breg join at Donaueschingen to form the Danube.

56331.q: Which city on the Danube has the tallest church tower in the world, on its minster?
56331.e: Ulm Minster stands in Ulm on the Danube; its tower is about 162 metres high.
56331.m: The tallest church tower in the world is in Ulm on the Danube.

56332.q: Why is the Danube Delta protected by UNESCO?
a: Because of its rich wildlife and plant life
56332.e: The Danube Delta is one of the largest wetlands in Europe with many bird species and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991.
56332.m: The Danube Delta is a paradise for birds.

56333.q: In which direction does the Danube mainly flow?
56333.e: The Danube flows roughly eastwards to the Black Sea, unlike most large rivers in Central Europe.
56333.m: The Danube flows from west to east.

56334.q: What happens to the water of the young Danube at the Danube Sinkhole?
a: It seeps away and flows underground to the Rhine
56334.e: Near Immendingen, Danube water seeps into the limestone and comes out again at the Aachtopf spring; from there it flows via Lake Constance to the Rhine.
56334.m: Part of the Danube flows underground to the Rhine.

56335.q: Which valley of the Danube in Lower Austria is known for wine and apricots and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
56335.e: The Wachau between Melk and Krems has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
56335.m: The Wachau is a famous landscape on the Danube.

56336.q: Which city is called the City of Three Rivers because the Inn and the Ilz flow into the Danube there?
56336.e: In Passau, on the border with Austria, the Inn and the Ilz flow into the Danube.
56336.m: Passau lies where three rivers meet.

56337.q: What is Johann Strauss’s famous waltz about the Danube called?
a: The Danube Waltz on the Rhine
56337.e: Johann Strauss wrote the waltz in Vienna in 1867. In Austria it is played at every New Year’s Concert.
56337.m: “The Blue Danube” is the most famous waltz.

56338.q: Which is the largest peninsula in Europe?
56338.e: The Scandinavian Peninsula, with Norway, Sweden and part of Finland, is the largest peninsula in Europe.
56338.m: Scandinavia is the largest peninsula in Europe.

56339.q: Which peninsula in south-eastern Europe includes countries such as Greece, Albania and Bulgaria?
56339.e: The Balkan Peninsula is named after the Balkan Mountains in Bulgaria and lies between the Adriatic, the Aegean and the Black Sea.
56339.m: Greece lies on the Balkan Peninsula.

56340.q: Which peninsula forms the southernmost part of the Greek mainland?
56340.e: The Peloponnese is connected to the rest of the mainland only by a narrow isthmus.
56340.m: The Peloponnese lies in the south of Greece.

56341.q: On which peninsula are Spain and Portugal?
56341.e: The Iberian Peninsula lies in south-western Europe between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. The Pyrenees separate it from France.
56341.m: Spain and Portugal lie on the Iberian Peninsula.

56342.q: On which peninsula is most of Denmark?
56342.e: Jutland juts north from northern Germany between the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. Denmark also has many islands, for example Zealand with Copenhagen.
56342.m: Most of Denmark lies on the Jutland peninsula.

56343.q: Which peninsula in south-west England ends at Land’s End?
56343.e: Cornwall reaches far out into the Atlantic; Land’s End is the westernmost point of England.
56343.m: Cornwall is the peninsula in south-west England.

56344.q: Which peninsula in north-western France juts far out into the Atlantic?
56344.e: Brittany lies between the English Channel and the Atlantic. It is known for its rocky coasts and lighthouses.
56344.m: Brittany is a peninsula in France.

56345.q: About how deep is the North Sea on average?
56345.e: The North Sea is a shallow shelf sea with an average depth of about 95 metres.
56345.m: The North Sea is a shallow sea.

56346.q: Which strait connects the North Sea towards the Baltic Sea?
56346.e: The Skagerrak lies between Norway and Denmark and leads via the Kattegat to the Baltic Sea.
56346.m: The Skagerrak opens the North Sea to the Baltic.

56347.q: Which channel connects the North Sea in the south-west with the Atlantic?
56347.e: The English Channel lies between England and France; its narrowest point is the Strait of Dover.
56347.m: The English Channel separates England from France.

56349.q: What is a particularly high flood on the North Sea coast, caused when strong wind pushes the water against the coast, called?
56349.e: In a storm surge, high tide and a strong north-westerly wind come together; the water then rises far above normal high tide.
56349.m: Storm surges happen when high tide and a storm come together.

56350.q: In which country does a long dam separate the IJsselmeer from the North Sea?
56350.e: The Afsluitdijk, about 32 kilometres long, was completed in 1932. It turned the bay called the Zuiderzee into the lake IJsselmeer.
56350.m: The Afsluitdijk turned a bay into a lake.

56351.q: Which Scottish group of islands lies in the far north between the North Sea and the Atlantic?
56351.e: The Shetland Islands are the northernmost part of Scotland and lie on the boundary between the North Sea and the Atlantic.
56351.m: The Shetland Islands lie in the far north of Great Britain.

56352.q: What effect does the North Atlantic Current have on Norway’s coast?
a: The harbours stay ice-free in winter
56352.e: Thanks to the warm water, many Norwegian harbours stay ice-free in winter despite being so far north.
56352.m: Because of warm Atlantic water, Norway’s harbours hardly freeze.

56353.q: Why does Western Europe often have mild winters and cool summers because of the Atlantic?
a: The sea evens out the temperatures
The Atlantic is always icy cold
56353.e: Water stores heat well; westerly winds bring the balancing sea air inland. This is called a maritime climate.
56353.m: The sea gives Western Europe a balanced climate.

56354.q: Which country in the North Atlantic lies right on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two tectonic plates drift apart?
56354.e: Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. There, the North American and Eurasian plates move about 2 centimetres apart every year.
56354.m: Iceland lies on the boundary between two tectonic plates.

56355.q: Which ship sank in the North Atlantic in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
56355.e: The Titanic sank on its maiden voyage from England to New York, south-east of Newfoundland.
56355.m: In spring, icebergs drift south in the North Atlantic.

56356.q: Which two pressure areas over the North Atlantic strongly influence the weather in Europe?
56356.e: Between the Azores High in the south and the Icelandic Low in the north, westerly winds blow and bring weather from the Atlantic to Europe.
56356.m: The Azores High and the Icelandic Low steer Europe’s weather.

56357.q: After the Pacific, which is the second largest ocean on Earth?
56357.e: The Atlantic covers about a fifth of the Earth’s surface and separates Europe and Africa from the Americas.
56357.m: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.

56358.q: Why is Ireland so green that it is called the Emerald Isle?
56358.e: Moist air from the Atlantic brings a lot of rain, and the mild maritime climate lets grass grow almost all year round.

56359.q: How many countries border the Black Sea?
56359.e: The countries on the Black Sea are Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia.
56359.m: Six countries lie on the Black Sea.

56360.q: What is special about the deep water of the Black Sea?
56360.e: Below about 150 to 200 metres the Black Sea has no oxygen, but there is poisonous hydrogen sulphide; almost only bacteria live there.
56360.m: There is hardly any life in the depths of the Black Sea.

56361.q: Why is the Black Sea less salty than the Mediterranean?
a: Large rivers bring a lot of fresh water
56361.e: Many large rivers bring fresh water; the salt content is about half that of the open sea.
56361.m: Lots of river water makes the Black Sea less salty.

56362.q: About how deep is the Black Sea at its deepest point?
56362.e: The greatest depth of the Black Sea is about 2200 metres.
56362.m: The Black Sea is over 2000 metres deep.

56363.q: Which city is Romania’s most important port on the Black Sea?
56363.e: Constanța is Romania’s largest seaport and one of the largest ports on the Black Sea.
56363.m: Constanța is Romania’s gateway to the sea.

56364.q: Which country in the Caucasus borders the Black Sea?
56364.e: Georgia lies on the eastern shore of the Black Sea. The port and holiday resort of Batumi is on its coast.
56364.m: Georgia lies on the Black Sea.

56365.q: Which strait, running through the middle of Istanbul, connects the Black Sea with the Mediterranean region?
56365.e: In Istanbul the Bosporus separates Europe from Asia. Ships pass through it from the Black Sea towards the Mediterranean.
56365.m: The Bosporus is the gateway to the Black Sea.

56366.q: Which Turkish port city lies on the Black Sea coast in north-eastern Turkey?
56366.e: Trabzon lies on the Black Sea coast; Antalya, Izmir and Bodrum lie on the Mediterranean or the Aegean.
56366.m: Trabzon is a port city on the Black Sea.

56367.q: What are summers typically like in a Mediterranean climate?
56367.e: In summer the Mediterranean region is under the influence of high-pressure areas, so it is hot and it hardly rains.
56367.m: In a Mediterranean climate, summers are hot and dry.

56368.q: In which season does most rain fall in a Mediterranean climate?
a: In the winter half of the year
56368.e: In winter, low-pressure areas move over the Mediterranean and bring most of the rain.
56368.m: By the Mediterranean it rains mainly in winter.

56369.q: Which tree is considered the typical plant of the Mediterranean climate, because it grows almost only there?
56369.e: The olive tree tolerates hot, dry summers but not hard frost; where it grows shows quite exactly the area of Mediterranean climate.
56369.m: Where olives grow, there is a Mediterranean climate.
