56370.q: What is the dense, evergreen scrub in the Mediterranean region called?
56370.e: Maquis consists of evergreen shrubs such as myrtle, broom and rockroses.
56370.m: Maquis is the typical scrubland of the Mediterranean.

56371.q: Why do many Mediterranean plants have small, hard, leathery leaves?
a: So that they lose little water in summer
So that they catch more rain
So that they can carry snow in winter
So that animals can eat them more easily
56371.e: They are called sclerophyllous plants; their tough leaves protect against water loss during the dry summers.
56371.m: Hard-leaved plants save water in the summer heat.

56372.q: Which danger is especially great in the Mediterranean region in summer because of the dryness?
56372.e: Because of the long dry period, plants are parched in summer, and a single spark can start big fires.
56372.m: Dry summers increase the risk of forest fires by the Mediterranean.

56373.q: What is the cold north wind that blows through the Rhône valley to the Mediterranean called?
56373.e: The mistral is a cold, dry wind that blows down through the Rhône valley towards the Gulf of Lion.
56373.m: The mistral blows through the Rhône valley.

56374.q: What is the hot wind that blows from the Sahara across the Mediterranean to southern Europe called?
56374.e: The sirocco brings hot, often dusty air from North Africa; sometimes it even carries Sahara dust as far as Switzerland.
56374.m: The sirocco brings desert air to southern Europe.

56375.q: Why is the exact number of countries in Europe disputed?
a: Because some countries lie only partly in Europe
Because new countries appear every year
Because the UN does not count countries
56375.e: Russia, Turkey, Kazakhstan and Georgia lie only partly in Europe. Depending on how you count, you get about 45 to 50 countries.
56375.m: Because some countries lie on two continents, the number of countries in Europe varies.

56376.q: Which country has the largest total area of all countries with territory in Europe?
56376.e: At over 17 million km², Russia is the largest country on Earth. About a quarter of it lies in Europe.
56376.m: Russia is the largest country in the world by area.

56377.q: Which is the second smallest country in Europe?
56377.e: Monaco is only about 2 km² in size. Only one country in Europe is even smaller.
56377.m: Monaco is the second smallest country in Europe.

56378.q: Which microstate lies entirely within Italy, but not in Rome?
56378.e: San Marino is surrounded by Italy and lies in the hills near Rimini. It is considered one of the oldest republics in the world.
56378.m: San Marino is a small republic in the middle of Italy.

56379.q: Which EU country is the largest by area?
56379.e: With about 550,000 km² in its European part, France is the largest country in the EU, ahead of Spain and Sweden.
56379.m: France is the largest country in the European Union.

56380.q: Which country has the most inhabitants if you count only countries lying entirely in Europe?
56380.e: Germany has over 83 million inhabitants. Russia and Turkey have more, but they lie only partly in Europe.
56380.m: Germany is the most populous country lying entirely in Europe.

56381.q: What form of state is Monaco?
56381.e: Monaco is a principality. At the head of the state is a prince from the Grimaldi family.
56381.m: Monaco is ruled by a prince.

56382.q: Which princely family has ruled Monaco for centuries?
56382.e: The Grimaldi family has ruled Monaco since the Middle Ages. Albert II comes from this family.

56383.q: Which famous motor race takes place every year on the streets of Monaco?
56383.e: Since 1929, racing cars have driven through the narrow streets of Monaco. Today the race is part of Formula 1.
56383.m: At the Monaco Grand Prix, Formula 1 cars race through the city.

56384.q: What is Monaco especially known for compared with all the countries in the world?
56384.e: Almost 40,000 people live on about 2 km². This makes Monaco one of the most densely populated countries on Earth.

56385.q: Which well-known district of Monaco is famous for its casino?
56385.e: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco with the famous casino. Saint-Tropez, Cannes and Menton are in France.
56385.m: The famous casino is in Monte Carlo.

56387.q: What is Andorra especially popular with tourists for?
56387.e: Andorra has large ski areas and low taxes on many goods. That is why many visitors come to ski and shop.
56387.m: Andorra attracts people with ski slopes and cheap shopping.

56388.q: Does Andorra have access to the sea?
a: Yes, to the Bay of Biscay
56388.e: Andorra lies in the middle of the Pyrenees and has no coast. Like Switzerland, it is landlocked.
56388.m: Like Switzerland, Andorra has no sea.

56389.q: Which treaty from 1923 links Liechtenstein closely with Switzerland?
56389.e: With the Customs Treaty of 1923, Switzerland and Liechtenstein form a single customs area. That is why there are no customs checks between the two countries.
56389.m: Since the Customs Treaty of 1923, Liechtenstein and Switzerland form one customs area.

56390.q: What is special about Liechtenstein’s location?
56390.e: Liechtenstein borders only countries without a sea. Apart from Uzbekistan, it is the only doubly landlocked country in the world.

56391.q: What form of state is Liechtenstein?
56391.e: Liechtenstein is a principality with a constitution. The head of state is Prince Hans-Adam II; since 2004 Hereditary Prince Alois has run the affairs of state.

56394.q: Which troop from Switzerland guards the Pope?
56394.e: The Pontifical Swiss Guard protects the Pope. Its guards are Catholic Swiss men.

56395.q: Since which year has the Pontifical Swiss Guard existed?
56395.e: Pope Julius II brought Swiss mercenaries to Rome in 1506. This makes the Guard one of the oldest armies in the world.
56395.m: The Swiss Guard has existed since 1506.

56396.q: Which famous church stands in Vatican City?
56396.e: St Peter’s Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world and stands on St Peter’s Square in Vatican City.
56396.m: St Peter’s Basilica is in the Vatican.

56397.q: In which chapel of the Vatican is a new Pope elected?
56397.e: The cardinals elect the Pope in the conclave in the Sistine Chapel. Its ceiling was painted by Michelangelo.
56397.m: The Pope is elected in the Sistine Chapel.

56398.q: Which city completely surrounds Vatican City?
56398.e: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. It lies in the middle of Rome and has been a separate state since 1929.
56398.m: Vatican City lies in the middle of Rome.

56399.q: After a papal election, which sign shows that a new Pope has been chosen?
56399.e: After each round of voting the ballot papers are burned. White smoke from the chimney means a new Pope has been elected.
56399.m: White smoke announces a new Pope.

56400.q: Which ancient language is still an official language of the Holy See in the Vatican today?
56400.e: Latin is the official language of the Holy See. In everyday life in the Vatican, mainly Italian is spoken.
56400.m: Latin is still an official language in the Vatican.

56401.q: Which three capitals belong to the Baltic states?
56401.e: Estonia’s capital is Tallinn, Latvia’s is Riga and Lithuania’s is Vilnius.
56401.m: The Baltic capitals are Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius.

56402.q: Which capital is the furthest north of all the capitals in Europe?
56402.e: Reykjavík in Iceland lies at about 64 degrees north and is the northernmost capital of an independent country.
56402.m: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of an independent country.

56403.q: Which language family do most of Europe’s languages belong to?
56403.e: Almost all of Europe’s major languages, such as German, French, Russian or Greek, belong to the Indo-European language family.
56403.m: Most of Europe’s languages are Indo-European.

56404.q: Which language group does Italian belong to?
56404.e: Like French and Spanish, Italian comes from Latin and is a Romance language.

56405.q: Which of these languages is a Slavic language?
56405.e: Like Czech and Russian, Polish is a Slavic language. The other three languages belong to other groups.

56406.q: Which language spoken in Spain and France is not related to any other known language?
56406.e: Basque is a language isolate. It is older than the Romance languages around it and not related to any known language.

56407.q: Which language group does Romansh, the fourth national language of Switzerland, belong to?
56407.e: Romansh developed from the Latin that the Romans brought to the Alps. So it is a Romance language.

56408.q: Which of these languages is a Germanic language?
56408.e: Like German, English and Swedish, Dutch is a Germanic language.

56409.q: Which official language of the EU comes from the Semitic language family?
56409.e: Maltese developed from Arabic and is the only Semitic official language of the EU. It is written in Latin letters.

56410.q: Which language group do Irish and Welsh belong to?
56410.e: Irish, Scottish Gaelic, Welsh and Breton are Celtic languages. They are spoken mainly on the western edge of Europe.
56410.m: Irish and Welsh are Celtic languages.

56411.q: Who is the Cyrillic script named after?
56411.e: The script is named after Cyril, the apostle to the Slavs, who with his brother Methodius brought Christianity to the Slavs in the 9th century.
56411.m: The Cyrillic script bears the name of the missionary Cyril.

56412.q: In which script is Russian written?
56412.e: Russian is written with the Cyrillic alphabet, which has 33 letters.

56413.q: Which EU country uses the Cyrillic script as its official script?
56413.e: Bulgaria writes in Cyrillic. Since Bulgaria joined the EU in 2007, Cyrillic has been the EU’s third script alongside Latin and Greek.
56413.m: Bulgaria is the Cyrillic country of the EU.

56414.q: Which language is written in both Cyrillic and Latin letters?
56414.e: Serbian can be written in Cyrillic and in Latin letters. Croatian, Slovene and Czech are written only in Latin letters.
56414.m: Serbian is written in two scripts.

56415.q: From which alphabet were many Cyrillic letters taken?
56415.e: Many Cyrillic letters, such as Г (G) or П (P), come from the Greek alphabet.
56415.m: The Cyrillic script is related to the Greek one.

56416.q: Which sound does the Cyrillic letter “Р” stand for?
56416.e: The Cyrillic “Р” looks like a Latin P, but is pronounced like R.
56416.m: The Cyrillic Р is pronounced like an R.

56417.q: Which of these languages is NOT written in Cyrillic?
56417.e: Polish is a Slavic language, but it is written in Latin letters.
56417.m: Polish is written in Latin letters even though it is Slavic.

56418.q: Which sound does the Cyrillic letter “Н” stand for?
56418.e: The Cyrillic “Н” looks like a Latin H, but is pronounced like N.
56418.m: The Cyrillic Н is pronounced like an N.

56419.q: Which Cyrillic letter is pronounced like the English “sh”?
56419.e: Ш is pronounced like “sh”. Ж sounds like the s in “measure”, Щ like “shch” and Ч like “ch”.
56419.m: The letter Ш sounds like sh.

56420.q: What is the group of EU countries that pay with the euro called?
56420.e: The countries with the euro form the eurozone. Since 2026, 21 countries have belonged to it, the most recent being Bulgaria.
56420.m: The euro countries form the eurozone.

56421.q: Which country joined the eurozone in 2023 as its 20th member?
56421.e: Croatia introduced the euro on 1 January 2023, replacing the kuna.
56421.m: Croatia has paid with the euro since 2023.

56422.q: Which EU country has secured the right by treaty not to have to introduce the euro?
56422.e: Denmark has an exception and keeps the Danish krone. Finland, Ireland and Austria use the euro.
56422.m: Denmark does not have to introduce the euro.

56423.q: Which currency do Sweden, Poland and the Czech Republic have (as of 2025)?
56423.e: Sweden has the krona, Poland the złoty and the Czech Republic the koruna. They are in the EU, but not in the eurozone.
56423.m: Not all EU countries pay with the euro.

56424.q: Which country outside the EU uses the euro without its own agreement with the EU?
56424.e: Montenegro and Kosovo adopted the euro as their currency on their own, without being members of the EU.
56424.m: Montenegro pays with the euro even though it is not in the EU.

56425.q: What is the same on the front of all euro coins?
56425.e: The value side is the same in all countries. Each country designs the other side itself, for example with landmarks.
56425.m: Each euro country designs one side of its coins itself.

56426.q: What is the most important feature of the Schengen Area?
a: No regular checks on people at the internal borders
56426.e: In the Schengen Area, people are normally not checked at the borders between the member states.
56426.m: In the Schengen Area you cross borders without passport checks.

56427.q: What place is the Schengen Agreement named after?
56427.e: The agreement was signed in 1985 in Schengen, a wine-growing village on the Moselle in Luxembourg.
56427.m: Schengen is a small village in Luxembourg.

56428.q: In which year was the first Schengen Agreement signed?
56428.e: Five countries signed the first agreement in Schengen in 1985. Border checks were dropped from 1995.

56429.q: Since when has Switzerland applied the Schengen Agreement?
56429.e: Voters said yes to Schengen in 2005. From December 2008, checks on people at the national borders were lifted.
56429.m: Switzerland has been in the Schengen Area since 2008.

56430.q: Which EU country is NOT part of the Schengen Area (as of 2025)?
56430.e: Ireland has an exception and controls its own borders, partly because of the Common Travel Area with Great Britain.
56430.m: Ireland is in the EU, but not in the Schengen Area.

56431.q: Which countries fully joined the Schengen Area in 2025?
56431.e: Since 1 January 2025, Bulgaria and Romania have been full Schengen members, including at their land borders.
56431.m: Bulgaria and Romania have been fully in Schengen since 2025.

56432.q: Which non-EU country, like Switzerland, is part of the Schengen Area?
56432.e: Besides Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein are also Schengen members without being in the EU.
56432.m: Norway is also in the Schengen Area.

56433.q: How many countries are in the Schengen Area (as of 2025)?
56433.e: The Schengen Area includes 25 EU countries and 4 other countries, 29 countries in total.

56434.q: In which city do the borders of Switzerland, Germany and France meet?
56434.e: At the Three Countries Corner in the Rhine port of Basel, Switzerland, Germany and France meet.
56434.m: The Three Countries Corner is in Basel.

56435.q: Which lake is surrounded by Switzerland, Germany and Austria?
56435.e: Lake Constance has shores in Switzerland, Germany and Austria. The exact border in the lake has never been fixed.

56436.q: What is the German municipality that is completely surrounded by Swiss territory called?
56436.e: Büsingen is a German exclave in the canton of Schaffhausen. People there mostly pay with Swiss francs.
56436.m: Büsingen is a German village in the middle of Switzerland.

56437.q: Which Italian municipality is an exclave in the canton of Ticino?
56437.e: Campione d’Italia lies on Lake Lugano and is completely surrounded by Swiss territory.
56437.m: Campione d’Italia is an Italian village in Ticino.

56438.q: Which neighbouring country almost completely surrounds the canton of Geneva?
56438.e: The canton of Geneva is largely surrounded by France and is connected to the rest of Switzerland only by a narrow strip.
56438.m: Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France.

56439.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbouring countries is NOT a member of the European Union?
56439.e: Liechtenstein is not in the EU, but it is a member of the European Economic Area. The other four neighbours are EU members.
56439.m: Liechtenstein is Switzerland’s only neighbour outside the EU.

56440.q: Which country in Europe is the only grand duchy in the world?
56440.e: Luxembourg is ruled by a grand duke. Today it is the only grand duchy in the world.

56441.q: Which island country in the North Atlantic belongs to Europe and lies close to the Arctic Circle?
56441.e: Iceland lies between Greenland and Norway, just south of the Arctic Circle, and counts as part of Europe.
56441.m: Iceland is a European island country in the North Atlantic.

56442.q: What is the name of the Prince of Monaco (as of 2025)?
56442.e: Albert II has been Prince of Monaco since 2005. He succeeded his father Rainier III.
56442.m: The Prince of Monaco is Albert II.

56443.q: Which famous museum about the sea stands on the Rock of Monaco?
56443.e: The Oceanographic Museum opened in 1910. For a long time the ocean explorer Jacques-Yves Cousteau was its director.
56443.m: Monaco has a large museum of the sea.

56444.q: About how many inhabitants does Andorra have (as of 2024)?
56444.e: About 80,000 people live in Andorra, many of them from Spain, Portugal and France.

56445.q: Is Andorra a member of the European Union?
56445.e: Andorra is not in the EU. But it has signed various agreements with the EU.
56445.m: Andorra is not part of the EU.

56446.q: In which mountain range is Andorra?
56446.e: Andorra lies in the middle of the Pyrenees. The country’s highest mountain, Coma Pedrosa, is about 2940 m high.

56448.q: About how many times larger than Liechtenstein is Andorra?
56448.e: Andorra covers about 468 km², Liechtenstein about 160 km². 468 divided by 160 gives about 3.
56448.m: Andorra is about three times the size of Liechtenstein.

56449.q: What is the name of the Pope who was elected in May 2025?
56449.e: In May 2025 the cardinals elected the American Robert Francis Prevost. He took the name Leo XIV.
56449.m: Since 2025 the Pope has been called Leo XIV.

56450.q: Which language group do Latvian and Lithuanian belong to?
56450.e: Latvian and Lithuanian are the only Baltic languages still spoken today. They belong to the Indo-European family.
56450.m: Latvian and Lithuanian are Baltic languages.

56451.q: How many countries were the first to introduce the euro in 1999?
56451.e: Eleven EU countries started with the euro in 1999, including Germany, France and Italy. Greece followed in 2001.
56451.m: The euro started with eleven countries.

56452.q: Which euro banknote has the highest value?
56452.e: The highest euro banknote is the 500-euro note. It has not been issued since 2019, but it is still valid.
56452.m: The largest euro note is the 500.

56453.q: Which of these countries does NOT belong to the European Economic Area (EEA)?
56453.e: The EEA includes the EU countries plus Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. Switzerland rejected joining in a popular vote in 1992.
56453.m: Switzerland is not in the EEA.

56454.q: Into which two countries was Czechoslovakia peacefully divided in 1993?
56454.e: On 1 January 1993, the Czech Republic and Slovakia were formed from Czechoslovakia, without a war.
56454.m: In 1993 Czechoslovakia became the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

56455.q: Which capital is built on 14 islands?
56455.e: Stockholm lies where Lake Mälaren flows into the Baltic Sea and stretches over 14 islands.
56455.m: Stockholm is built on many islands.

56456.q: Which capital of an EU country has been divided by a ceasefire line since 1974?
56456.e: Since 1974 Nicosia, the capital of Cyprus, has been divided into a Greek Cypriot and a Turkish Cypriot part.
56456.m: Nicosia in Cyprus is a divided capital.

56457.q: In which capital does the European Commission have its seat?
56457.e: The European Commission sits in Brussels, the capital of Belgium. The European Parliament also meets in Strasbourg.
56457.m: The EU Commission sits in Brussels.

56458.q: Which capital lies on the river Vltava?
56458.e: Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic, lies on the Vltava. The famous Charles Bridge crosses this river.

56459.q: Which two capitals on the Danube are only about 60 km apart?
56459.e: Vienna and Bratislava are the two capitals in Europe that are closest to each other. Both lie on the Danube.
56459.m: Vienna and Bratislava lie very close together on the Danube.

56460.q: Which capital also has the Swedish name Helsingfors as well as its Finnish name?
56460.e: In Finland, Finnish and Swedish are official languages. That is why Helsinki also has the Swedish name Helsingfors.
56460.m: In Swedish, Helsinki is called Helsingfors.

56461.q: Which capital lies highest of all the capitals in the EU?
56461.e: Madrid lies at about 650 m above sea level on the Spanish plateau and is the highest capital in the EU.
56461.m: Madrid is the highest capital in the EU.

56462.q: About how many guards does the Pontifical Swiss Guard have today?
56462.e: The Guard was enlarged to 135 men in 2018. This makes it one of the smallest armies in the world.
56462.m: The Swiss Guard has about 135 guards.

56463.q: Which country has the most inhabitants in the European Union (as of 2024)?
56463.e: Germany has about 83 million inhabitants, making it the most populous country in the EU. France follows with about 68 million.
56463.m: Germany is the most populous country in the EU.

56464.q: Which country with territory in Europe has the most inhabitants in total (as of 2024)?
56464.e: Russia has about 146 million inhabitants, most of whom live in the European part west of the Urals. No other country with territory in Europe has so many people.
56464.m: Russia has more inhabitants than any other country with territory in Europe.

56465.q: Which country in Europe has the fewest inhabitants?
56465.e: Only a few hundred people live in the Vatican in Rome. It is also the smallest country in the world by area.
56465.m: The Vatican is the smallest country in Europe.

56466.q: Which country in Europe has the highest population density?
56466.e: In the city-state of Monaco about 38,000 people live on about 2 square kilometres. That makes almost 20,000 inhabitants per square kilometre.
56466.m: Monaco is the most densely populated country in Europe.

56467.q: Which EU member country has the highest population density?
56467.e: The island republic of Malta has over 1,600 inhabitants per square kilometre. That is more than in any other EU country.
56467.m: Malta is the most densely populated country in the EU.

56468.q: About how many inhabitants does Switzerland have (as of 2024)?
56468.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, about 9 million people lived in Switzerland at the end of 2024. The population is growing mainly through immigration.
56468.m: About 9 million people live in Switzerland.

56469.q: Which country has the lowest population density in Europe?
56469.e: In Iceland there are only about 4 inhabitants per square kilometre. Much of the island consists of glaciers, lava fields and highlands.
56469.m: Iceland is the most thinly populated country in Europe.

56470.q: About how many people live in the European Union (as of 2024)?
56470.e: Together, the 27 EU member states have about 450 million inhabitants. That is about six out of ten people in Europe.
56470.m: About 450 million people live in the EU.

56471.q: Which city is the largest city lying entirely in Europe?
56471.e: Moscow has about 13 million inhabitants. Istanbul is larger, but it lies partly in Asia.
56471.m: Moscow is the largest city lying entirely in Europe.

56472.q: Which city has the most inhabitants within its city limits in the European Union?
56472.e: Berlin has almost 4 million inhabitants, making it the largest city in the EU. Within its tight city limits, Paris has only about 2 million.
56472.m: Berlin is the most populous city in the EU.

56473.q: Which capital of an EU country has the fewest inhabitants?
56473.e: Malta’s capital Valletta has only about 5,000 to 6,000 inhabitants. It was built as a fortress city in the 16th century.
56473.m: Valletta is the smallest capital in the EU.

56474.q: Which is the most populous city in Scandinavia?
56474.e: The Swedish capital Stockholm has almost a million inhabitants. It is built on 14 islands.
56474.m: Stockholm is the largest city in Scandinavia.

56475.q: Why does the city of Paris have only about 2 million inhabitants, although more than 12 million people live in the greater area?
a: The city boundary is drawn very tightly
56475.e: The municipality of Paris covers only about 105 square kilometres. Most people in the metropolitan region live in suburbs outside this boundary.
56475.m: The city of Paris is small, but its greater area is huge.

56476.q: Which is the most populous city in Switzerland?
56476.e: Zurich has over 440,000 inhabitants, making it the largest Swiss city. But it is not the capital of Switzerland.
56476.m: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland.

56477.q: Which is the largest city in Italy?
56477.e: Rome has almost 3 million inhabitants. Milan is the second largest city and the economic centre of Italy.
56477.m: Rome is the largest city in Italy.

56478.q: Which city is the second largest in Switzerland by population?
56478.e: Geneva has about 200,000 inhabitants. Basel follows in third place.
56478.m: Geneva is the second largest city in Switzerland.

56479.q: In geography, what is called the “Blue Banana”?
a: A type of banana from Spain
A railway line from Paris to Rome
56479.e: The Blue Banana is a curved belt with many cities, industry and transport. A large share of Europe’s people live and work here.
56479.m: The Blue Banana is Europe’s strongest economic region.

56480.q: Between which regions does the Blue Banana stretch?
56480.e: The economic region reaches from Manchester and London via the Benelux countries and the Rhine area to Milan. On the map it looks like an arc.
56480.m: The Blue Banana reaches from England to northern Italy.

56481.q: Which capital lies in the Blue Banana?
56481.e: The Blue Banana reaches from England via the Benelux countries and the Rhine area to northern Italy. Brussels lies right in the middle.
56481.m: Brussels lies in the Blue Banana.

56482.q: Which river forms an important transport route in the Blue Banana?
56482.e: Many industrial areas and cities lie along the Rhine, such as Basel, Cologne and the Ruhr. The Rhine is one of the busiest waterways in the world.
56482.m: The Rhine is the lifeline of the Blue Banana.

56483.q: Which Swiss city with an important Rhine port lies in the Blue Banana?
56483.e: Basel lies on the Rhine and has the Swiss Rhine Ports. From here ships can travel all the way to the North Sea.
56483.m: Basel is Switzerland’s gateway to the Rhine.

56484.q: Where does the “Blue Banana” get its name from?
a: From its curved shape on the map
From banana imports in the ports
56484.e: On the map the economic region forms a curved strip. The blue colour probably recalls the European flag.
56484.m: The Blue Banana is named after its shape on the map.

56485.q: Which Italian economic metropolis lies at the southern end of the Blue Banana?
56485.e: Milan is the industrial and financial centre of northern Italy. The Blue Banana ends in the south with the area around Milan.
56485.m: Milan forms the southern end of the Blue Banana.

56486.q: Which German industrial region lies in the Blue Banana?
56486.e: The Ruhr is one of the largest urban areas in Europe and lies close to the Rhine. In the past, coal and steel shaped the region.
56486.m: The Ruhr is part of the Blue Banana.

56487.q: Which is the largest seaport in Europe?
56487.e: More than 400 million tonnes of goods are handled in the port of Rotterdam every year. No other port in Europe reaches this amount.
56487.m: Rotterdam is the largest port in Europe.

56488.q: At the mouth of which rivers does the port of Rotterdam lie?
56488.e: Rotterdam lies in the shared delta of the Rhine and the Meuse. This connects ships directly with the inland regions.
56488.m: Rotterdam lies at the mouth of the Rhine and the Meuse.

56489.q: How did the port of Rotterdam gain new land for port facilities?
a: It pumped sand into the sea
56489.e: For the Maasvlakte 2 area, sand was pumped into the North Sea. This created new land where the largest container ships dock.
56489.m: Rotterdam built up port land in the sea.

56490.q: Why is the port of Rotterdam important for Switzerland?
a: Goods reach Basel by Rhine ship
Trains from there go only to Switzerland
56490.e: Rhine ships bring goods such as containers and fuel from Rotterdam to the Rhine ports of Basel. This gives Switzerland access to the sea.
56490.m: Switzerland is linked to Rotterdam via the Rhine.

56491.q: Rotterdam was the largest port in the world until 2004. On which continent are the ports that have overtaken it since then?
56491.e: Ports such as Shanghai and Singapore grew strongly through world trade. But Rotterdam is still the largest port in Europe.
56491.m: Today the largest ports in the world are in Asia.

56492.q: Which goods are handled in particularly large amounts at the port of Rotterdam and processed in refineries?
56492.e: Rotterdam is a centre of the oil industry with several refineries. Crude oil is one of the port’s most important goods.
56492.m: A great deal of oil is handled in Rotterdam.

56493.q: Which Belgian port is the second largest seaport in Europe after Rotterdam?
56493.e: The port of Antwerp lies on the Scheldt and has been merged with Bruges since 2022. It is the second largest port in Europe.
56493.m: Antwerp is the second largest port in Europe.

56494.q: Into which sea do ships sail from the port of Rotterdam?
56494.e: A dug waterway, the Nieuwe Waterweg, connects Rotterdam directly with the North Sea.
56494.m: Rotterdam is connected to the North Sea.

56495.q: What is France’s high-speed train called?
56495.e: TGV stands for “train à grande vitesse”, meaning high-speed train. In regular service it travels at up to 320 km/h.
56495.m: The TGV is France’s fast train.

56496.q: Which train holds the speed record for wheeled trains on rails?
56496.e: On 3 April 2007 a modified TGV reached 574.8 km/h. This is still the record for wheel-on-rail trains.
56496.m: At almost 575 km/h, the TGV holds the rail record.

56497.q: What are Deutsche Bahn’s high-speed trains called?
56497.e: ICE stands for Intercity-Express. On new lines the trains travel at up to 300 km/h, and they also come to Basel and Zurich.
56497.m: The ICE is Germany’s fast train.

56498.q: Which country in Europe has the longest network of high-speed lines?
56498.e: Since 1992 Spain has built a very large network totalling almost 4,000 kilometres. The lines connect Madrid with many large cities in the country.
56498.m: Spain has the longest high-speed network in Europe.

56499.q: Through which tunnel does the Eurostar travel from London to Paris?
56499.e: The Channel Tunnel is about 50 kilometres long and runs under the English Channel. It connects England with France.
56499.m: The Eurostar travels through the Channel Tunnel.

56500.q: Roughly what is the top speed of high-speed trains such as the TGV or ICE?
56500.e: On new high-speed lines, the TGV and ICE travel at up to about 300 km/h in everyday service, the TGV even up to 320 km/h.
56500.m: Fast trains travel at up to about 300 km/h.

56501.q: Which Italian high-speed train has a name meaning “red arrow”?
56501.e: “Freccia” means arrow and “rossa” means red. The Frecciarossa travels at up to 300 km/h between Italy’s large cities.
56501.m: The Frecciarossa is Italy’s red arrow.

56502.q: Which cities did the first TGV line connect from 1981?
56502.e: The Paris-Lyon line was the first high-speed line in Europe. It greatly reduced the journey time.
56502.m: The first TGV ran from Paris to Lyon.

56503.q: What is the high-speed train that connects Switzerland directly with Paris called?
56503.e: TGV Lyria runs from Zurich, Basel, Geneva and Lausanne, among others, to Paris. From Basel the journey takes only about three hours.
56503.m: You can travel from Switzerland to Paris with the TGV Lyria.

56504.q: About how long is the Gotthard Road Tunnel, opened in 1980?
56504.e: The Gotthard Road Tunnel is 16.9 kilometres long and connects Göschenen with Airolo. A second tube has been under construction since 2021.
56504.m: The Gotthard Road Tunnel is about 17 kilometres long.

56505.q: In which year was the first Gotthard railway tunnel opened?
56505.e: The summit tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo, about 15 kilometres long, opened in 1882. More than 190 workers died during its construction.
56505.m: The Gotthard railway has run through the mountain since 1882.

56506.q: Which NRLA tunnel was the first to open, in 2007?
56506.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 35 kilometres long. It connects the Bernese Oberland with Valais.
56506.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel went into service in 2007 as the first NRLA tunnel.

56507.q: Which base tunnel in Ticino completed the flat railway route through the Alps in 2020?
56507.e: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long and lies between Bellinzona and Lugano. With it, the Gotthard route is flat all the way through.
56507.m: The Ceneri Base Tunnel opened in 2020.

56508.q: What does the Alpine Initiative, accepted in 1994, call for?
a: Moving freight from road to rail
A ban on all lorries in Switzerland
56508.e: The people accepted the Alpine Initiative in 1994. Freight through the Alps should travel by train rather than by lorry wherever possible.
56508.m: The Alpine Initiative wants to move goods onto the railway.

56509.q: What is the charge that lorries in Switzerland pay according to distance and weight called?
56509.e: The distance-related heavy vehicle fee (HVF) has existed since 2001. Part of the money was used to build the NRLA.
56509.m: The heavy vehicle fee makes lorry journeys more expensive and supports the railway.

56510.q: Which Alpine pass between Austria and Italy is one of the busiest in the Alps?
56510.e: Millions of lorries cross the Brenner every year. A base tunnel for the railway is being built underneath it.
56510.m: The Brenner is Austria’s most important Alpine crossing.

56511.q: What is the transport of whole lorries on goods trains through the Alps called?
56511.e: On the rolling motorway, lorries travel on low-floor railway wagons. The drivers travel along in a separate carriage.
56511.m: On the rolling motorway, lorries travel by train.

56512.q: Which country in the European Union produces the farm products with the greatest value?
56512.e: France has a lot of fertile land and a favourable climate. It produces especially large amounts of grain, milk, meat and wine.
56512.m: France is the largest farming country in the EU.

56513.q: Which small European country is one of the largest exporters of farm products in the world?
56513.e: The Netherlands export a great deal of vegetables, flowers, dairy products and meat. Modern greenhouses make high yields possible.
56513.m: Despite its small size, the Netherlands is a farming giant.

56514.q: Which country is often called the “breadbasket of Europe” because of its fertile black earth soils?
56514.e: Ukraine has wide areas of very fertile black earth. The country exports a lot of wheat, maize and sunflower oil.
56514.m: Ukraine is the breadbasket of Europe.

56515.q: Which country is the largest producer of olive oil in the world?
56515.e: Huge olive groves grow especially in Andalusia. In normal harvest years almost half of the world’s olive oil comes from Spain.
56515.m: Spain produces the most olive oil.

56516.q: What is grown in the “sea of plastic” in southern Spain?
56516.e: In the province of Almería there are huge greenhouses made of plastic sheeting. In winter a lot of vegetables come from there to the rest of Europe.
56516.m: Vegetables for Europe grow in the sea of plastic.

56517.q: What is land in the Netherlands that has been reclaimed from the sea and enclosed by dykes called?
56517.e: Polders often lie below sea level and are protected by dykes. Pumps keep the land dry so that it can be used as fields or pasture.
56517.m: A polder is land reclaimed from the sea.

56518.q: What is the shared policy with which the EU has supported its farming since 1962 called?
56518.e: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) pays subsidies to farmers and regulates the farm market. It is one of the largest items in the EU budget.
56518.m: With the Common Agricultural Policy, the EU supports its farmers.

56519.q: Which type of farming is most common in the Swiss mountain areas?
56519.e: In the mountains, meadows and pastures are better suited than fields. In summer the cows often graze on the alpine pastures.
56519.m: In the Swiss mountains, farmers mainly keep cows.

56520.q: Which French region does real champagne come from?
56520.e: Only sparkling wine from the Champagne region in north-eastern France may be called champagne. The name is protected.

56521.q: In which country is the Rioja wine region?
56521.e: Rioja lies in northern Spain on the river Ebro. It is known for red wines made from the Tempranillo grape.
56521.m: Rioja is a famous wine region in Spain.

56522.q: Which wine comes from the Douro Valley in Portugal?
56522.e: Port is made in the Douro Valley. It gets its name from the city of Porto, from where it was shipped.
56522.m: Port comes from the Douro Valley.

56523.q: Which wine region on Lake Geneva has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007?
56523.e: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux lie between Lausanne and Montreux. They were built on the steep slopes over centuries.
56523.m: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56524.q: Which canton has the largest vineyard area in Switzerland?
56524.e: About a third of Switzerland’s vineyard area is in Valais. The sunny, dry climate is ideal for it.
56524.m: Valais is the largest wine canton in Switzerland.

56525.q: What is the harvest of grapes in autumn called?
56525.e: During the grape harvest, the ripe grapes are cut from the vines. In Swiss German it is also called “Wümmet”.
56525.m: Picking the grapes is called the grape harvest.

56526.q: In which country is the famous Tokaj wine region?
56526.e: Tokaj lies in north-eastern Hungary. The sweet Tokaji wines are well known.
56526.m: Tokaji is a wine from Hungary.

56527.q: Along which German river do vines grow on particularly steep slopes?
56527.e: Wine has been grown on the steep slate slopes of the Moselle since Roman times.
56527.m: Vines grow on steep slopes along the Moselle.

56528.q: Which country invests its income from North Sea oil in the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world?
56528.e: Norway saves its oil income in a state fund for future generations. The fund owns shares in thousands of companies around the world.
56528.m: Norway saves its oil money in a huge state fund.

56529.q: From where is oil extracted in the North Sea?
56529.e: The oil lies deep under the seabed. Large drilling rigs, also called oil platforms, have been bringing it up since the end of the 1960s.
56529.m: North Sea oil is extracted with drilling rigs.

56531.q: In which country is the oil city of Aberdeen?
56531.e: Aberdeen lies on the North Sea coast of Scotland. From there the oil platforms are supplied by helicopters and ships.

56532.q: In which country is the oil city of Stavanger?
56532.e: Stavanger lies on the west coast of Norway. Many oil companies are based there, and there is even an oil museum.

56533.q: What happened on the Piper Alpha oil platform in the North Sea in 1988?
a: An explosion with a huge fire
56533.e: On Piper Alpha off Scotland, gas exploded and a huge fire broke out. 167 people died. Afterwards the safety rules were made stricter.
56533.m: The Piper Alpha disaster led to stricter safety rules.

56534.q: What did the disused oil storage buoy “Brent Spar” become known for in 1995?
a: Protests prevented it being sunk in the sea
It was the first wooden oil tanker
It brought oil all the way to Switzerland
It was the largest drilling rig in the world
56534.e: The company wanted to sink the disused facility in the Atlantic. After protests by Greenpeace and many customers, it was taken apart on land.
56534.m: After protests, Brent Spar was disposed of on land.

56535.q: Why has oil production in the British part of the North Sea been falling since about 2000?
a: The North Sea has become too deep
56535.e: British production reached its peak in 1999. Since then many oil fields have been largely used up.
56535.m: The North Sea oil fields are slowly running out.

56536.q: Which country built the world’s first offshore wind farm in 1991?
56536.e: The Vindeby wind farm with eleven turbines was built off the Danish coast in 1991. It was in operation until 2017.
56536.m: The first wind farm at sea was in Denmark.

56537.q: What is an offshore wind farm?
a: Wind turbines in the sea off the coast
56537.e: “Offshore” means “off the coast”. The wind turbines stand on foundations in the seabed.
56537.m: An offshore wind farm stands in the sea.

56538.q: Why is the North Sea particularly suitable for wind farms?
a: The wind is strong and the sea is shallow
56538.e: Over the sea the wind blows more strongly and steadily than on land. Because the North Sea is shallow in many places, foundations are easy to build.
56538.m: In the North Sea a lot of wind blows over shallow water.

56539.q: What are the wind turbines in an offshore wind farm for?
56539.e: The wind turns the rotors, and a generator in the turbine turns this into electricity. Germany’s first wind farm at sea, alpha ventus, went into operation in 2010.
56539.m: Wind turbines turn wind into electricity.

56540.q: Which country has the largest offshore wind power capacity in Europe (as of 2024)?
56540.e: Some of the largest wind farms in the world, such as Hornsea, stand off the British coast. Germany follows in second place.
56540.m: Great Britain has the most wind power at sea.

56541.q: On which sandbank in the North Sea is a wind farm being built that is set to become the largest in the world?
56541.e: Dogger Bank lies about 130 kilometres off the English coast and is only 15 to 36 metres deep there. The Dogger Bank wind farm is being built in several stages.
56541.m: A huge wind farm is being built on Dogger Bank.

56542.q: How does the electricity from offshore wind farms get to land?
a: Through undersea cables on the seabed
56542.e: The wind turbines are connected to a substation platform. From there, undersea cables carry the electricity to the grid on land.
56542.m: Wind power comes ashore through undersea cables.

56543.q: In which country is the port city of Esbjerg, a centre of wind power?
56543.e: Esbjerg lies on Denmark’s North Sea coast. Many wind turbines for wind farms at sea are shipped from there.
56543.m: Esbjerg is a centre of wind power in Denmark.

56544.q: Which country is the most visited tourist destination in the world?
56544.e: France welcomes about 100 million foreign visitors every year. Paris, the Côte d’Azur and the Alps are popular.
56544.m: France is the most popular tourist destination in the world.

56545.q: Which museum is the most visited art museum in the world?
56545.e: The Louvre in Paris has almost 9 million visitors a year. The Mona Lisa hangs there too.
56545.m: The Louvre in Paris is the most visited museum in the world.

56546.q: Which city has charged day visitors an entry fee on certain days since 2024?
56546.e: Venice is visited by a huge number of day tourists. The fee is meant to manage the crowds and protect the old town.
56546.m: Venice charges day visitors an entry fee.

a: Too many tourists put a strain on a place
56547.e: With overtourism, residents, nature and sights suffer from the crowds. Examples are Venice, Barcelona or Hallstatt.
56547.m: Overtourism means too many tourists overload a place.

56548.q: After France, which country is the second most popular tourist destination in the world?
56548.e: Spain welcomed about 94 million foreign visitors in 2024. The Mediterranean beaches and the islands are especially popular.
56548.m: Spain is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the world.

56549.q: Where is the highest railway station in Europe?
56549.e: Jungfraujoch station lies at 3454 metres above sea level. It is marketed as the “Top of Europe” and attracts visitors from all over the world.
56549.m: Jungfraujoch station is the highest in Europe.

56550.q: Which holiday resort at the foot of the Matterhorn is car-free?
56550.e: In Zermatt, normal cars with combustion engines are not allowed. Visitors arrive by train and get around the village in electric vehicles.
56550.m: Zermatt is a car-free holiday resort.

56551.q: What is the rocky coast between Barcelona and the French border, a popular holiday area, called?
56551.e: Costa Brava means “wild coast”. It lies in Catalonia and is known for its coves.
56551.m: The Costa Brava lies in north-eastern Spain.

56552.q: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
56552.e: Antoni Gaudí worked on the church for over 40 years. It is still not finished and is one of the most visited sights in Spain.
56552.m: The Sagrada Família is a work by Gaudí.

56553.q: In which country is the tidal power station on the Rance, opened in 1966?
56553.e: The power station lies in Brittany near Saint-Malo. Until 2011 it was the largest tidal power station in the world.
56553.m: The tidal power station on the Rance is in France.

56554.q: What does a tidal power station use to produce electricity?
a: Ebb and flow of the tides
56554.e: At high tide water flows into a bay, at low tide it flows out again. As it does so, it drives turbines.
56554.m: A tidal power station uses the rise and fall of the tides.

56555.q: What mainly causes the tides, the rise and fall of the sea?
56555.e: The Moon pulls on the water of the oceans and so creates tidal bulges. The Sun also plays a part, but more weakly.
56555.m: The Moon is the main reason for the tides.

56556.q: Why was the tidal power station on the Rance built in Brittany of all places?
a: The tidal range there is very large
The sea is especially warm there
France’s longest river flows into the sea there
56556.e: In the Rance estuary the difference between low and high tide can be more than 12 metres. The larger this tidal range, the more electricity can be produced.
56556.m: Tidal power stations need a large tidal range.

56557.q: Which European country produces about 90 per cent of its electricity from hydropower?
56557.e: Norway has many mountains, lakes and a lot of rain and snow. That is why almost all its electricity comes from hydroelectric power stations.
56557.m: Norway produces almost all its electricity from hydropower.

56558.q: What is the highest gravity dam in the world, in the canton of Valais, called?
56558.e: The Grande Dixence dam is 285 metres high. It holds back the Lac des Dix in the Val d’Hérémence.
56558.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

56559.q: On which river is the large Iron Gate hydroelectric power station between Serbia and Romania?
56559.e: At the Iron Gate the Danube breaks through the Carpathians. Two large power stations dam the river there.
56559.m: The Iron Gate power station lies on the Danube.

56560.q: In which year did Geneva become part of the Swiss Confederation?
56560.e: After French rule ended, Geneva joined the Confederation as a canton in 1815. The Congress of Vienna confirmed this step.
56560.m: Geneva has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

56561.q: Which reformer worked in Geneva in the 16th century?
56561.e: John Calvin made Geneva a centre of the Reformation. That is why the city was also called the “Protestant Rome”.
56561.m: Calvin shaped the Reformation in Geneva.

56562.q: Who is shown on the big Reformation Wall in Geneva?
56562.e: The Reformation monument in the Parc des Bastions shows large statues of reformers, including John Calvin.
56562.m: The Reformation Wall in Geneva shows the reformers.

56563.q: What is the cathedral in Geneva's old town called?
56563.e: A famous reformer preached in St Pierre Cathedral in the 16th century. From the north tower you can see over the whole city.

56564.q: Which United Nations organisation for health has its headquarters in Geneva?
56564.e: The World Health Organization (WHO) was founded in 1948. It deals with health issues all over the world, for example vaccination programmes.
56564.m: The WHO has its headquarters in Geneva.

56565.q: Which famous philosopher was born in Geneva in 1712?
56565.e: Rousseau wrote important works about education and the state. There is a statue of him on Rousseau Island in Geneva.

56566.q: Which international agreements to protect the wounded and prisoners in war are named after Geneva?
56566.e: The first Geneva Convention was signed in Geneva in 1864. Today almost every country in the world has accepted the agreements of 1949.
56566.m: The Geneva Conventions protect people in war.

56567.q: Which canton ruled Vaud as a subject territory until 1798?
56567.e: Bern conquered Vaud in 1536 and ruled it for over 250 years through bailiffs. Only in 1798 did Vaud free itself.
56567.m: For a long time Vaud was a subject territory of Bern.

56568.q: In which town in Vaud does the Fête des Vignerons take place?
56568.e: The great winegrowers' festival only takes place about every 20 to 25 years, most recently in 2019. It is a UNESCO living cultural heritage.
56568.m: The Fête des Vignerons is celebrated in Vevey.

56569.q: Which canton in western Switzerland has the most inhabitants?
56569.e: Vaud has over 800,000 inhabitants and, after Zurich and Bern, is the third-largest canton by population (as of 2024).
56569.m: Vaud is the most populous canton in French-speaking Switzerland.

56570.q: Which man from Vaud was executed in 1723 because he wanted to free Vaud from Bernese rule?
56570.e: Jean Daniel Abraham Davel marched to Lausanne with soldiers in 1723, but found no support. Today he is seen as a folk hero of Vaud.
56570.m: Major Davel is a hero of Vaud.

56571.q: Which European football association has its headquarters in Nyon?
56571.e: UEFA is Europe's football association and organises, for example, the Champions League and the European Championship. Its headquarters are on Lake Geneva in Nyon.
56571.m: UEFA has its headquarters in Nyon.

56572.q: What is the big open-air festival that takes place near Nyon every summer called?
56572.e: The Paléo Festival has been held since 1976 and is one of the biggest open-air festivals in Switzerland. It lasts six days.
56572.m: The Paléo Festival takes place near Nyon.

56573.q: Which famous film comedian spent the last 25 years of his life near Vevey?
56573.e: He lived from early 1953 until his death in 1977 at the Manoir de Ban in Corsier-sur-Vevey. Today there is a museum there about his life and his films.
56573.m: Charlie Chaplin lived on Lake Geneva near Vevey.

56574.q: Which flower festival takes place every spring in Morges on Lake Geneva?
56574.e: In the Parc de l'Indépendance over 100,000 tulips bloom in April and May. The festival is called the Fête de la Tulipe.
56574.m: Every spring Morges celebrates the tulip festival.

56575.q: What is the Gothic cathedral of Lausanne called?
56575.e: Notre-Dame Cathedral was consecrated in the 13th century. It is seen as one of the most beautiful Gothic buildings in Switzerland.

56576.q: Which big international sports organisation has its headquarters in Lausanne?
56576.e: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is based in Lausanne. That is why Lausanne calls itself the Olympic Capital. FIFA is based in Zurich, UEFA in Nyon.

56577.q: Which form of transport is found in Switzerland only in Lausanne?
56577.e: Lausanne is the only Swiss city with a metro. Line M2 climbs over 300 metres from the lake to the upper town.
56577.m: Lausanne has the only metro in Switzerland.

56578.q: Who founded a settlement on the lakeshore of today's Lausanne about 2000 years ago?
56578.e: The Romans called their settlement Lousonna. It was near today's district of Vidy, where you can still see ruins and a museum.
56578.m: The Romans already settled in Lausanne.

56579.q: Which Olympic Games took place in Lausanne in January 2020?
56579.e: Young athletes aged 15 to 18 took part in these Games. Some events also took place elsewhere in Vaud, in Valais, in the Grisons and in France.
56579.m: Lausanne hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games in 2020.

56580.q: On which lake does the city of Lausanne lie?
56580.e: Lausanne lies on the northern shore of Lake Geneva, which is called Lac Léman in French. The city climbs steeply up the slope from the shore.

56581.q: What was found at La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel?
a: Weapons and tools of the Celts
56581.e: Many Celtic swords, jewellery and tools came to light at La Tène. A period of the Iron Age is named after the site.
56581.m: Many Celtic objects were found at La Tène.

56582.q: What is the big waterfall on the Doubs near Les Brenets called?
56582.e: There the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. The waterfall lies on the border with France.
56582.m: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the border with France.

56583.q: On which day does the canton of Neuchâtel celebrate the founding of its republic every year?
56583.e: On 1 March 1848 republicans marched to Neuchâtel and removed the royal government. This day is a public holiday in the canton.
56583.m: 1 March is the holiday of the Republic of Neuchâtel.

56584.q: Which big museum about timekeeping is in La Chaux-de-Fonds?
56584.e: The Musée international d'horlogerie shows thousands of clocks, watches and instruments from many centuries. Part of it is underground.
56584.m: There is a big watch and clock museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

56585.q: In which building do the government and parliament of the canton of Neuchâtel meet?
a: In the town hall of Le Locle
56585.e: The castle stands on a hill above the old town, right next to the Collegiate Church. It has been the seat of the cantonal authorities for centuries.
56585.m: The Neuchâtel government works in the castle.

56586.q: Which raw material was mined in the Val-de-Travers until 1986?
56586.e: In the La Presta mines, rock containing asphalt was dug out for road surfaces. Today you can visit the tunnels.
56586.m: Asphalt used to be mined in the Val-de-Travers.

56587.q: What special thing can you see at the Col-des-Roches in Le Locle?
56587.e: The underground mills used the power of a stream that disappears into a cave. They have been restored and are now a museum.
56587.m: In Le Locle mills used to turn underground.

56588.q: What is the region around Porrentruy in the north of the canton of Jura called?
56588.e: The Ajoie sticks out into France like a nose. Its main town is Porrentruy (Pruntrut in German).
56588.m: The Ajoie is the northernmost region of the Jura.

56589.q: Which canton did the Jura separate from when it became a canton of its own in 1979?
56589.e: The northern Jura belonged to the canton of Bern until 1978. After several popular votes it became a canton of its own in 1979.
56589.m: The canton of Jura used to be part of the canton of Bern.

56591.q: What was discovered when the A16 motorway was built near Porrentruy?
56591.e: During construction thousands of dinosaur footprints from the Jurassic came to light. Today they are on show in the Jurassica museum.
56591.m: Thousands of dinosaur tracks were found near Porrentruy.

56593.q: What is the A16 motorway, which runs through the Jura from Biel to Boncourt, called?
56593.e: The Transjurane connects the Jura with the Swiss Plateau and France. It has many tunnels and bridges.
56593.m: The A16 motorway is called the Transjurane.

56594.q: The German name of this town is Delsberg. What is it called in French?
56594.e: French is spoken in the canton of Jura, so Delémont is the official name. “Delsberg” is the German name.
56594.m: Delsberg is called Delémont in French.

56595.q: Delémont is the capital of which canton?
56595.e: Delémont, Delsberg in German, is the capital of the canton of Jura.
56595.m: Delémont is the capital of the canton of Jura.

56596.q: Roughly how many inhabitants does Delémont have (as of 2023)?
56596.e: At the end of 2023, 12,739 people lived in Delémont. Even so, it is the biggest municipality in the canton of Jura.
56596.m: Delémont is a small capital with about 12,700 inhabitants.

56597.q: What is special about the canton of Jura, whose capital is Delémont?
56597.e: The canton of Jura separated from the canton of Bern and has existed since 1979. This makes it the youngest canton in Switzerland.
56597.m: The Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland.

56598.q: In which year did Fribourg join the Swiss Confederation?
56598.e: Fribourg was admitted in 1481 together with Solothurn. The Agreement of Stans made this possible.
56598.m: Fribourg has been part of the Confederation since 1481.

56599.q: To which saint is the cathedral of Fribourg dedicated?
56599.e: The Gothic Cathedral of St Nicholas is the landmark of the city of Fribourg. Its tower is about 74 metres high.
56599.m: Fribourg's cathedral is called St Nicholas.

56600.q: Which Swiss university calls itself the only bilingual university in the country?
56600.e: At the University of Fribourg you can study in German and French. It was founded in 1889.
56600.m: In Fribourg you study in German and French.

56601.q: Which district of Fribourg is mainly German-speaking?
56601.e: The Sense district lies in the east of the canton on the border with Bern. People there speak the Sensler German dialect.
56601.m: German is spoken in the Sense district.

56603.q: Which town is the second biggest in the canton of Fribourg after the capital?
56603.e: Bulle is the main town of the Gruyère district and has been growing fast for years. The town has over 20,000 inhabitants.
56603.m: Bulle is the second biggest town in the canton of Fribourg.

56604.q: What is the traditional harvest festival with a big feast in the canton of Fribourg called?
56604.e: The Bénichon (Kilbi in German) includes a long menu with cakes, meat and saffron bread. It is celebrated in autumn, when the cows come back from the alpine pastures.
56604.m: In autumn the people of Fribourg celebrate the Bénichon.

56605.q: Which noble family founded the town of Fribourg in 1157?
56605.e: Duke Berchtold IV of Zähringen founded the town on a loop of the Saane. The Zähringer also founded other towns such as Bern.
56605.m: Fribourg was founded by the Zähringer.

56606.q: Which spa resort in Valais is known for its hot thermal springs?
56606.e: A great deal of warm water flows out of the springs of Leukerbad every day. Guests came to bathe there as early as the Middle Ages.
56606.m: In Leukerbad you bathe in warm thermal water.

56607.q: In which valley in Valais do the Tschäggättä roam around with wooden masks at carnival time?
56607.e: The Tschäggättä wear carved wooden masks and sheepskins. The custom is very old in the Lötschental.
56607.m: The Tschäggättä belong to the Lötschental.

56608.q: Which Roman building can you still see in Martigny today?
56608.e: The Romans built an amphitheatre in Martigny for games and fights. Today, for example, cow fights take place there.
56608.m: There is a Roman amphitheatre in Martigny.

56609.q: Which monastery in Valais has existed without interruption since the year 515?
56609.e: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice is seen as the oldest continuously existing monastery in the Western world. Its church treasure is very valuable.
56609.m: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice is over 1500 years old.

56610.q: By area, where does Valais rank among the biggest cantons in Switzerland?
56610.e: Valais covers about 5200 square kilometres. Only the Grisons and Bern are bigger.
56610.m: Valais is the third biggest canton in Switzerland.

56611.q: Roughly how high above sea level is the town of Sion?
56611.e: The old town of Sion lies in the Rhône valley at about 500 metres above sea level. But the mountains all around are over 3000 metres high.
56611.m: Sion lies about 500 metres above sea level.

56612.q: What are the two castle hills rising above Sion called?
56612.e: On Valère stands a fortified church, on Tourbillon a castle ruin. The two hills are the landmark of Sion.
56612.m: Valère and Tourbillon are the castle hills of Sion.

56613.q: What is in the basilica on Valère hill in Sion?
a: One of the oldest playable organs in the world
The longest wooden bridge in Switzerland
56613.e: The organ of the Valère Basilica dates from around 1430. It is still played at concerts today.
56613.m: One of the oldest playable organs in the world is in Sion.

56614.q: Which bid did the voters of Valais reject in 2018?
56614.e: In the vote, a majority said no to the funding for “Sion 2026”. That is why Switzerland withdrew the bid.
56614.m: In 2018 Valais said no to the Olympics in Sion.

56615.q: On which river does Sion lie?
56615.e: Sion lies in the middle of the Rhône valley in Valais. The Val d'Hérens also joins the Rhône valley near Sion.

56826.q: Which canton is the Entlebuch in?
56826.e: The Entlebuch is in the canton of Lucerne, between the city of Lucerne and the Emmental. It is a rural mountain region.
56826.m: The Entlebuch belongs to the canton of Lucerne.

56827.q: Which mountain lies on the border between the Entlebuch and the Emmental?
56827.e: The Napf is a viewpoint mountain between the Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne and the Emmental in the canton of Bern. It is about 1400 m high.
56827.m: The Napf lies between the Entlebuch and the Emmental.

56828.q: Which title did UNESCO give the Entlebuch in 2001?
56828.e: In 2001 the Entlebuch became the first area in Switzerland to be named a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Nature and the economy are meant to live in harmony there.
56828.m: The Entlebuch is a UNESCO biosphere.

56829.q: Which holiday resort in the Entlebuch lies at the foot of the Brienzer Rothorn?
56829.e: Sörenberg belongs to the municipality of Flühli in the upper Entlebuch. From there a cable car goes up to the Brienzer Rothorn.
56829.m: Sörenberg is the well-known holiday resort in the Entlebuch.

56830.e: The Entlebucher Mountain Dog is the smallest of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds. It used to be used for driving cattle.
56830.m: The Entlebucher Mountain Dog is named after the Entlebuch.

56831.q: What is the aim of a biosphere like the one in the Entlebuch?
a: To protect nature while still using the land sustainably
To move all the inhabitants away
To build as many factories as possible
To cut down the whole forest
56831.e: In a biosphere, people go on living and working. But they treat nature in a way that keeps it intact.
56831.m: In a biosphere, people and nature live in harmony.

56832.q: Which sector employs especially many people in the Entlebuch compared with the rest of Switzerland?
56832.e: About a third of the workers in the Entlebuch work in farming and forestry. The Swiss average is only a few per cent.
56832.m: Many people in the Entlebuch work in farming and forestry.

56833.q: Which kind of landscape is especially common in the Entlebuch?
56833.e: The Entlebuch has a great many raised bogs and fens. They are important habitats for rare plants and animals.
56833.m: The Entlebuch is rich in moors.

56834.q: Which canton are the Freiberge mostly in?
56834.e: The Freiberge lie in the south-west of the canton of Jura. A small part belongs to the canton of Bern.
56834.m: The Freiberge are mostly in the canton of Jura.

56835.q: Which place is the main town of the Freiberge?
56835.e: Saignelégier is the main town of the Freiberge. The village lies in the middle of the high plateau.
56835.m: Saignelégier is the main town of the Freiberge.

56836.q: What are the Freiberge called in French?
56836.e: The French name Franches-Montagnes means “free mountains”. In the Middle Ages, settlers who cleared the land for farming were given special freedoms.
56836.m: In French the Freiberge are called Franches-Montagnes.

56837.q: Which animal breed are the Freiberge known for?
56837.e: The Freiberger is the only Swiss horse breed. You can see many of these strong horses on the pastures of the Freiberge.
56837.m: The Freiberge are the home of the Freiberger horse.

56838.q: Roughly how high is the plateau of the Freiberge?
56838.e: The Freiberge are a plateau at an average of about 1000 m above sea level. That is why the winters there are long and cold.
56838.m: The Freiberge lie at a height of about 1000 metres.

56839.q: Why are there hardly any streams on the plateau of the Freiberge?
a: The water seeps into the limestone ground
56839.e: The limestone underground is full of karst. Rainwater seeps into cracks and flows away underground.
56839.m: In the karst of the Freiberge, water seeps into the ground.

56840.q: Which river borders the Freiberge to the north and north-west in a deep valley?
56840.e: The Doubs has cut a deep valley into the limestone of the Jura. It borders the plateau of the Freiberge to the north and north-west.
56840.m: The Doubs flows in a deep valley at the edge of the Freiberge.

56841.q: Which winter sport is especially popular on the flat plateau of the Freiberge?
56841.e: The Freiberge are a wide, rolling plateau without steep slopes. That makes them ideal for long cross-country ski trails.
56841.m: In winter, people love cross-country skiing in the Freiberge.

56842.q: Roughly what share of Switzerland’s area do the Alps cover?
56842.e: The Alps, together with the Prealps, cover about 60 per cent of the country. That makes them the largest of the main regions.
56842.m: The Alps cover about 60 per cent of Switzerland.

56843.q: Which river collects the water from most of the Central Plateau?
56843.e: With its tributaries such as the Saane, Emme, Reuss and Limmat, the Aare takes in the water of a large part of the Central Plateau. At Koblenz it flows into the Rhine.
56843.m: The Aare drains most of the Central Plateau.

56844.q: Roughly what share of Switzerland’s area does the Jura cover?
56844.e: The Jura is the smallest of the three main regions. It covers about 10 per cent of the country.
56844.m: The Jura makes up about 10 per cent of Switzerland.

56845.q: Switzerland is about 41,300 km² in size. About how many km² of it belong to the Central Plateau if you count 30 per cent?
56845.e: 30 per cent of 41,300 km² is 0.3 times 41,300, which is 12,390 km². Rounded, that is about 12,400 km².
56845.m: The Central Plateau is about 12,400 square kilometres in size.

56846.q: In which main region do most of Switzerland’s people live?
56846.e: Although the Central Plateau has only about a third of the area, most of the population lives there. The largest cities are there too.
56846.m: Most people in Switzerland live on the Central Plateau.

56847.q: Lake Geneva lies at 372 m above sea level, Lake Constance at 395 m. How much higher is Lake Constance?
56847.e: 395 m minus 372 m is 23 m. So the two lakes at either end of the Central Plateau lie at almost the same height.
56847.m: Lake Constance is only 23 metres higher than Lake Geneva.

56848.q: Which towns lie at the southern foot of the Jura, where the Jura meets the Central Plateau?
56848.e: Towns such as Biel, Grenchen and Solothurn line up along the southern foot of the Jura. Here the Jura chain meets the flat Central Plateau.
56848.m: Biel, Grenchen and Solothurn lie at the southern foot of the Jura.

56849.q: Who decided in 1863 to name the highest summit of the Monte Rosa massif after General Dufour?
56849.e: The Swiss Federal Council gave the summit its present name in 1863. In this way it honoured the general and map-maker Guillaume-Henri Dufour.
56849.m: The Federal Council gave the Dufourspitze its name in 1863.

56850.q: Which country did Charles Hudson come from, who led the first roped party up the Dufourspitze?
56850.e: Charles Hudson was an English clergyman and a well-known mountaineer. At that time, many first ascents in the Alps were made by English visitors with local mountain guides.
56850.m: The Englishman Charles Hudson led the first roped party up the Dufourspitze.

56851.q: In which war did Guillaume-Henri Dufour lead the federal troops as general in 1847?
56851.e: In the Sonderbund War of 1847, Dufour led the troops of the Diet. The war lasted only a few weeks and caused relatively few deaths.
56851.m: General Dufour led the troops in the Sonderbund War in 1847.

56852.q: In which year was the Dufourspitze climbed for the first time?
56852.e: On 1 August 1855 a roped party led by Charles Hudson reached the summit. The mountain guides Johannes and Matthäus Zumtaugwald and Ulrich Lauener broke the trail.
56852.m: The Dufourspitze was first climbed in 1855.

56854.q: Which mountain in the Alps is higher than the Dufourspitze?
56854.e: Only Mont Blanc, on the border between France and Italy, is higher, at about 4800 m. That makes the Dufourspitze the second-highest summit in the Alps.
56854.m: After Mont Blanc, the Dufourspitze is the second-highest summit in the Alps.

56855.q: Which SAC hut is the starting point for the normal route up the Dufourspitze?
56855.e: The normal route from the Swiss side starts at the Monte Rosa Hut at 2883 m above sea level. The hut is known for its modern, energy-saving design.
56855.m: People climbing the Dufourspitze usually start at the Monte Rosa Hut.

56857.q: What is the Matterhorn called in Valais German?
56857.e: In Valais German the Matterhorn is simply called Horu or Hore, meaning “the horn”.
56857.m: In Valais German the Matterhorn is called Horu.

56858.q: On the border between which two countries does the Matterhorn stand?
56858.e: The border between Valais and the Italian Aosta Valley runs over the summit of the Matterhorn.
56858.m: The Matterhorn stands on the border with Italy.

56859.q: How many men died on the way down after the first ascent of the Matterhorn?
56859.e: On the descent one climber slipped and pulled three others with him; the rope to the remaining men broke. Only three members of the party survived.
56859.m: Four men died on the descent after the first ascent of the Matterhorn.

56861.q: Which car-free village lies at the foot of the Matterhorn?
56861.e: Zermatt lies in the Matter Valley in Valais, right below the Matterhorn. Cars may only drive as far as Täsch.
56861.m: Zermatt lies at the foot of the Matterhorn.

56862.q: How did the Matterhorn get its typical pyramid shape?
a: Glaciers wore it down during the ice ages
56862.e: During the ice ages, glaciers wore away the rock from several sides. This left a steep horn-shaped peak with sharp ridges.
56862.m: Ice-age glaciers shaped the Matterhorn into a pyramid.

56864.q: Why do climbers fear the north face of the Matterhorn?
a: It is very steep, cold and often icy.
It is covered in thick forest.
It is very hot there in summer.
It is completely flat and slippery.
56864.e: The north face gets hardly any sun. It is very steep, often icy, and rocks fall. It was first climbed only in 1931.
56864.m: The Matterhorn north face is steep, cold and icy.

56865.q: Which cog railway runs up from Zermatt to a viewpoint looking at the Matterhorn?
56865.e: The Gornergrat Railway runs from Zermatt to over 3000 metres. From the top you can see the Matterhorn and many glaciers.
56865.m: The Gornergrat Railway offers a view of the Matterhorn.

56866.q: Which two mountains form the famous trio in the Bernese Oberland together with the Eiger?
56866.e: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side and can be seen clearly from Interlaken and Grindelwald.
56866.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau form the famous trio.

56867.q: Why is the Eiger north face considered especially dangerous?
a: Because of falling rocks and sudden changes in the weather
Because it is made of soft sand
Because there is a volcano there
56867.e: The face is about 1650 metres high. Falling rocks, ice and sudden changes in the weather long made it one of the most feared faces in the Alps.
56867.m: The Eiger north face is dangerous because of falling rocks and the weather.

56868.q: Which railway runs in a tunnel through the Eiger up to the Jungfraujoch?
56868.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs from the Kleine Scheidegg through the Eiger and the Mönch to the Jungfraujoch at about 3450 metres.
56868.m: The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger to the Jungfraujoch.

56869.q: Roughly how high is the Mönch?
56869.e: A measurement in 1999 gave 4110 metres above sea level. That makes the Mönch one of the four-thousanders of the Bernese Oberland.
56869.m: The Mönch is about 4100 metres high.

56870.q: Where does the name of the mountain Mönch probably come from?
a: From a monastery on the summit
From a monk who climbed it first
From a monk’s habit made of snow
56870.e: In the past, castrated horses, known as “Münche”, spent the summer on the alpine pastures at the foot of the mountain. So the mountain above was first called Münchenberg.
56870.m: The Mönch is probably named after castrated horses on the alpine pastures.

56871.q: Why have there been different heights given for the Mönch over time?
a: The cap of old snow on the summit changes
The summit was once blown up
In the past the height was measured in feet
56871.e: The measurements gave 4099 m (1935), 4107 m (1993) and 4110 m (1999). The differences come partly from measuring errors and partly from the growing cap of snow and firn.
56871.m: The height of the Mönch varies because its cap of firn changes.

56872.q: Which summit is the highest of the trio Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau?
a: They are all the same height
56872.e: At 4158 m above sea level, the Jungfrau is higher than the Mönch and the Eiger.
56872.m: The Jungfrau is the highest summit of the trio.

56874.q: On the border between which two cantons does the Jungfrau lie?
56874.e: The north side of the Jungfrau belongs to the Bernese Oberland, the south side to Valais.
56874.m: The Jungfrau lies between Bern and Valais.

56875.q: How high is Piz Bernina according to the national map?
56875.e: The national map of Switzerland gives 4048 metres for Piz Bernina.

56876.q: What is special about Piz Bernina?
a: It is the only four-thousander in the Eastern Alps
It is the highest mountain in Switzerland
56876.e: Piz Bernina is 4048 metres high. East of it, there is no other mountain in the Alps higher than 4000 metres.
56876.m: Piz Bernina is the only four-thousander in the Eastern Alps.

56878.q: Which place in the Upper Engadine lies on the north side at the foot of Piz Bernina?
56878.e: Pontresina lies north of the Bernina massif and is a starting point for climbs of Piz Bernina.
56878.m: Pontresina lies at the foot of Piz Bernina.

56879.q: What was the name “Bernina” first used for?
a: For the area around the Bernina Pass
For a monastery in the Engadine
For a lake near St Moritz
56879.e: The name first referred to the area around the Bernina Pass. Only later was it given to the highest summit.
56879.m: The name Bernina comes from the area around the Bernina Pass.

56880.q: What does “bianco” mean in the name of the Biancograt on Piz Bernina?
56880.e: “Bianco” is Italian and means white. The Biancograt is a narrow, snow-white ridge that many climbers use to reach the summit.
56880.m: The Biancograt is a snow-white ridge on Piz Bernina.

56881.q: Which cantons meet at the Säntis?
a: St Gallen and the two Appenzells
56881.e: The cantons of St Gallen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden meet at the Säntis.
56881.m: The Säntis lies between St Gallen and the two Appenzells.

56882.q: How do most visitors get up the Säntis?
a: By a lift inside the mountain
56882.e: Since 1935 a cable car has run from the Schwägalp to the summit of the Säntis.
56882.m: A cable car goes up the Säntis.

56883.q: What has been measured on the Säntis for over 140 years?
a: The water level of Lake Constance
56883.e: There has been a weather station on the Säntis since 1882. It is one of the oldest mountain weather stations in Switzerland.
56883.m: The weather has been measured on the Säntis for over 140 years.

56884.q: How many countries can you see from the Säntis on a clear day?
56884.e: You can see Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein, Italy and France.
56884.m: From the Säntis you can see six countries on a clear day.

56885.q: Roughly how tall is the transmitter tower on the Säntis?
56885.e: The transmitter tower on the summit is 123 metres tall. It sends radio and mobile phone signals across eastern Switzerland.
56885.m: There is a transmitter tower about 120 metres tall on the Säntis.

56886.q: Which nickname has the Rigi had for a long time?
56886.e: Because of its wonderful view over lakes and Alps, the Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”. The name itself, however, actually means something else.
56886.m: The Rigi is also called the Queen of the Mountains.

56887.q: From which two places do cog railways go up the Rigi?
56887.e: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway runs up from Lake Lucerne, the Arth-Rigi Railway from Arth-Goldau. From Weggis there is a cable car, not a cog railway.
56887.m: Cog railways run up the Rigi from Vitznau and Arth-Goldau.

56888.q: Which place on the Rigi can be reached by cable car from Weggis?
56888.e: The cable car links Weggis on Lake Lucerne with Rigi Kaltbad. From there a cog railway also continues towards the summit.
56888.m: A cable car runs from Weggis to Rigi Kaltbad.

56889.q: Which rock, made of pebbles cemented together, makes up most of the Rigi?
56889.e: Nagelfluh formed from gravel that rivers brought down from the young Alps. The round stones are stuck together as if in concrete.
56889.m: The Rigi is made mainly of nagelfluh.

56890.q: What is the steepest gradient of the Pilatus Railway?
56890.e: The Pilatus Railway climbs gradients of up to 48 per cent. That makes it the steepest cog railway in the world.
56890.m: With gradients of up to 48 per cent, the Pilatus Railway is the steepest cog railway in the world.

56891.q: Which figure from an old legend is Pilatus named after?
56891.e: According to legend, the ghost of the Roman governor Pontius Pilate rests in a lake on the mountain. That is where the mountain’s name comes from.
56891.m: According to legend, Pilatus is named after Pontius Pilate.

56892.q: According to an old Lucerne legend, what happens if you throw a stone into the Pilatus lake?
a: The lake dries up at once
56892.e: According to the legend, the ghost of Pontius Pilate rests in the lake. Anyone who disturbs it with a stone sets off terrible storms.
56892.m: According to legend, a stone in the Pilatus lake causes a storm.

56893.q: Which three cantons share the Pilatus massif?
56893.e: The Pilatus massif lies where the cantons of Lucerne, Nidwalden and Obwalden meet. Its summit can be reached by railway or cable car from Kriens and from Alpnachstad.
56893.m: Pilatus lies in Lucerne, Nidwalden and Obwalden.

56894.q: Which mountain group does the Titlis belong to?
56894.e: The Titlis is one of the highest summits of the Uri Alps. It rises between the Engelberg valley and the Gadmer valley.
56894.m: The Titlis belongs to the Uri Alps.

56895.q: Near which monastery village is the Titlis?
56895.e: The Titlis rises above Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. The village is known for its monastery and as a holiday resort.

56896.q: At roughly what height does the Titlis Cliff Walk suspension bridge hang?
56896.e: The Titlis Cliff Walk opened in December 2012 at 3041 m above sea level. It crosses a drop about 500 metres deep.
56896.m: The Titlis Cliff Walk hangs at about 3000 metres above sea level.

56897.q: Who is said to have been the first to climb the Titlis in the 18th century?
a: A monk from the nearby monastery
56897.e: Swiss sources name a monk from the monastery in the valley as the first to climb it, in 1739. Other documents mention a party of four in 1744.
56897.m: The Titlis was probably first climbed by a monk from the monastery in the 18th century.
