56898.q: Which mountain lake lies by the middle station of the cable car up the Titlis?
56898.e: The Trübsee lies on a plateau below the Titlis. Passengers change there on their way to the summit.
56898.m: The Trübsee lies on the way to the Titlis.

56899.q: Which pass road runs past the south side of the Titlis?
56899.e: The Susten Pass road runs through the Gadmer valley on the south side of the Titlis and links Bern with Uri.
56899.m: The Susten Pass road runs past the south of the Titlis.

56900.q: What is the wild gorge of the Reuss on the northern climb to the Gotthard called?
56900.e: The route to the Gotthard goes through the Schöllenen between Göschenen and Andermatt. The Devil’s Bridge there, with its legend, is well known.
56900.m: The Devil’s Bridge stands in the Schöllenen Gorge.

56901.q: How did people travel over the Gotthard Pass in the 19th century, before the railway tunnel existed?
56901.e: After the carriage road was built, stagecoaches regularly crossed the pass. The journey was long and dangerous in winter.
56901.m: In the past, people crossed the Gotthard by stagecoach.

56902.q: Which village in Ticino lies at the southern foot of the Gotthard Pass?
56902.e: The pass road leads down from the top of the pass to Airolo in the Leventina. The southern entrance of the old railway tunnel is there too.
56902.m: Airolo lies at the southern foot of the Gotthard.

56903.q: How many workers died building the first Gotthard railway tunnel?
56903.e: Officially, 177 workers died in accidents. Many more fell ill because of the bad air and the heat in the tunnel.
56903.m: About 180 workers died building the first Gotthard tunnel.

56904.q: Roughly how long is the first Gotthard railway tunnel?
56904.e: The summit tunnel is about 15 km long. When it opened, it was the longest tunnel in the world.
56904.m: The old Gotthard railway tunnel is about 15 kilometres long.

56905.q: Which engineer led the building of the first Gotthard railway tunnel and died during the work?
56905.e: The Geneva engineer Louis Favre died of heart failure in 1879 during an inspection in the tunnel. He did not live to see the tunnel open.
56905.m: Louis Favre led the building of the first Gotthard tunnel.

56906.q: What does the National Gotthard Museum at the top of the pass show?
a: The history of travel over the pass
Animals from all over the world
56906.e: In the old warehouse building at the top of the pass, you learn how mule drivers, stagecoaches and later trains and cars crossed the Gotthard.
56906.m: The Gotthard Museum shows the history of travel over the pass.

56907.q: Which famous dog breed is named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard?
56907.e: The monks of the hospice were already breeding St Bernards more than 300 years ago. The dogs helped to find travellers in the snow.
56907.m: The St Bernard dog comes from the Great St Bernard.

56908.q: Which Italian valley does the Great St Bernard link with Valais?
56908.e: The pass leads from the Rhône valley in Valais over into the Aosta Valley in Italy.
56908.m: The Great St Bernard links Valais with the Aosta Valley.

56909.q: What were St Bernard dogs used for on the Great St Bernard in the past?
a: To find lost travellers in the snow
To pull sledges full of cheese
To guard the hospice against thieves
56909.e: With their keen sense of smell, the dogs found people who had lost their way in fog or snow. The dog Barry is said to have saved more than 40 people.
56909.m: St Bernard dogs rescued travellers on the pass.

56910.q: On which animal did Napoleon really cross the Great St Bernard?
56910.e: Famous paintings show Napoleon on a rearing horse. In reality he rode over the pass on a sure-footed mule.
56910.m: Napoleon crossed the pass on a mule.

56911.q: Roughly how long is the road tunnel under the Great St Bernard?
56911.e: The tunnel is 5.85 km long and links Valais with Italy.
56911.m: The Great St Bernard Tunnel is almost 6 kilometres long.

56912.q: Why is the road tunnel under the Great St Bernard especially important in winter?
a: The pass road is then closed because of snow
The tunnel is free in winter
You can ski in the tunnel
Only trains run there in winter
56912.e: The pass road is usually closed in winter from October to June. Through the tunnel you can still get to Italy all year round.
56912.m: The tunnel is open in winter too.

56913.q: Which people already used a route over the Great St Bernard about 2000 years ago?
56913.e: The Romans built a road over the pass and put up a temple to the god Jupiter at the top.
56913.m: Even the Romans crossed the Great St Bernard.

56914.q: At roughly what height is the top of the Great St Bernard Pass?
56914.e: The top of the pass is at 2469 m above sea level, on the border with Italy. The hospice stands there.
56914.m: The Great St Bernard is at about 2500 metres.

56916.q: Which valley region of Valais lies west of the Furka Pass?
56916.e: The Furka Pass links the Urseren valley with the Goms, the uppermost part of the Rhône valley.
56916.m: The Goms lies west of the Furka.

56917.q: What does the heritage railway use in summer to travel over the old mountain line at the Furka?
56917.e: The Furka Steam Railway runs with historic steam locomotives over the old line near the Rhône Glacier. Volunteers rebuilt it.
56917.m: Steam trains run over the old Furka mountain line.

56918.q: What does the Latin word “furca”, from which the name Furka comes, mean?
56918.e: “Furca” means a two-pronged fork. The name describes the gap between two mountains.
56918.m: The name Furka comes from the Latin word for fork.

56919.q: What is the highest railway station in Europe, in the saddle between the Mönch and the Jungfrau, called?
56919.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger and the Mönch up to the Jungfraujoch at 3454 metres. It is the highest railway station in Europe.
56919.m: The Jungfraujoch lies between the Mönch and the Jungfrau.

56920.q: The Furka Pass separates the catchment areas of which two large rivers?
56920.e: Water from the Valais side flows into the Rhône and the Mediterranean. Water from the Uri side reaches the Rhine and the North Sea via the Reuss.
56920.m: The Furka separates the area of the Rhône from that of the Rhine.

56921.q: Roughly how long is the Furka Base Tunnel?
56921.e: The Furka Base Tunnel of the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway is about 15.4 km long.
56921.m: The Furka Base Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long.

56922.q: Which building opened at the top of the Julier Pass in 2017?
56922.e: The ten-sided theatre tower was designed by Giovanni Netzer and was meant as a temporary building. The first performance took place in August 2017.
56922.m: Since 2017 there has been a theatre tower on the Julier Pass.

56923.q: Which well-known holiday resort in the Upper Engadine do you reach from Chur over the Julier Pass?
56923.e: After the Julier Pass you come to Silvaplana and straight after that to St Moritz in the Upper Engadine.
56923.m: Over the Julier Pass you drive to St Moritz in the Upper Engadine.

56924.q: What does the study of language say about the name Julier?
a: It is older than the Romans
It comes from the month of July
56924.e: The link with Julius Caesar is a folk explanation. The name is older than Roman times; its exact meaning is disputed.
56924.m: The name Julier is older than Roman times.

56925.q: Which European watershed runs over the Julier Pass?
a: Between the Rhine and the Danube
Between the Rhône and the Po
Between the Rhine and the Rhône
Between the Danube and the Po
56925.e: Water from the north side flows via the Albula to the Rhine, water from the Engadine side via the Inn to the Danube.
56925.m: The watershed between the Rhine and the Danube runs over the Julier Pass.

56926.q: What at the top of the Julier Pass reminds us of the Romans?
56926.e: The Romans already used the Julier Pass. At the top there are remains of columns from that time.
56926.m: Even the Romans travelled over the Julier Pass.

56927.q: Roughly how high is the Maloja Pass?
56927.e: The top of the pass is at 1812 m above sea level; the highest point of the road, in the village of Maloja, is at 1815 m.
56927.m: The Maloja Pass is at about 1800 metres above sea level.

56928.q: Which canton is the Maloja Pass in?
56928.e: The Maloja Pass is in the canton of Grisons. It links the Upper Engadine with the Bregaglia.
56928.m: The Maloja Pass is in the Grisons.

56929.q: What is special about the Maloja Pass?
a: The Engadine side is almost flat
It is the highest pass in Switzerland
It does not have a single bend
You can only cross it on foot
56929.e: From Maloja eastwards, the Engadine slopes down only gently. On the west side, however, the road winds steeply down with 13 hairpin bends.
56929.m: The Maloja Pass is almost flat on the Engadine side and steep on the Bregaglia side.

56930.q: Into which valley does the road from the Maloja Pass wind steeply down in many bends?
56930.e: West of the Maloja Pass the land drops steeply into the Bregaglia. The valley belongs to the Grisons and is Italian-speaking.
56930.m: From the Maloja Pass the road leads steeply down into the Bregaglia.

56931.q: Which famous painter lived in Maloja from 1894?
56931.e: Giovanni Segantini painted many pictures of the Engadine mountain landscape in Maloja. He died in 1899 on the Schafberg in the Upper Engadine.
56931.m: The painter Giovanni Segantini lived in Maloja.

56932.q: In which canton are most of Switzerland’s four-thousanders?
56932.e: Most Swiss four-thousanders are in the Valais Alps, for example around Zermatt and Saas-Fee. Only a few are in the Bernese Oberland or the Grisons.
56932.m: Most of Switzerland’s four-thousanders are in Valais.

56933.q: Near which holiday resort in Valais are there especially many four-thousanders?
56933.e: Around Zermatt there are many four-thousanders, including the Matterhorn, the Breithorn and the Dufourspitze.
56933.m: There are many four-thousanders around Zermatt.

56934.q: Which is the highest mountain that lies entirely on Swiss territory?
56934.e: The Dom is about 4545 m above sea level. All the higher Swiss summits lie on the border with Italy.
56934.m: The Dom is the highest mountain entirely in Switzerland.

56935.q: Which is the highest mountain in Switzerland?
56935.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is 4634 m high. It lies on the border with Italy.
56935.m: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

56936.q: Which four-thousander forms a famous trio with the Eiger and the Mönch in the Bernese Oberland?
56936.e: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side above Grindelwald and Wengen. At 4158 m, the Jungfrau is the highest of the three.
56936.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau form a famous trio.

56937.q: Why are snow cornices on mountain ridges dangerous for climbers?
56937.e: A cornice is an overhanging edge of snow. Anyone who steps on it can fall with it. That is why there were many accidents on the Lyskamm.
56937.m: Snow cornices can suddenly break off.

56938.q: Which of these Swiss mountains is higher than 4000 metres?
56938.e: The Weissmies in the Saas Valley is just over 4000 m above sea level. The Tödi, Pizol and Glärnisch are all clearly lower than 4000 m.
56938.m: The Weissmies in the Saas Valley is a four-thousander.

56939.q: What do you need to climb a four-thousander safely?
56939.e: Routes up four-thousanders often cross glaciers with crevasses. You need a rope, crampons, experience or a mountain guide.
56939.m: Four-thousanders need experience and glacier equipment.

56940.q: Which river flows through the canton of Uri into Lake Lucerne?
56940.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area, flows through the Reuss valley in Uri and enters Lake Lucerne at Flüelen.
56940.m: The Reuss is the river of the canton of Uri.

56941.q: Which mountain is the highest point of the canton of Glarus?
56941.e: At 3614 m above sea level, the Tödi is the highest summit of the Glarus Alps.
56941.m: The Tödi is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus.

56942.q: Which mountain is the highest point of the Swiss Central Plateau?
56942.e: The Napf, between the Emmental and the Entlebuch, reaches 1408 m above sea level.
56942.m: The Napf is the highest mountain of the Central Plateau.

56943.q: Up which of Lucerne’s local mountains does the steepest cog railway in the world run?
56943.e: The Pilatus Railway runs from Alpnachstad up Pilatus. With gradients of up to 48 per cent, it is the steepest cog railway in the world.
56943.m: The steepest cog railway in the world runs up Pilatus.

56944.q: On which lake in the canton of Ticino is the lowest point in Switzerland?
56944.e: Lake Maggiore lies at about 193 m above sea level. That is the lowest point in Switzerland.
56944.m: The lowest point in Switzerland is on Lake Maggiore.

56945.q: Which mountain massif forms the highest point of the canton of Vaud?
56945.e: The summit of the Diablerets reaches about 3210 m above sea level on the border with Valais.
56945.m: Les Diablerets are the highest point of Vaud.

56946.q: Which well-known cheese is named after a region in the canton of Fribourg?
56946.e: Gruyère comes from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg. The little town of Gruyères with its castle is there too.
56946.m: Gruyère cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg.

56947.q: Which two striking rocky peaks rise above the cantonal capital Schwyz?
56947.e: The two Mythen are the landmark of the canton of Schwyz. A steep footpath leads up the Great Mythen.
56947.m: The Mythen are the landmark of Schwyz.

56948.q: Which mountain is the highest summit of the Alpstein in eastern Switzerland?
56948.e: The Säntis is about 2500 m high and lies on the border of the cantons of St Gallen and Appenzell. From its summit you can see six countries on a clear day.
56948.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain of the Alpstein.

56949.q: Which is the largest lake that lies entirely in the canton of Bern?
56949.e: Lake Thun lies entirely in the canton of Bern and is larger than Lake Brienz. Lake Biel is smaller and also borders the canton of Neuchâtel.
56949.m: Lake Thun is the largest lake entirely in the canton of Bern.

56950.q: What is the large nature reserve on the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel called?
56950.e: The Grande Cariçaie is a long area of reeds, wet meadows and riverside woods. It formed when the lake level was lowered and shallow shores dried out.
56950.m: The Grande Cariçaie on Lake Neuchâtel is a large protected shoreline.

56951.q: Roughly how deep is Lake Neuchâtel at its deepest point?
56951.e: Lake Neuchâtel is about 150 metres deep at its deepest point. It is about 38 kilometres long.
56951.m: Lake Neuchâtel is up to about 150 metres deep.

56952.q: What is special about Lake Constance compared with other lakes?
a: The borders in the lake are not fixed by treaty
It is the deepest lake in Europe
56952.e: For the largest part of Lake Constance, the Obersee, there is no treaty on where the border runs. The countries have different views on it.
56952.m: In the Obersee of Lake Constance the borders are not fixed by treaty.

56953.q: Which Swiss cantons border Lake Constance?
56953.e: Thurgau has most of the Swiss shore. St Gallen borders the Obersee, Schaffhausen the end of the Untersee.
56953.m: Thurgau, St Gallen and Schaffhausen border Lake Constance.

56954.q: What are the two main parts of Lake Constance called?
56954.e: The large Obersee (Upper Lake) and the smaller Untersee (Lower Lake) are joined at Konstanz by the Seerhein.
56954.m: Lake Constance consists of the Obersee and the Untersee.

56955.q: Roughly how large is Lake Lucerne?
56955.e: At about 114 square kilometres, it is one of the largest lakes in Switzerland.
56955.m: Lake Lucerne is about 114 square kilometres in size.

56956.q: Which rock ledge on Lake Uri recalls the legend of William Tell?
56956.e: According to the legend, Tell leapt ashore at this spot from the boat of the bailiff Gessler. The Tell Chapel stands there today.
56956.m: The Tellsplatte on Lake Uri recalls William Tell.

56957.q: What was discovered at Obermeilen on Lake Zurich in the winter of 1853/54, when the water was low?
56957.e: Because of the low water level, wooden posts and finds came to light. The researcher Ferdinand Keller explained them as the remains of villages built on piles.
56957.m: Pile dwellings were discovered at Obermeilen in 1854.

56958.q: Which ferry links the two shores of Lake Zurich?
56958.e: The car ferry between Horgen and Meilen crosses the lake in about ten minutes. It saves drivers the detour via Zurich.
56958.m: A ferry crosses Lake Zurich between Horgen and Meilen.

56959.q: Which lake is the deepest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland?
56959.e: Lake Brienz is up to about 260 metres deep. Lake Thun and Lake Lucerne are just over 210 metres deep.
56959.m: Lake Brienz is the deepest lake entirely in Switzerland.

56960.q: Which steam railway runs from Brienz up a viewpoint mountain?
56960.e: The Brienz Rothorn Railway is a cog railway that still runs with steam locomotives. From the summit you can see far across Lake Brienz.
56960.m: The Brienz Rothorn Railway runs by steam from Brienz up the Rothorn.

56962.q: Which of the three Jura lakes is the largest?
56962.e: The Jura lakes are Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten. Lake Neuchâtel is much larger than Lake Biel.
56962.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest Jura lake.

56964.q: Which neighbouring country does Switzerland share Lake Lugano with?
56964.e: Lake Lugano lies on the border with Italy. About two thirds belong to Switzerland, the rest to Italy.
56964.m: Switzerland and Italy share Lake Lugano.

56965.q: Which valley is Lake Sils in?
56965.e: Lake Sils lies in the Upper Engadine between Maloja and Sils. It is the largest of the Upper Engadine lakes.
56965.m: Lake Sils is in the Upper Engadine.

56966.q: At roughly what height is Lake Sils?
56966.e: Lake Sils lies at almost 1800 metres above sea level. That is why it usually freezes over in winter.
56966.m: Lake Sils lies at almost 1800 metres above sea level.

56967.q: Which sport can you do on the frozen Lake Sils in winter?
56967.e: In winter Lake Sils usually freezes over. Then ski trails run across the ice, for example during the Engadin Ski Marathon.
56967.m: In winter you can go cross-country skiing on Lake Sils.

56968.q: What runs on Lake Sils between Sils and Maloja in summer?
56968.e: For over a hundred years, a scheduled boat has run on Lake Sils in summer. It passes the Chastè peninsula.
56968.m: A passenger boat runs on Lake Sils.

56969.q: Which lake in the Upper Engadine is especially popular with kitesurfers and windsurfers?
56969.e: On many afternoons a strong and very steady wind blows over Lake Silvaplana. That makes it a well-known spot for kitesurfers.
56969.m: Lake Silvaplana is a popular kitesurfing lake.

56970.q: Why are reservoirs built in the Alps?
a: So that cargo ships can sail
56970.e: The stored water flows down through pipes to a power station, where it drives turbines. Hydropower supplies most of Switzerland’s electricity.

56971.q: What is a pumped-storage power station?
a: A power station that pumps water up into a higher lake
A power station that stores oil
A power station that stores wind
A power station that cleans water
56971.e: When there is plenty of electricity, water is pumped upwards. When electricity is needed, it flows back down and drives turbines.
56971.m: A pumped-storage power station pumps water up and later uses it for electricity.

56972.q: Where are most of Switzerland’s large reservoirs?
56972.e: The Alps have deep valleys, lots of water and big differences in height. That is why most dams are there, for example at Lago di Lei or Lac des Dix.
56972.m: Most large reservoirs are in the Alps.

56973.q: What was the Jura Water Correction mainly built for?
a: To prevent flooding in the Seeland
56973.e: The Aare and the Jura lakes often used to burst their banks. With new canals and lower lake levels, the Seeland was protected from floods.
56973.m: The Jura Water Correction protects the Seeland from floods.

56974.q: By roughly how much were the lake levels lowered during the first Jura Water Correction?
56974.e: The levels of Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Biel and Lake Murten fell by about 2.5 metres. This uncovered wide strips of shore.
56974.m: The lake levels were lowered by about 2.5 metres.

56975.q: What did the marshes in the Seeland become after the Jura Water Correction?
56975.e: The drained soils are very fertile. That is why the Seeland is now called the vegetable garden of Switzerland.
56975.m: The Seeland is the vegetable garden of Switzerland.

56976.q: Which river was diverted into Lake Biel during the Jura Water Correction?
56976.e: Since then, a new canal has led the Aare into Lake Biel. There it drops its gravel instead of flooding the land.
56976.m: Since the correction, the Aare flows into Lake Biel.

56977.q: Which structure at Port controls the water level of the Jura lakes today?
56977.e: The Port regulating weir at the outflow of Lake Biel was completed in 1939. It can control how much water flows out of Lake Biel.
56977.m: The Port regulating weir controls the Jura lakes.

56978.q: Which traces from prehistoric times appeared on the shores after the lake levels were lowered?
56978.e: When the shores dried out, many remains of pile-dwelling villages were found. Among them were settlements from the Bronze Age.
56978.m: Pile-dwelling settlements appeared when the lakes were lowered.

56979.q: Which cantons took part in the Jura Water Correction?
a: Bern, Solothurn, Fribourg, Neuchâtel and Vaud
Bern, Lucerne, Zug, Aargau and Zurich
Vaud, Valais, Geneva, Jura and Basel
Fribourg, Uri, Schwyz, Glarus and Bern
56979.e: All five cantons suffered from the floods of the Jura lakes and the Aare. Together with the Confederation, they paid for the project.
56979.m: Five cantons took part in the Jura Water Correction.

56980.q: After Lake Geneva, which is the second-largest lake with a Swiss shore?
56980.e: Including the Untersee, Lake Constance is clearly larger than Lake Neuchâtel, the largest lake entirely in Switzerland. Only part of Lake Constance belongs to Switzerland.
56980.m: Lake Constance is the second-largest lake with a Swiss shore.

56981.q: Roughly what share of the area of Lake Geneva belongs to Switzerland?
56981.e: Of Lake Geneva’s roughly 580 square kilometres, about 345 are in Switzerland. The rest belongs to France.
56981.m: About 60 per cent of Lake Geneva belongs to Switzerland.

56982.q: Which lake with a Swiss part is the deepest?
56982.e: Lake Maggiore is up to about 372 metres deep. Its deepest point, in the Italian part, lies far below sea level.
56982.m: Lake Maggiore is the deepest lake with a Swiss part.

56983.q: Which lake in Switzerland holds the most water?
56983.e: Lake Geneva holds about 89 cubic kilometres of water. It is both large and very deep.
56983.m: Lake Geneva holds the most water of all Swiss lakes.

56984.q: Which lake is in the canton of Lucerne and is known for a battle in 1386?
56984.e: The Battle of Sempach took place by Lake Sempach in 1386. The lake is about 14 square kilometres in size.
56984.m: Lake Sempach is in the canton of Lucerne.

56985.q: Which is the largest lake in the Jura?
56985.e: The Lac de Joux lies in the Vallée de Joux in the canton of Vaud at about 1000 metres above sea level. It is about 9 kilometres long and is considered the largest lake in the Jura mountains.
56985.m: The Lac de Joux is the largest lake in the Jura.

56986.q: Which river forms the border with France for a long stretch in the Jura?
56986.e: In the Jura, the Doubs flows a long way along the border between Switzerland and France. The Lac des Brenets and the Saut du Doubs waterfall are there too.
56986.m: The Doubs forms the border with France in the Jura.

56987.q: Which site on Lake Neuchâtel gave its name to a whole period of the Iron Age?
56987.e: At La Tène, at the north-eastern end of the lake, many Celtic weapons and tools were found. The later Iron Age is called the La Tène period after this place.
56987.m: The La Tène period is named after the site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel.

56988.q: What is the cold wind called that suddenly blows down from the Jura onto Lake Neuchâtel?
56988.e: The Joran often comes very suddenly after hot summer days. It is dangerous for sailors and swimmers on the lake.
56988.m: The Joran is a dangerous downslope wind on Lake Neuchâtel.

56989.q: At which castle on Lake Neuchâtel did the Confederates defeat Charles the Bold in 1476?
56989.e: At Grandson, on the west shore of Lake Neuchâtel, the Confederates won against the Duke of Burgundy. The castle still stands by the lake today.
56989.m: The Confederates won at Grandson on Lake Neuchâtel in 1476.

56990.q: Which river flows into Lake Neuchâtel at Yverdon-les-Bains?
56990.e: The Orbe comes from the Jura and is called the Thielle in its lower course. At Yverdon-les-Bains it flows into Lake Neuchâtel.
56990.m: The Orbe flows into Lake Neuchâtel at Yverdon.

56991.q: Which Thurgau town on Lake Constance directly borders the German town of Konstanz?
56991.e: Kreuzlingen and Konstanz have grown together. The national border runs right through the built-up area.
56991.m: Kreuzlingen lies right next to Konstanz.

56992.q: In which little town does the Rhine leave the Untersee?
56992.e: At Stein am Rhein the Untersee ends and the High Rhine flows on towards Schaffhausen. The little town is known for its painted houses.
56992.m: The Rhine leaves Lake Constance at Stein am Rhein.

56993.q: Who built a fort at Arbon on Lake Constance about 1700 years ago?
56993.e: The Romans built a fort at Arbon and called the place Arbor Felix. Remains of it can still be seen today.
56993.m: The Romans built a fort at Arbon.

56994.q: How many countries border Lake Constance?
56994.e: Switzerland, Germany and Austria border Lake Constance.
56994.m: Three countries meet at Lake Constance.

56995.q: Which place on Lake Lucerne was its own little republic until 1817?
56995.e: Gersau bought its freedom in the Middle Ages and was long considered the smallest republic in the world. In 1817 it became part of the canton of Schwyz.
56995.m: Gersau was its own little republic until 1817.

56996.q: Which four places gave Lake Lucerne its German name, Vierwaldstättersee (Lake of the Four Forest Cantons)?
56996.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden used to be called the forest cantons. Together with Lucerne, they were the four forest cantons on the lake.
56996.m: Lake Lucerne’s German name comes from Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne.

56997.q: Which footpath around Lake Uri was opened in 1991 for the 700th birthday of the Confederation?
56997.e: Each canton designed a section of the path, its length depending on the canton’s population. The path runs from the Rütli to Brunnen.
56997.m: The Swiss Path runs around Lake Uri.

56998.q: Which road runs along the east shore of Lake Uri from Brunnen to Flüelen?
56998.e: The Axenstrasse was built into the steep rock and runs through tunnels and galleries. It is the important link from Schwyz to Uri.
56998.m: The Axenstrasse runs along Lake Uri.

56999.q: Which town lies where the Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne?
56999.e: The Reuss flows out of Lake Lucerne in the town of Lucerne. The famous Chapel Bridge crosses it.
56999.m: The Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne in Lucerne.

57000.q: Which arm of Lake Lucerne reaches south as far as Flüelen?
57000.e: Lake Uri is the south-eastern arm of the lake and lies in the canton of Uri. Flüelen is at its end.
57000.m: Lake Uri reaches as far as Flüelen.

57001.q: What is the peninsula on the left shore of Lake Zurich near Wädenswil called?
57001.e: The Au peninsula juts into the lake between Wädenswil and Horgen. It is a popular recreation area with vineyards and a castle.
57001.m: The Au peninsula is near Wädenswil on Lake Zurich.

57002.q: What has the long wooden footbridge across Lake Zurich linked since 2001?
57002.e: The wooden footbridge is about 840 metres long and only for pedestrians. It follows an old pilgrims’ route to Einsiedeln.
57002.m: A long wooden footbridge links Rapperswil and Hurden.

57003.q: What happened to Lake Zurich in the winter of 1963?
57003.e: When the lake froze in 1963, people could walk across the whole of Lake Zurich. It has not frozen over completely since then.
57003.m: In the winter of 1963 Lake Zurich froze over completely.

57004.q: Where does the city of Zurich get most of its drinking water from?
57004.e: Lake water works pump water from the depths of Lake Zurich and clean it. The rest comes from groundwater and springs.
57004.m: The city of Zurich drinks mainly treated lake water.

57005.q: Roughly how large is Lake Zurich, including the Obersee?
57005.e: Lake Zurich is about 88 square kilometres in size. That makes it one of the large lakes in Switzerland.
57005.m: Lake Zurich is about 88 square kilometres in size.

57006.q: Roughly how long is Lake Zurich from Zurich to Schmerikon?
57006.e: From the city of Zurich to Schmerikon at the upper end, the lake measures about 40 kilometres. It is long and rather narrow.
57006.m: Lake Zurich is about 40 kilometres long.

57007.q: Which river flows through Lake Thun?
57007.e: The Aare flows from Lake Brienz into Lake Thun and leaves it again in Thun.
57007.m: The Aare flows through Lake Thun.

57008.q: Roughly how large is Lake Thun?
57008.e: Lake Thun is about 48 square kilometres in size. That makes it clearly larger than neighbouring Lake Brienz.
57008.m: Lake Thun is about 48 square kilometres in size.

57009.q: Which castle stands on a rocky spur in a bay on the south shore of Lake Thun?
57009.e: Spiez Castle stands above the bay with the harbour and the vineyards. It is one of the best-known views on Lake Thun.
57009.m: Spiez Castle stands above a bay on Lake Thun.

57010.q: What is performed every summer at the Thunerseespiele?
57010.e: At the Thunerseespiele, musicals are shown on a stage right on the lakeshore in Thun.
57010.m: The Thunerseespiele present musicals by the lake.

57012.q: Why is Lake Brienz often turquoise-green?
a: Because of fine rock flour from glaciers
Because of algae in the water
Because of copper in the lake bed
57012.e: The streams that feed it bring very fine rock from glaciers. These particles float in the water and scatter the light.
57012.m: Glacier flour gives Lake Brienz its turquoise-green colour.

57013.q: Which valley does the Aare come from before it flows into Lake Brienz?
57013.e: The Aare rises in the Grimsel area and flows through the Hasli Valley with Meiringen. At Brienz it flows into the lake.
57013.m: The Aare comes through the Hasli Valley into Lake Brienz.

57014.q: Which village on the south shore of Lake Brienz lies on a small peninsula?
57014.e: Iseltwald lies on a peninsula on the south shore. At the end of the peninsula stands the little Seeburg castle.
57014.m: Iseltwald lies on a peninsula in Lake Brienz.

57015.q: What grows on the sunny slopes on the north shore of Lake Biel?
57015.e: On the north shore of Lake Biel there are wine villages such as Twann and Ligerz. The vines benefit from the sun and the lake.
57015.m: Wine grows on the north shore of Lake Biel.

57016.q: Which French-speaking little town in the canton of Bern lies at the western end of Lake Biel?
57016.e: La Neuveville belongs to the canton of Bern, but people there speak French. The little town lies at the south-western end of the lake.
57016.m: La Neuveville lies at the western end of Lake Biel.

57018.q: Why was the level of Lake Biel lowered in the 19th century?
a: To protect the Seeland from flooding
So that bigger ships could sail
So that the fish had more room
57018.e: The Seeland used to be flooded often. With the Jura Water Correction, rivers were diverted and the lake levels lowered.
57018.m: The lake levels were lowered to protect the Seeland.

57019.q: Which place lies between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun?
57019.e: Interlaken means between the lakes. The town lies on the plain between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun.
57019.m: Interlaken lies between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun.

57020.q: What is the village of Twann on Lake Biel known for?
57020.e: Twann is an old wine village on the north shore of Lake Biel. There are many vineyards around the village.
57020.m: Twann is a wine village on Lake Biel.

57021.q: Roughly how deep is Lake Walen at its deepest point?
57021.e: Lake Walen is up to about 151 metres deep. Its shores are steep because it lies between high mountains.
57021.m: Lake Walen is up to about 150 metres deep.

57022.q: What did the name Walensee (Lake Walen) originally mean?
57022.e: By “Walen”, the Alemannic settlers meant the Romance-speaking people further east. A language border used to run along the lake.
57022.m: The name Walensee means lake of the Romance speakers.

57023.q: Where has the Linth been directed since the Linth Correction over 200 years ago?
57023.e: From 1807 to 1811 the Linth was diverted into Lake Walen. Since then it has dropped its gravel there, and the marshes in the Linth plain became drier.
57023.m: Since the Linth Correction, the Linth flows into Lake Walen.

57024.q: Which little town lies at the western end of Lake Walen?
57024.e: Weesen lies at the western end of the lake, where the Linth leaves Lake Walen again.
57024.m: Weesen lies at the western end of Lake Walen.

57025.q: Which river is now the main river flowing into Lake Walen?
57025.e: Since the Linth Correction, the Linth has flowed into Lake Walen near Mollis. It brings the lake the most water.
57025.m: The Linth is the main river flowing into Lake Walen.

57026.q: Which other lake does the water of Lake Lugano flow on into?
57026.e: The water leaves Lake Lugano at Ponte Tresa by the river Tresa and flows into Lake Maggiore at Luino.
57026.m: Lake Lugano drains into Lake Maggiore.

57027.q: What is special about Lake Lugano, even though it is not very large?
57027.e: Lake Lugano is only about 49 square kilometres in size, but almost 300 metres deep at its deepest point.
57027.m: Lake Lugano is small but very deep.

57028.q: Which picturesque village lies at the southern tip of the peninsula between the arms of Lake Lugano?
57028.e: Morcote lies at the foot of Monte Arbostora and has many steps and arcades. In 2016 it was voted the most beautiful village in Switzerland.

57029.q: Which lakeside path runs from Castagnola to Gandria on Lake Lugano?
57029.e: Olive trees grow again along the Olive Path, and signs explain their history. The path runs along the foot of Monte Brè.
57029.m: The Olive Path runs from Castagnola to Gandria.

57031.q: Roughly what share of Lake Lugano belongs to Switzerland?
57031.e: About 63 per cent of the lake’s area is in the canton of Ticino. The rest belongs to Italy.
57031.m: About two thirds of Lake Lugano belongs to Switzerland.

57032.q: What are the mysterious “Sils balls” that wash up on the shore in autumn?
57032.e: The balls of larch needles grow up to 30 centimetres across. Exactly how they form has not yet been fully worked out.
57032.m: The Sils balls are made of larch needles.

57033.q: What is Lake Sils called in Romansh?
57033.e: In the Engadine people speak Romansh. There Sils is called Segl, and “Lej” means lake.
57033.m: In Romansh, Lake Sils is called Lej da Segl.

57034.q: Which river rises in the Upper Engadine and flows through the lakes towards Austria?
57034.e: The Inn flows through the Upper Engadine lakes, then through the Lower Engadine to Austria. Later it flows into the Danube.
57034.m: The Inn flows through the Upper Engadine lakes.

57035.q: What is the wind called that blows over the Upper Engadine lakes on summer afternoons?
57035.e: During the day the Maloja wind blows from the Maloja Pass down the valley. That is unusual, because valley winds usually blow up the valley.
57035.m: The Maloja wind blows in the Upper Engadine in the afternoon.

57036.q: Roughly how high is the Mauvoisin dam in Valais?
57036.e: The Mauvoisin arch dam in the Val de Bagnes is about 250 metres high. It is one of the highest arch dams in the world.
57036.m: The Mauvoisin dam is about 250 metres high.

57037.q: How does an arch dam hold back the water?
a: It passes the water pressure sideways into the rock walls
It is so heavy that it does not move
It lets the water out through holes
It is held in place with cables
57037.e: The wall curves towards the lake. The water pressure is passed through the arch into the sides of the valley, so the wall can be thinner.
57037.m: An arch dam passes the water pressure into the rock walls.

57038.q: Which canton is the large Nant de Drance pumped-storage power station in?
57038.e: Nant de Drance lies near Finhaut between the Emosson and Vieux Emosson reservoirs. It was completed in 2022.
57038.m: The Nant de Drance pumped-storage power station is in Valais.

57039.q: Which reservoir was created on the Aare below Bern in 1920?
57039.e: For the Mühleberg power station, the Aare was dammed to form Lake Wohlen. It lies west of the city of Bern.
57039.m: Lake Wohlen is a reservoir on the Aare near Bern.

57040.q: What was discovered near the Emosson reservoir in Valais in 1976?
57040.e: In 1976 many fossil footprints were found on a rock slab above the Lac du Vieux Emosson. They come from prehistoric reptiles and are about 250 million years old.
57040.m: There are ancient fossil footprints near the Emosson reservoir.

57041.q: Which reservoir on the Aare in the canton of Aargau is an important reserve for water birds?
57041.e: The Klingnau reservoir was created in 1935 for a river power station. Many migrating birds rest in its shallow bays.
57041.m: The Klingnau reservoir is a bird reserve.

57042.q: Instead of concrete, what else can a dam be built from?
57042.e: Some reservoirs are held back by a wide dam of earth and rock. One example is the Mattmarksee in the Saas Valley.
57042.m: A dam can also be made of earth and rock.

57043.q: Which three lakes are called the Jura lakes?
57043.e: The three lakes lie at the foot of the Jura and are joined by canals. In the Jura Water Correction they were regulated together.
57043.m: Lakes Neuchâtel, Biel and Murten are the Jura lakes.

57044.q: What did the Seeland often look like before the Jura Water Correction?
57044.e: Before the correction, large parts of the Seeland were often under water. Many fields were marsh, and people suffered from diseases.
57044.m: The Seeland used to be often marshy and flooded.

57045.q: Which little town with a well-preserved ring wall lies on Lake Murten?
57045.e: Murten lies on the east shore of Lake Murten. You can still walk along its old town wall today.

57046.q: Where did the Aare flow near Aarberg before the first Jura Water Correction?
a: Straight towards Büren, past Lake Biel
57046.e: In the past, the Aare flowed through the Seeland past Lake Biel and dropped a lot of gravel. Only the canal led it into the lake.
57046.m: Before the correction, the Aare flowed past Lake Biel.

57047.q: Why are Lakes Neuchâtel, Biel and Murten at almost the same height?
a: Because they are joined by canals
Because they are the same age
Because they are fed by the same spring
57047.e: The three lakes are joined by canals and regulated together. Their levels are all at about 429 metres above sea level.
57047.m: Thanks to canals, Lakes Neuchâtel, Biel and Murten are at almost the same height.

57048.q: Roughly what share of Europe’s freshwater reserves does Switzerland have?
57048.e: Switzerland makes up only about 0.4 per cent of Europe’s area, but has about 6 per cent of its freshwater reserves. Glaciers, lakes and lots of rain make this possible.
57048.m: Little Switzerland has about 6 per cent of Europe’s fresh water.

57049.q: How many different seas does water from Switzerland reach?
57049.e: Swiss water flows into the North Sea, the western Mediterranean, the Adriatic and the Black Sea. That is why Switzerland is also called the “land of four seas”.
57049.m: Water from Switzerland flows into four different seas.

57051.q: Which of these rivers does NOT rise in the area of the Gotthard massif?
57051.e: The Rhine, Rhône, Reuss and Ticino all rise around the Gotthard massif. The Inn, on the other hand, has its source further east in the Upper Engadine.
57051.m: The Inn rises in the Engadine, not at the Gotthard.

57052.q: Which mountain lake is considered the source of the Rhine?
57052.e: Lake Toma lies at about 2340 m above sea level near the Oberalp Pass. The Anterior Rhine flows out of it.
57052.m: Lake Toma near the Oberalp Pass is considered the source of the Rhine.

57053.q: Which of Switzerland’s water stores is getting smaller and smaller because of global warming?
57053.e: Switzerland stores water in lakes, in groundwater and in glaciers. The glaciers are melting because of warming and lose a lot of ice every year.
57053.m: Glaciers, as water stores, are shrinking.

57054.q: Why are glaciers important water stores for Swiss rivers?
a: They store rain and snow as ice and release it in summer
They filter salt out of sea water
They keep the water frozen all year
They bring water from abroad into Switzerland
57054.e: Glaciers collect snow as ice over many years. In hot, dry summers their meltwater then gives the rivers especially large amounts of water.
57054.m: Glaciers store water as ice and release it to the rivers in summer.

57055.q: Which large European river gets NO water from Switzerland?
57055.e: Swiss water reaches the Danube via the Inn and the Po via the Ticino and Adda, and the Aare and Rhine carry it to the North Sea. The Elbe, however, rises in the Czech Republic and has no tributaries from Switzerland.
57055.m: Swiss water reaches the Rhine, Rhône, Danube and Po, but not the Elbe.

57056.q: Roughly how long is the Aare?
57056.e: The Aare is 288 kilometres long. It flows from the Grimsel to the border with Germany, where it joins the Rhine.
57056.m: The Aare is almost 290 kilometres long.

57057.q: Through which three cantonal capitals does the Aare flow?
57057.e: The Aare loops around the old town of Bern, then flows through Solothurn and later through Aarau. Lucerne is on the Reuss, Fribourg on the Saane.
57057.m: Bern, Solothurn and Aarau are on the Aare.

57058.q: What happened in Bern’s Matte district on the Aare in August 2005?
57058.e: In August 2005 heavy rain caused major floods in Switzerland. In Bern the Aare flooded the low-lying Matte district.
57058.m: In August 2005 the Aare flooded Bern’s Matte district.

57059.q: Which lake in the Seeland does the Aare flow through?
57059.e: The Aare is led into Lake Biel by the Hagneck Canal. At Nidau it leaves the lake through the Nidau-Büren Canal.
57059.m: The Aare flows through Lake Biel.

57060.q: What record temperature did the Aare reach in Bern in August 2022?
57060.e: On 4 August 2022, the water of the Aare in Bern measured 24.1 degrees Celsius. At the time that was the highest value since measurements began in 1970.
57060.m: In August 2022 the Aare in Bern was over 24 degrees.

57061.q: Which gorge has the Aare cut between Innertkirchen and Meiringen?
57061.e: The Aare Gorge is about 1.4 kilometres long, and its rock walls rise up to 180 metres. The Aare wore it through a barrier of limestone.
57061.m: Near Meiringen the Aare flows through the Aare Gorge.

57062.q: Why is the Aare dammed at the Mühleberg power station west of Bern?
a: To add salt to drinking water
To make ice for the winter
57062.e: The Mühleberg hydropower station generates electricity from the Aare. The dam created Lake Wohlen.
57062.m: The Mühleberg power station generates electricity from the Aare.

57063.q: Which two glaciers feed the Aare at its source?
57063.e: The Aare begins in the Grimsel area from the meltwater of the Oberaar Glacier and the Unteraar Glacier. Both carry the river’s name.
57063.m: The Aare rises at the Oberaar and Unteraar glaciers.

57064.q: On average, how much water pours over the Rhine Falls every second in summer?
57064.e: In summer, on average about 600 cubic metres of water flow over the Rhine Falls every second. That is about 600,000 litres each second.
57064.m: In summer about 600 cubic metres of water thunder over the Rhine Falls every second.

57065.q: How much water flowed over the Rhine Falls per second during the record flood of 1965?
57065.e: In 1965 the largest amount of water was measured, at about 1250 cubic metres per second. The smallest amount, in 1921, was only about 95 cubic metres per second.
57065.m: The record at the Rhine Falls is about 1250 cubic metres of water per second.

57066.q: Which hard rock is the rock step of the Rhine Falls made of?
57066.e: There, the Rhine flows from hard Jura limestone onto soft gravel. It could hardly wear away the limestone, but it could wear away the gravel, and so the step formed.
57066.m: The Rhine Falls formed at a step of hard limestone.

57067.q: How deep is the pool that the Rhine Falls has washed out beneath it?
57067.e: The falling water has washed out a pool, called a plunge pool, about 13 metres deep. That is deeper than a four-storey house is tall.
57067.m: Below the Rhine Falls there is a pool about 13 metres deep.

57068.q: Which little castle stands on the Neuhausen side right by the pool of the Rhine Falls?
57068.e: Schlössli Wörth stands on a small island by the pool of the Rhine Falls near Neuhausen. It used to be a customs post for river boats.
57068.m: Schlössli Wörth lies by the pool of the Rhine Falls.

57069.q: What was electricity from a power station at the Rhine Falls used for from 1889?
57069.e: Europe’s first aluminium works started operating in Neuhausen by the Rhine Falls in 1889. Making aluminium needs a great deal of electricity.
57069.m: From 1889, electricity from the Rhine Falls powered Europe’s first aluminium works.

57070.q: What stands on the middle rock in the Rhine Falls?
57070.e: A large Swiss flag flies on the middle rock of the Rhine Falls. The rocks are remains of the old limestone wall.
57070.m: The Swiss flag flies on the middle rock in the Rhine Falls.

57071.q: About how many people visited the Rhine Falls in 2013?
57071.e: In 2013 about 1.3 million visitors came to the Rhine Falls. It is one of the most visited sights in Switzerland.
57071.m: Well over a million people visit the Rhine Falls every year.

57072.q: Where does the Reuss rank among Switzerland’s largest rivers?
57072.e: Only the Rhine, Aare and Rhône are larger than the Reuss. Its catchment area covers about 3400 square kilometres.
57072.m: The Reuss is the fourth-largest river in Switzerland.

57073.q: In which village do the Furkareuss and the Gotthardreuss join?
57073.e: In Hospental in the Urseren valley, the Furkareuss and the Gotthardreuss join. From there the river is simply called the Reuss.
57073.m: In Hospental two source rivers join to form the Reuss.

57074.q: What is the nature reserve called where the Reuss flows into Lake Uri?
57074.e: Near Flüelen and Seedorf, the Reuss has built a delta into Lake Uri. The Reuss Delta has been protected since 1985.
57074.m: The Reuss Delta on Lake Uri is a nature reserve.

57075.q: What does the needle weir in Lucerne control?
a: The water level of Lake Lucerne
57075.e: At the needle weir, individual wooden posts, the needles, can be put in or pulled out. This controls how much water flows out of the lake.
57075.m: The needle weir in Lucerne controls the level of Lake Lucerne.

57076.q: Which river from the Entlebuch flows into the Reuss at Emmenbrücke?
57076.e: The Kleine Emme comes from the Entlebuch and flows into the Reuss between Reussbühl and Emmenbrücke. It should not be confused with the Emme from the Emmental.
57076.m: The Kleine Emme flows into the Reuss at Emmenbrücke.

57077.q: Which river carries the water of Lake Zug to the Reuss?
57077.e: The Lorze flows out of Lake Zug at Cham. At Maschwanden it joins the Reuss from the right.
57077.m: The Lorze links Lake Zug with the Reuss.

57078.q: Which small town in Aargau with a covered wooden bridge lies on the Reuss?
57078.e: Bremgarten lies in a bend of the Reuss and has an old covered wooden bridge. Below the town, the Reuss flows largely naturally for about 25 kilometres.
57078.m: Bremgarten, with its wooden bridge, lies on the Reuss.

57079.q: Which river does the Reuss flow into?
57079.e: The Reuss flows into the Aare at Brugg. Shortly after, the Limmat joins too, and then the Aare flows into the Rhine.
57079.m: The Reuss flows into the Aare at Brugg.

57080.q: Which river does the Limmat flow into?
57080.e: The Limmat flows from Lake Zurich through Zurich and Baden and joins the Aare at Brugg, at the place called the “water castle”.
57080.m: The Limmat flows into the Aare.

57081.q: Which large city does the Limmat flow through right after leaving the lake?
57081.e: The Limmat begins at the Quaibrücke at the outflow of Lake Zurich and flows right through the old town of Zurich.

57082.q: Which town in Aargau with warm healing springs lies on the Limmat?
57082.e: Baden lies on the Limmat and has been known for its warm thermal springs since Roman times. Aarau is on the Aare, Rheinfelden on the Rhine.
57082.m: The spa town of Baden lies on the Limmat.

57083.q: Which monastery lies in a bend of the Limmat in Aargau?
57083.e: The former Cistercian monastery of Wettingen lies right on a bend of the Limmat. It was founded in the 13th century.
57083.m: Wettingen Abbey lies on the Limmat.

57084.q: Which river joins the Limmat in the city of Zurich at the Platzspitz?
57084.e: The Sihl comes from the Sihlsee and flows through Zurich. At the Platzspitz behind the main station, it joins the Limmat.
57084.m: In Zurich the Sihl flows into the Limmat.

57085.q: Which river power station lies on the Limmat in the city of Zurich?
57085.e: The Letten power station uses the current of the Limmat in the middle of Zurich. Many more river power stations stand on the Limmat before it ends.
57085.m: The Letten power station generates electricity from the Limmat in Zurich.

57086.q: Which canton does the Linth come from, whose water later flows on as the Limmat?
57086.e: The Linth rises on the Tödi in the canton of Glarus. It flows through Lake Walen and Lake Zurich and is then called the Limmat.
57086.m: The Linth comes from the canton of Glarus.

57087.q: Who led the Linth Correction from 1807, when the Linth was diverted into Lake Walen?
57087.e: Hans Conrad Escher led the diversion of the Linth into Lake Walen to protect the Linth plain from floods. As thanks, he was given the extra name “von der Linth”.
57087.m: Hans Conrad Escher von der Linth tamed the Linth.

57088.q: Which valley does the Inn flow through in Switzerland?
57088.e: The Inn flows through the Upper and Lower Engadine in the Grisons. The valley is even named after the river: En is the Romansh name of the Inn.
57088.m: The Inn flows through the Engadine.

57089.q: What is special where the Inn joins the Danube?
a: On average the Inn carries more water than the Danube
The Inn is twice as long as the Danube there
The Inn joins it over a waterfall
The Inn is warmer than the Danube there
57089.e: On average over the year, the Inn brings about 740 cubic metres of water per second to Passau, the Danube only about 690. Even so, after they meet the river is called the Danube.
57089.m: At Passau the Inn brings more water on average than the Danube.

57090.q: Which three seas does the water from the Lunghin Pass in the Upper Engadine flow to?
a: North Sea, Adriatic and Black Sea
Black Sea, Baltic and North Sea
57090.e: Three large catchment areas meet at the Lunghin Pass. The water flows via the Rhine, the Po and the Inn into three different seas.
57090.m: The Lunghin Pass is a triple watershed of Europe.

57091.q: Which village on the Inn is known as the gateway to the Swiss National Park?
57091.e: The visitor centre of the National Park is in Zernez. Many hikes into the park start from there.
57091.m: Zernez is the gateway to the National Park.

57093.q: Near which pass in the Upper Engadine does the Inn rise?
57093.e: The Inn rises at Lake Lunghin above Maloja. Then it flows through the Upper Engadine lakes.
57093.m: The Inn rises near the Maloja Pass.

57094.q: Which countries does the Inn flow through?
a: Switzerland, Germany and the Czech Republic
57094.e: The Inn rises in the Grisons, flows through Tyrol and later forms the border with Bavaria. In Germany it finally flows into the Danube.
57094.m: The Inn flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany.

57095.q: Which spa resort in the Lower Engadine lies on the Inn?
57095.e: Scuol lies on the Inn in the Lower Engadine and is known for its mineral springs. Davos, Arosa and Klosters are not in the Engadine.
57095.m: Scuol is a spa resort on the Inn in the Lower Engadine.

57096.q: Roughly how long is the Ticino river?
57096.e: The Ticino is 248 kilometres long. A large part of it is in Italy, after Lake Maggiore.
57096.m: The Ticino is about 250 kilometres long.

57097.q: Which lake does the Ticino river flow into?
57097.e: The Ticino flows through the canton of Ticino and enters Lake Maggiore at Magadino.
57097.m: The Ticino flows into Lake Maggiore.

57098.q: Which capital of the canton of Ticino does the Ticino river flow through?
57098.e: The Ticino flows past Bellinzona, the capital of the canton of Ticino. Just before, the Moesa from the Mesolcina joins the Ticino.

57099.q: Which plain does the Ticino flow through just before Lake Maggiore?
57099.e: Between Bellinzona and Lake Maggiore, the Ticino flows through the flat Magadino plain. There is a lot of farming and vegetable growing there.
57099.m: Before Lake Maggiore, the Ticino crosses the Magadino plain.

57100.q: Where does the Ticino river rise?
57100.e: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass. Then it flows through the Bedretto valley and the Leventina to Lake Maggiore.
57100.m: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass.

57101.q: Which large Italian river does the Ticino flow into?
57101.e: After Lake Maggiore, the Ticino flows through northern Italy and joins the Po near Pavia.
57101.m: The Ticino flows into the Po.

57102.q: What is the river Ticino called in German?
57102.e: In German the river Ticino is called Tessin. The canton of Ticino is named after it.
57102.m: In German the Ticino is called Tessin.

57103.q: Which large Italian city gets water from the Ticino through an old canal?
57103.e: The Naviglio Grande was built in the Middle Ages and carries water from the Ticino to Milan.
57103.m: An old canal carries water from the Ticino to Milan.

57104.q: Roughly how long is the Saane?
57104.e: The Saane is about 126 kilometres long. It is one of the most important tributaries of the Aare.
57104.m: The Saane is about 130 kilometres long.

57105.q: Which river joins the Saane at Laupen?
57105.e: The Sense forms part of the border between the cantons of Bern and Fribourg. At Laupen it flows into the Saane.
57105.m: At Laupen the Sense flows into the Saane.

57107.q: Which cantonal capital does the Saane flow through?
57107.e: The Saane flows through the city of Fribourg in a deep gorge. The old town lies right by the river.
57107.m: The Saane flows through the city of Fribourg.

57108.q: Which place in the Pays-d’Enhaut in Vaud does the Saane flow through?
57108.e: In the Pays-d’Enhaut the Saane flows through Château-d’Oex and Rossinière. There it is called the Sarine in French.
57108.m: The Saane flows through Château-d’Oex in the Pays-d’Enhaut.

57110.q: In which mountains does the Saane rise?
57110.e: The Saane rises at about 2300 metres above sea level in the Bernese and Valais Alps near the Sanetsch Pass.
57110.m: The Saane rises in the Alps.

57111.q: What is the language border near Fribourg also called, because there it roughly follows the river?
57111.e: Near Fribourg the Saane roughly separates German-speaking and French-speaking areas. So people speak of the “Saanegraben” (Saane ditch) instead of the “Röstigraben”, the usual nickname for the language border.
57111.m: Near Fribourg the Saane roughly forms the language border.

57112.q: Which river does the Doubs flow into?
57112.e: The Doubs joins the Saône at Verdun-sur-le-Doubs in France. With it, its water travels on southwards.
57112.m: The Doubs is a tributary of the Saône.

57113.q: Which sea does the water of the Doubs finally reach?
57113.e: Via the Saône and the Rhône, the water of the Doubs flows into the Mediterranean. So part of the Jura also belongs to the Rhône area.
57113.m: The water of the Doubs flows into the Mediterranean.

57114.q: Roughly how high is the Saut du Doubs waterfall?
57114.e: The Saut du Doubs lies on the border near Les Brenets and is about 27 metres high. You can also reach it by boat across the Lac des Brenets.
57114.m: The Saut du Doubs is about 27 metres high.

57115.q: What is the large loop of the Doubs that lies entirely on Swiss soil called?
57115.e: The Clos du Doubs is a stretch of about 29 kilometres entirely in Switzerland. After it, the river turns back towards France.
57115.m: In the Clos du Doubs, the Doubs flows entirely through Swiss territory.

57116.q: How far apart, in a straight line, are the source and the mouth of the Doubs?
57116.e: The Doubs is about 450 kilometres long, but it makes huge detours. Its source and mouth are only about 90 kilometres apart.
57116.m: The Doubs makes big detours; its source is close to its mouth.

57117.q: In which country does the Doubs rise?
57117.e: The Doubs rises from a karst spring near Mouthe in the French Jura. Only later does it reach the Swiss border.
57117.m: The Doubs rises in the French Jura.

57118.q: Which canton is the loop of the Doubs around Saint-Ursanne in?
57118.e: Saint-Ursanne and the large river loop are in the canton of Jura. There the Doubs flows through a deep, wooded valley.
57118.m: The Doubs loop near Saint-Ursanne is in the canton of Jura.

57119.q: At which village in Neuchâtel does the Doubs begin to form the border with France?
57119.e: From Les Brenets the national border follows the Doubs. Le Landeron and La Neuveville lie on Lake Biel, Les Verrières in the Val-de-Travers.
57119.m: From Les Brenets the Doubs forms the border with France.

57120.q: Roughly how long is the Rhône Glacier today?
57120.e: The Rhône Glacier is almost 8 kilometres long and about 2 kilometres wide. It covers about 15 square kilometres.
57120.m: The Rhône Glacier is almost 8 kilometres long.

57121.q: Which Alpine pass is the Rhône Glacier on?
57121.e: The Furka Pass road runs close past the Rhône Glacier. At the Hotel Belvédère you can walk up to the glacier.
57121.m: The Rhône Glacier is on the Furka Pass.

57122.q: Which village in Valais did the Rhône Glacier almost reach around 1856?
57122.e: Around 1856 the glacier was at its largest and reached almost to the hotels of Gletsch. Today it ends far above, at over 2200 m above sea level.
57122.m: The Rhône Glacier used to reach almost to Gletsch.

57123.q: What has formed in front of the tongue of the Rhône Glacier since about 2007?
57123.e: Because the glacier is shrinking back, meltwater collects behind a rock barrier. This has created a new lake, which will keep growing.
57123.m: A new lake has formed in front of the melting Rhône Glacier.

57124.q: What can you visit inside the ice of the Rhône Glacier in summer?
57124.e: An ice grotto that you can walk into is cut into the glacier tongue. A short path leads up to it from the Furka road.
57124.m: There is an ice grotto in the Rhône Glacier.

57125.q: Why do researchers know so exactly how much the Rhône Glacier has shrunk?
a: It has been measured for over 150 years
It grows by the same amount every year
57125.e: The Rhône Glacier has been measured almost without gaps since the 19th century. That makes it one of the best-studied glaciers.
57125.m: The Rhône Glacier has been measured for over 150 years.

57126.q: Roughly how long is the Rhône from its source to the Mediterranean?
57126.e: The Rhône is about 810 kilometres long. About a third of it is in Switzerland, the rest in France.
57126.m: The Rhône is about 810 kilometres long.

57127.q: What is the large delta of the Rhône on the Mediterranean called?
57127.e: In the Camargue the Rhône splits into two arms and forms a large delta. It is known for flamingos and white horses.
57127.m: The Rhône flows into the Mediterranean in the Camargue.

57128.q: What do you call the border between two catchment areas?
57128.e: A watershed separates areas whose water flows into different rivers. It usually runs along mountain ridges and passes.
57128.m: A watershed separates two catchment areas.

57129.q: What share of Switzerland’s area drains via the Rhine?
57129.e: About two thirds of Switzerland lies in the catchment area of the Rhine, because the Aare, Reuss and Limmat belong to it too. The water finally flows into the North Sea.
57129.m: About two thirds of Switzerland drains via the Rhine.

57130.q: Which catchment area does the canton of Geneva belong to?
57130.e: Geneva lies at the outflow of Lake Geneva, through which the Rhône flows. The Arve from France also belongs to the Rhône area there.
57130.m: The canton of Geneva belongs to the catchment area of the Rhône.

57131.q: Which river area does the water from the Val Poschiavo flow into?
57131.e: The Poschiavino flows into Italy into the Adda, and the Adda flows into the Po. So the water from the Val Poschiavo reaches the Adriatic.
57131.m: The Val Poschiavo drains via the Adda to the Po.

57132.q: From which valley in the Grisons does Swiss water flow into the Adige?
57132.e: The Rom flows through the Val Müstair into South Tyrol and joins the Adige there. The Adige finally reaches the Adriatic.
57132.m: The Val Müstair drains into the Adige.

57133.q: From what share of Switzerland’s area does the water come that meets at Brugg in the “water castle”?
57133.e: Where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet, water from about 40 per cent of Switzerland gathers. That is why the place is called the water castle of Switzerland.
57133.m: At the water castle near Brugg, water from about 40 per cent of Switzerland comes together.

57134.q: Which sea does the water of Lake Neuchâtel finally flow into?
57134.e: Lake Neuchâtel drains via the Zihl into Lake Biel and from there with the Aare to the Rhine. So its water reaches the North Sea, even though the lake is in western Switzerland.
57134.m: The water of Lake Neuchâtel flows via the Aare and Rhine into the North Sea.

57135.q: Roughly what share of Swiss electricity production came from hydropower in 2024?
57135.e: According to the Swiss Federal Office of Energy, about 59.5 per cent of the electricity produced in Switzerland in 2024 came from hydropower. That makes it the most important domestic source of electricity.
57135.m: Hydropower supplies about 60 per cent of Swiss electricity (as of 2024).

57136.q: Why is Switzerland especially well suited to hydropower?
a: Because of the mountains, lots of rain and snow and steep slopes
Because of its long sea coast
57136.e: A lot of rain and snow falls in the mountains. The water flows steeply down into the valleys and can drive turbines on the way.
57136.m: Mountains, rain and snow and steep slopes make Switzerland a hydropower country.

57137.q: What is a run-of-river power station?
a: A power station that uses the flowing water of a river
A power station that stores water in a mountain lake for months
A power station that makes electricity from sea waves
A power station that heats water into steam
57137.e: A run-of-river power station dams a river with a weir and constantly uses the water flowing through. It mainly supplies steady electricity around the clock.
57137.m: A run-of-river power station uses the flowing water of a river.

57138.q: What does a pumped-storage power station do when there is a lot of spare electricity?
a: It pumps water into a higher reservoir
It lets the reservoir run empty
It sends the water to the sea
57138.e: With spare electricity, the power station pumps water upwards. When electricity is needed later, the water flows back down and drives turbines.
57138.m: A pumped-storage power station stores energy by pumping water upwards.

57139.q: What is the highest dam in Switzerland, in Valais, called?
57139.e: The Grande Dixence dam is 285 metres high. It is the highest gravity dam in the world.
57139.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest dam in Switzerland.

57141.q: What is the reservoir behind the Grande Dixence mainly used for?
57141.e: The stored water flows down through tunnels to power stations in the Rhône valley. There it drives turbines that generate electricity.
57141.m: The Grande Dixence supplies water for generating electricity.

57142.q: Where does most of the water in the Grande Dixence reservoir come from?
a: From groundwater on the Central Plateau
57142.e: In summer, snow and glacier ice melt around the four-thousanders of Valais. The meltwater is led through tunnels to the reservoir.
57142.m: Glacier water fills the Grande Dixence reservoir.

57143.q: Roughly how high is the Grande Dixence dam?
57143.e: The Grande Dixence is about 285 metres high. It is the highest dam in Switzerland.
57143.m: The Grande Dixence is about 285 metres high.

57144.q: Why are reservoirs for power stations often built high up in the mountains?
a: The water falls a long way and drives the turbines powerfully
No people who need electricity live there
The water is warmer up there
57144.e: The bigger the difference in height, the more force the water has down at the turbines. That produces a lot of electricity.
57144.m: A big drop gives a lot of electricity from hydropower.

57145.q: Which record does the Grande Dixence hold?
a: It is the highest gravity dam in the world
It is the longest bridge in Switzerland
It is the deepest lake in Europe
It is the oldest dam in the world
57145.e: The Grande Dixence holds back the water with its enormous weight. At 285 metres, it is the highest gravity dam in the world.
57145.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

57146.q: Roughly how thick is the ice of the Aletsch Glacier at Konkordiaplatz?
57146.e: At Konkordiaplatz the glacier is more than 900 metres thick. Towards the tongue the ice gets much thinner.
57146.m: At Konkordiaplatz the Aletsch ice is almost a kilometre thick.

57147.q: Which organisation declared the Jungfrau-Aletsch region a World Heritage Site?
57147.e: UNESCO honours especially valuable natural and cultural sites as World Heritage. The Jungfrau-Aletsch region was the first natural heritage site in the Alps.
57147.m: The Jungfrau-Aletsch region is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

57150.q: Which conifer grows in the old Aletsch Forest beside the glacier?
57150.e: In the protected Aletsch Forest, Swiss stone pines grow that are several hundred years old. The Swiss stone pine is a typical tree high up in the Alps.
57150.m: Ancient Swiss stone pines grow in the Aletsch Forest.

57151.q: What are the dark stripes running along the Great Aletsch Glacier?
57151.e: When two arms of a glacier flow together, their lateral moraines join to form a medial moraine. On the Aletsch Glacier they form long dark bands.
57151.m: The dark stripes on the Aletsch Glacier are medial moraines.

57152.q: When did the Alpine glaciers last reach a big maximum?
57152.e: At the end of the Little Ice Age, around 1850, the Alpine glaciers were especially large. Since then they have been melting back, with short breaks.
57152.m: The glaciers have been getting smaller since about 1850.

57153.q: What is the main cause of glacier loss in Switzerland today?
57153.e: Higher temperatures melt more ice in summer than is added as snow in winter. That is why the glaciers are losing mass.
57153.m: Global warming is melting the glaciers.

57154.q: Roughly what percentage of their ice volume did Swiss glaciers lose in the record year 2022?
57154.e: According to the glacier monitoring network GLAMOS, about 6 per cent of the ice volume melted away in 2022. The causes were a winter with little snow, Saharan dust and a hot summer.
57154.m: In 2022 more glacier ice melted than ever measured before.

57155.q: What does comparing old glacier photos with today’s photos show?
a: The glaciers have become much smaller
The glaciers have stayed the same
The glaciers have moved somewhere else
57155.e: In photos from 100 years ago, many glaciers reach far down into the valley. Today the ice often ends far higher up, and rubble lies where it used to be.
57155.m: Old photos show how much the glaciers have shrunk.

57156.q: According to GLAMOS, by how much did the volume of Swiss glaciers shrink between 2015 and 2025?
57156.e: In 2025 GLAMOS reported that Swiss glaciers had lost about a quarter of their volume in ten years. They had never melted so fast since measurements began.
57156.m: In just ten years, about a quarter of Swiss glacier ice disappeared.

57157.q: What is used at the ice grotto on the Rhône Glacier to slow down melting?
57157.e: Light-coloured fleece sheets reflect the sunlight and protect the ice. So clearly less ice melts in these places.
57157.m: White sheets keep the sun’s rays off the Rhône Glacier.

57158.q: Why does a glacier melt faster when dust or soot lies on it?
a: Dark surfaces absorb more heat from the sun
Dust creates wind over the ice
57158.e: Bright ice and snow reflect a lot of sunlight. Dark dust reduces this reflection, so more heat is absorbed.
57158.m: Dark ice melts faster than bright ice.

57159.q: Which problem arises when glaciers shrink and the permafrost beneath them thaws?
a: Rockfalls and debris flows become more frequent
57159.e: Ice and frozen ground hold rocks and rubble together. When everything thaws, slopes can become unstable, and rockfalls and debris flows happen more often.
57159.m: Melting ice can make mountain slopes unstable.

57160.q: Which canton is the Morteratsch Glacier in?
57160.e: The Morteratsch Glacier lies in the Upper Engadine in the Bernina group. So it belongs to the canton of Grisons.
57160.m: The Morteratsch Glacier is in the Upper Engadine in the Grisons.

57161.q: Which mountain group is the Morteratsch Glacier in?
57161.e: The glacier flows north from the ice-covered high mountains in the south of the Upper Engadine. The Bernina group is the highest range in the Eastern Alps.
57161.m: The Morteratsch Glacier comes from the Bernina group.

57162.q: Which four-thousander rises above the accumulation zone of the Morteratsch Glacier?
57162.e: Piz Bernina is 4049 metres high and the only four-thousander in the Eastern Alps. The glacier’s accumulation zone lies between it and Piz Argient.
57162.m: Piz Bernina towers above the Morteratsch Glacier.

57163.q: Which railway line has a station right below the Morteratsch Glacier?
57163.e: Morteratsch station on the Bernina Railway lies in the valley in front of the glacier. At its maximum in 1857, the ice came to within about 100 metres of this spot.
57163.m: From Morteratsch station you can walk to the glacier.

57164.q: What do the signs along the glacier trail to the Morteratsch Glacier show?
a: How far the ice reached in which year
The height of the surrounding peaks
The names of the mountain guides
The animals in the National Park
57164.e: Along the trail there are signs with years at the former positions of the glacier tongue. So while walking you can see how far the glacier has shrunk back.
57164.m: On the Morteratsch glacier trail you walk through the years of retreat.

57165.q: By roughly how much did the Morteratsch Glacier get shorter from 1878 to 2015?
57165.e: From the start of measurements in 1878 to 2015, the tongue retreated by about 2649 metres. That is about 17 metres per year on average.
57165.m: The Morteratsch Glacier has lost several kilometres since 1878.

57166.q: Why is the Morteratsch Glacier getting shorter year after year?
a: Because of global warming, more ice melts.
Because it is sliding into a lake.
Because farmers dig the ice away.
57166.e: Because of global warming, more ice melts in summer than is added as snow in winter. That is why the glacier tongue is shrinking back.
57166.m: Glaciers are melting because of global warming.

57167.q: Roughly how long was the Morteratsch Glacier in 2015?
57167.e: In 2015 the glacier was still about 6 kilometres long. Since measurements began, it has got shorter year after year.
57167.m: Today the Morteratsch Glacier is only about six kilometres long.

57168.q: What do you call the rubble that a glacier carries and drops?
57168.e: A glacier picks up rock and drops it as moraine. Moraines are a mixture of large boulders, gravel, sand and fine clay.

57169.q: What is the ridge of rubble in front of the glacier tongue that marks the glacier’s furthest advance called?
57169.e: The terminal moraine forms where the glacier tongue stayed in place the longest. It shows how far the glacier once reached.
57169.m: The terminal moraine shows the outermost edge of a glacier.

57170.q: What is the moraine called that forms along the edges of a glacier?
57170.e: At the edge, rubble falls from the valley sides onto the ice and is pushed along. This forms long ridges along the glacier.
57170.m: Lateral moraines run along the edges of the glacier.

57171.q: What do you call the rubble that lies under a glacier and is ground up by the ice?
57171.e: Under the glacier, rock is ground up and spread out in a layer. This ground moraine is often very clayey and does not let water through.
57171.m: The ground moraine lies under the glacier.

57172.q: Which long-shaped hills did ice-age ice form, for example in the Zurich Oberland?
57172.e: Drumlins are long hills of moraine material that were shaped under the ice. Their long axis shows the direction the glacier flowed.
57172.m: Drumlins show how the ice once flowed.

57173.q: Why does a terminal moraine often dam a lake after the glacier has melted?
a: It is the remains of a volcano
57173.e: The terminal moraine forms a ridge across the valley. Meltwater and river water can collect behind it to form a lake.
57173.m: Many lakes are dammed by terminal moraines.

57174.q: On which ice-age moraine ridge does part of Zurich’s old town stand?
57174.e: The Lindenhof is part of the terminal moraine from the Zurich stage of the Linth Glacier. Together with other deposits, this moraine dams Lake Zurich.
57174.m: The Lindenhof in Zurich is a moraine hill.

57175.q: How can you tell that a large boulder on the Central Plateau is an erratic boulder?
a: Its rock does not otherwise occur in the area
It is always round like a ball
It always lies in a river
57175.e: A granite boulder on the Central Plateau, for example, comes from the Alps. Only a glacier could have brought it there.
57175.m: An erratic boulder does not match the rock of its surroundings.

57176.q: Why is an erratic boulder in Geneva harbour important for the whole of Switzerland?
a: All heights in Switzerland are measured from it
It marks the centre of Switzerland
It is the oldest boundary stone
It shows the highest water level
57176.e: On the erratic boulder Pierre du Niton there is a reference point for height. The heights of all places and mountains in Switzerland were worked out from it.
57176.m: All Swiss height measurements refer to an erratic boulder in Geneva.

57177.q: Why are many erratic boulders protected today?
a: They are important evidence of the ice age
57177.e: Erratic boulders show how far the glaciers reached during the ice age. Because many were broken up in the past, the remaining ones are protected today.
57177.m: Erratic boulders are protected evidence of the ice age.

57178.q: When did huge glaciers bring the erratic boulders to the Central Plateau?
57178.e: In the ice age, the Alpine glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. When they melted, the boulders they had carried were left behind.
57178.m: Erratic boulders were carried by glaciers during the ice age.

57179.q: Why were many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau destroyed in the past?
a: They were used as building stone
They were thought to be poisonous
57179.e: Erratic boulders were a handy raw material for walls, steps and fountains. That is why many were broken up before they were protected.
57179.m: Many erratic boulders used to end up as building material.

57180.q: Which rock, not otherwise found there, are many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau made of?
57180.e: Granite comes from the Alps. If a granite boulder lies on the Central Plateau, a glacier brought it there. Nagelfluh and sandstone occur naturally on the Central Plateau too.
57180.m: Many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau are made of Alpine granite.

57181.q: What covered large parts of the Swiss Central Plateau during the last ice age?
57181.e: In the last ice age, huge glaciers flowed out of the Alps onto the Central Plateau. They shaped valleys, hills and lake basins.
57181.m: In the ice age, glacier ice lay on the Central Plateau.

57182.q: About how many years ago were the glaciers of the last ice age at their largest?
57182.e: The maximum of the last glaciation was about 24,000 years ago. At that time, ice covered large parts of the Central Plateau.
57182.m: About 24,000 years ago the Central Plateau was under ice.

57183.q: How did many large lakes on the Swiss Central Plateau, such as Lake Zurich, form?
57183.e: The ice-age glaciers deepened valleys and created basins. After the ice melted, they filled with water, often also dammed by moraines.
57183.m: The large lakes of the Central Plateau are a gift of the ice age.

57184.q: Which glacier of the last ice age reached from Valais as far as the Solothurn area?
57184.e: The ice-age Rhône Glacier flowed over the Lake Geneva area onto the Central Plateau. It reached as far as the area of Solothurn and Wangen an der Aare.
57184.m: In the ice age, the Rhône Glacier covered the western Central Plateau.

57185.q: About how many years ago did the last ice age end?
57185.e: When the last cold period ended, about 11,700 years ago, the Holocene began. We are still living in this warm period today.
57185.m: We have been living in a warm period for about 11,700 years.

57186.q: What is the cool period between about 1300 and 1850, when the glaciers grew again, called?
57186.e: In the Little Ice Age, summers were cooler and the Alpine glaciers advanced several times. Many villages in the Alps were threatened by growing glaciers at that time.
57186.m: The Little Ice Age made the glaciers grow until 1850.

a: A rock surface polished smooth by ice
A crack in the glacier ice
57187.e: Stones on the underside of the glacier grind the rock smooth and leave scratches. The scratches show the direction the ice flowed.
57187.m: Glacier polish is rock polished by the ice.

57188.q: Which wind usually brings rain from the Atlantic to the north side of the Alps?
57188.e: Switzerland lies in the westerly wind zone. West winds bring moist air from the Atlantic and so often bring rain to the north side of the Alps.
57188.m: The west wind often brings rain to northern Switzerland.

57189.q: Which region of Switzerland has the mildest climate and the most palm trees in gardens?
57189.e: Ticino lies on the south side of the Alps and is protected from cold north winds. The mild winters allow palms, camellias and fig trees.
57189.m: The climate on the south side of the Alps is especially mild.

57190.q: What is the warm, dry downslope wind called that occurs on the north side of the Alps when the wind is from the south?
57190.e: With a south föhn, the air drops its rain on the south side of the Alps. On the north side it sinks, warms up and becomes dry and warm.
57190.m: The föhn is a warm downslope wind from the Alps.

57191.q: What is the weather usually like on the south side of the Alps during a south föhn?
a: It is icy cold and dry
